INUKTITUT TRANSLATION
ᑲᒪᔨ, ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᔪᓂ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᑲᒪᔨᐅᓗᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓂᒃ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓂᒃ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᕙᒡᓗᓂ ᐊᑭᓕᒃᓴᕆᔭᐅᔪᓂ ᐊᑭᓕᐅᑎᓂ/ᐊᑭᓕᖅᑕᐅᔭᕆᐊᓕᖕᓂ ᑎᑎᕋᖃᑦᑕᕐᓗᓂ, ᓂᐅᕕᕐᕕᒋᔭᖏᓐᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᖅᑕᐅᔪᓂ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᖅᑐᓂᒃ. ᐅᓇ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒃᓴᖅ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᕐᒥᔪᖅ ᑲᑎᕐᓱᐃᕙᓪᓕᐊᓂᕐᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᖃᑦᑕᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖅᑖᕆᕙᓪᓕᐊᔭᖏᓐᓂᒃ ᓄᓇᑦᓯᐊᕐᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᑦᑎᔪᓄᑦ, ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖅᑖᖅᑎᑦᑎᕙᖕᓂᕐᒥ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᒃᓴᓂ ᐊᖏᕈᑎᒋᔭᐅᓯᒪᔪᓂᒃ. ᑲᒪᔨ ᒪᑯᓂᖓ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᓂᐅᔪᓂ ᒪᓕᒃᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᖃᑦᑕᑦᑎᐊᖅᑐᖅ ᐊᑐᖁᔭᐅᔪᓂ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᓗᓂ ᓈᒻᒪᓈᕐᓯᒪᓗᑎᒃ ᐅᕘᓇ ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᔾᔪᓯᖏᓐᓂ, ᐃᓚᖃᕐᓗᓂ CAAPS, ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᔾᔪᓯᕐᒥᓐ, ᐊᑭᓕᖅᑕᐅᔭᕆᐊᓕᖕᓂ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᑕᐅᕙᒃᑐᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᓕᕆᕝᕕᐅᑉ ᐊᑭᓕᐅᑎᓄᑦ ᑎᑎᖃᖁᑎᖏᓐᓂᒃ.

ᑲᒪᔨ, ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᔪᓂ ᒪᓕᒃᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᒃᐸᖅᑐᖅ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᓄᑦ ᒪᓕᒐᕆᔭᐅᔪᓂ, ᐱᖁᔭᕆᔭᐅᔪᓂᒃ, ᐊᑐᐊᒐᕐᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᓕᕆᔾᔪᓯᕐᓂ, ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᖅᖢᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓂ ᑎᑎᕋᕐᕕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᖃᑦᑕᕐᑐᖅ ᓇᓕᒨᒌᒃᑲᓗᐊᕐᒪᖔᑕ ᐊᑐᖅᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓂ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑕᖅᑭᑕᒫᓐ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᓗ ᐊᓂᒍᕌᖓᑦ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᑐᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᔪᑦ ᓇᓕᒧᒌᒃᑲᓗᐊᕐᒪᖔᑕ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑕᐅᕙᒃᖢᑎᒃ. ᐅᓇ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᒃᓴᖅ ᐊᑭᓕᐅᑎᐅᖃᑦᑕᕐᓂᐊᖅᑐᓂ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᔪᓐᓇᕐᓗᓂ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑭᐅᔨᐅᓗᓂ ᐊᑐᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᔪᓂ ᑎᑎᕋᐅᓯᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᖃᑦᑕᖅᑐᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᕝᕕᐅᑉ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖏᓐᓂ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᒧᑦ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑕᐅᖃᑦᑕᕐᓂᖓ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᒻᒪᕆᐅᑉ ᑎᑎᕋᕐᕕᖓᓂᙶᖅᑐᒥ.

ᐅᓇ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᒃᓴᖅ ᐃᑲᔪᕐᓇᖅᑐᖅ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᐊᕆᔭᐅᔪᒃᓴᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᔨᒻᒪᕆᖕᒥᓐ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐊᔪᕈᓐᓃᕐᓴᖅᓯᒪᔭᕆᐊᖃᖅᖢᓂ ᐊᑭᓕᖅᑕᐅᔾᔪᑎᓕᕆᓂᕐᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᒃᓴᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᕐᒥᒃ ᑲᔪᓯᑏᓐᓇᕋᓱᒡᓗᒍ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᐅᑎᓕᕆᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᔭᕆᐊᖃᕌᖓᑦ.

ᐅᑯᐊ ᑕᒡᕙ ᐊᑐᕈᖕᓇᖅᑐᑦ ᐃᑲᔪᐃᓂᖃᕈᖕᓇᕐᓂᐊᕐᓗᑎᑦ:
  • ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᖃᑦᑕᖅᑐᖅ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓂᒃ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᕙᒃᑐᓂ ᐊᑭᓕᐅᑎᒃᓴᓄᑦ, ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖅᑖᕈᑎᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓄᑦ, ᐃᑲᔫᑎᓂ ᐊᖏᕈᑎᓂᒃ, ᓂᐅᕕᕆᐊᓕᖕᓄᑦ ᓱᕋᒃᓯᒪᔪᓕᕆᓂᕐᒥ, ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒧᑦ ᐊᐅᓪᓚᕆᐊᓕᖕᓄᑦ, ᐱᓕᕆᕝᕕᖕᒥᑦ ᑎᑎᖃᖁᑎᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᔾᔪᑎᓂ ᑎᑎᕋᐅᓯᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓂᒃ ᑕᒪᐃᓐᓄ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᖅᑕᐅᔪᓄᑦ.
  • ᑲᒪᔭᖃᐃᓐᓇᕐᓗᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᐃᑦ ᐃᓯᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᔪᓄᑦ ᑎᑎᕋᕐᕕᐅᕙᒃᑐᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᕐᓗᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᐃᑦ ᐃᓯᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᔪᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᔭᐅᔾᔪᓯᖏᓐᓂᒃ, ᐋᖅᑭᒋᐊᕈᑎᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑕᖅᑭᕐᒧᑦ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᔾᔪᑎᖏᓐᓂᒃ ᐅᑯᓄᖓ 4,000-ᖏᓐᓃᑦᑐᓂᒃ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᑦᑎᔪᓂᒃ.
  • ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᖅᐸᒡᓗᓂ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᓯᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᐊᑭᓕᐅᑎᐅᔭᕆᐊᓕᖕᓂ, ᐃᓚᖃᕐᓗᓂ CAAPS, ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖅᑖᕋᓱᒃᑐᓄᑦ, ᐋᓐᓂᐊᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐱᖁᑎᖃᕐᕕᒃᒧᑦ, ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥᒃ, ᓇᓗᓇᐃᒃᑯᑎᓂ, ᑮᓇᐅᔭᐃᑦ ᐱᑐᐃᓐᓇᕆᐊᓖᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎ ᐊᐅᓪᓚᕆᐊᖃᕐᐸᑦ ᐊᑭᓕᖅᑕᐅᔾᔪᑎᖏᓐᓂ ᐱᔪᒪᓂᖓᓂ ᑐᓂᔭᐅᓂᖓᓄᑦ.
  • ᑎᑎᕋᐅᓯᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓂᒃ ᖃᐅᔨᒋᐊᖅᐸᒡᓗᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᓐᓇᐅᓕᔭᖄᖓᑦ ᐊᔾᔨᒌᙱᑦᑐᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᕝᕕᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᐅᕙᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᔾᔪᓯᕆᔭᐅᔪᒧᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖅᑖᕋᓱᒍᑎᓄ ᐊᒃᑐᐊᔪᓂ ᓈᓕᒨᒌᓈᕐᓯᒪᒐᓗᐊᕐᒪᖔᑕ.
  • ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᕙᒡᓗᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᑐᓂᐅᖃᐅᑎᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᑦ ᐅᕘᓇ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᓄᑦ ᐊᖏᕈᑎᑎᒍᑦ, ᐊᑭᓕᐅᑎᐅᔪᓪᓗ ᒪᓕᒃᑲᓗᐊᕐᒪᖔᑕ ᐊᖏᕈᑎᒋᔭᐅᓯᒪᔪᓂᒃ, ᐊᖏᕐᑕᐅᓯᒪᔪᓂ ᐊᑭᓕᐅᑎᓄᑦ ᐸᕐᓇᐅᑎᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᓄᑦ ᐊᑦᑕᓇᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓇᓪᓕᐅᒃᑯᒫᓂᒃ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑏᑦ (WSCC) ᐊᑐᐊᒐᖏᑦ.
  • ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑐᐃᕙᒃᑐᖅ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᔨᓂᒃ ᐱᓇᓱᐊᖅᑕᖓᓂ ᐊᑐᓕᕋᓱᒃᖢᑎᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑐᕌᒐᕆᔭᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᐱᓕᕆᕝᕕᒃᒧᑦ.
ᓇᒃᓴᕐᓂᐊᖅᑕᑎᑦ ᐃᖅᖃᓇᐃᔮᕆᔭᖕᓄᑦ:
  • ᐊᓂᒍᐃᓯᒪᑦᑎᐊᕐᓗᓂ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᒃᑲᓐᓂᕈᑎᓂᒃ, ᐊᕐᕌᒍ ᐊᑕᐅᓯᕐᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᓕᒪᓗᓂ ᑲᒪᔨᐅᓂᕐᒥ, ᐊᒻᒪ ᐅᑯᓇᓂ ᓇᓕᐊᓐᓂᑐᐃᓐᓇᖅ:
    • ᐱᐊᓂᒃᓯᓯᒪᓗᓂ ᑎᓴᒪᓂᒃ (4) ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᐊᔪᕈᓐᓃᕐᓯᒪᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᒐᒃᓴᓂᒃ (PEP) ᐃᓚᖃᕐᓗᓂ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᓂ ᐱᐊᓱᓂᒃ (3) ᐱᓕᕆᓕᒪᓂᕐᒥᒃ.
    • ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ ᐊᔾᔨᖏᓐᓂᒃ; ᑲᑐᔾᔨᖃᑎᒌᓂ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᕆᔨᒻᒪᕆᐅᓯᒪᔪᓄᑦ (ACCA) ᐊᑐᖁᔭᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᖓᓱᓂ (3) ᐊᕐᕌᒍᓂ ᑕᒪᑐᒧᖓ ᐱᓕᕆᓕᒪᓗᓂ.
ᐃᒪᐃᑦᑐᓂ ᑐᓂᓯᓯᒪᕗᒍᑦ:
  • ᐱᕕᒃᓴᐅᔪᖅ ᐱᐅᔪᒥᑦ ᐊᒃᑐᐃᓂᖃᖅᑐᒥ ᓴᓇᔩᑦ ᐃᓅᓯᖏᑕ ᐱᐅᓂᖓᓂ ᓄᓇᑦᓯᐊᖅ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᓄᓇᕗᑦ ᐃᓗᓕᓕᒫᖓᓂ.
  • ᐅᑭᐅᕐᑕᖅᑐᕐᒦᔾᔪᑎᓕ $3,700 ᔭᓗᓇᐃᒥ ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ
  • ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᕐᓂᐊᖅᑐᓄᑦ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂ – ᐃᒡᓗᒧᑦ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᓂ ᐱᑕᖃᑐᐃᓐᓇᕆᐊᓕᒃ.
  • ᐱᐅᓪᓚᕆᒃᑐᑦ ᐃᑲᔫᓯᐊᒃᓴᑦ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᓱᖅᓯᒪᒧᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐊᑎᓕᐅᖅᑕᐅᖃᑕᐅᓗᓂ ᑭᒃᑯᓕᒫᓂᒃ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐃᓄᑐᖃᐅᔾᔪᓯᐊᒃᓴᓄᑦ.
  • ᐃᓕᑉᐸᓪᓕᐋᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐱᕙᓪᓕᐋᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᕈᑎᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑮᓇᐅᔭᖃᒃᑎᑦᑎᔪᑎᓂᒃ ᑐᕌᖓᑎᑕᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᐃᕝᕕᑦ ᐃᖃᓇᐃᔮᕆᔭᕐᓂ ᐱᕈᒃᐸᓪᓕᐊᓂᕐᓄᑦ.
  • ᐊᒥᓱᓂᒃ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᙱᑦᑐᓐᓇᐅᑎᖃᕐᓗᓂ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᕐᕕᖕᒥ ᐃᓕᖅᑯᓯᕐᒦᓪᓗᓂ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑐᐃᔪᒥ ᖃᓄᐃᙱᑦᑎᐊᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᕐᕕᖕᒥ-ᐃᓅᓯᕐᒥ ᓇᓕᒧᒌᒃᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥᒃ.
  • ᐊᔾᔨᒌᙱᑦᑑᑎᓂ ᐃᓕᖅᑯᓯᖃᐅᖅᖢᑎ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐊᓯᙳᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᔪᓂ ᒪᓕᒍᓐᓇᖅᖢᑎ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑐᙵᓱᒃᑎᑦᑎᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᐊᑐᕐᓯᒪᓯᒪᔭᕐᓄᑦ.
  • ᒐᕙᒪᑐᖃᒃᑯ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᑖᒃᓰᔭᐃᓂᕐᒧ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᓕᒃ ᒪᑯᑎᑐᓇᖅ ᓄᓇᑦᓯᐊᕐᒥ ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᓇᖕᒥᓂᖅ ᑖᒃᓰᔭᕈᑎᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐅᑭᐅᕐᑕᖅᑐᕐᒦᓐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᑖᒃᓯᓄᑦ ᐲᔭᖅᑕᐅᔭᕆᐊᓕᖕᓂᒃ.
ᐱᕋᔭᒃᓯᒪᙱᒃᑲᓗᐊᕐᒪᖔᑦ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑕᐅᓂᖅ: ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᖅᑖᕋᓱᒃᑐᖅ ᑐᓂᓯᔪᓐᓇᕐᓗᓂ ᓈᒻᒪᒃᑐᒥᒃ ᐱᕋᔭᒃᓯᒪᖕᒪᖔᑦ ᖃᐅᔨᒋᐊᖅᑕᐅᔾᔪᑎᒥᒃ. ᑐᓂᓯᙱᓐᓂᖅ ᓈᒻᒪᒃᑐᒥᒃ ᖃᐅᔨᒋᐊᖅᑕᐅᔾᔪᑎᒥᒃ ᑐᑭᑖᖅᑎᑕᐅᓯᒪᓂᐊᖅᑐᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᖅᑖᕈᓐᓇᙱᓐᓂᖓᓂᒃ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᒃᓴᒥᒃ.

ᓄᓇᖃᖅᑳᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᑐᐊᒐᖅ: ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᖅᑖᕋᓱᒃᑐᑦ ᐅᖃᑦᑎᐊᕆᐊᓖᑦ ᐊᔪᙱᔾᔪᑎᒋᔭᖏᓐᓂᒃ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔭᐅᖃᓯᐅᑎᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐅᕘᓇ ᓄᓇᖃᖅᑳᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᑐᐊᒐᖅᑎᒍᑦ.

ᐊᔾᔨᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᖅᓯᒪᓂᖅ: ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔭᐅᑐᐃᓐᓇᕆᐊᓕᒃ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᒥ ᑕᒪᐅᖔᖅᑐᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᑯᑦ ᓲᕐᓗ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᒥᑦ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᖅᓯᒪᓂᖅᑐᑦ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔭᐅᓐᓇᖅᑐᖅ ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ ᐊᑕᐅᓯᕐᒥ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᒥ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᖅᓯᒪᓗᓂ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᒥ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᕈᓐᓇᕐᓗᓂ. ᑭᓯᐊᓂ, ᐊᑕᐅᑦᑎᒃᑰᖓᓗᑎᒃ ᑕᒪᐃᓐᓂᒃ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔭᐅᔭᕆᐊᓖᑦ ᓴᖅᑭᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓂᑦ. ᓈᒪᔪᒧᑦ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᓯᒪᔪᓂᑦ ᓇᓕᒧᒃᑐᓄᑦ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔭᐅᒐᔭᖅᑐᓂᑦ ᑖᔅᓱᒥᖓ ᐃᓂᐅᔪᒧᑦ, ᖃᐅᔨᒋᐊᕐᕕᐅᔪᓐᓇᖅᑐᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑐᓕᕆᔨᒃᑯᑦ.

ᐊᔾᔨᖃᙱᓐᓂᖅ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓚᐅᑎᑦᑎᓂᖅ: ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᓄᑦ ᐊᑦᑕᓇᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓇᓪᓕᐅᒃᑯᒫᓂᒃ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑏᑦ ᐃᓚᓕᐅᔾᔨᓯᒪᔫᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᕐᕕᐅᔪᖅ. ᑎᒥᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᔪᕈᑎᖃᕈᑯᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑐᖅᑕᐅᔭᕆᐊᖃᕐᓗᑎᒃ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᓕᖅᑎᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᓇᓱᖕᓂᕐᓂ, ᐊᔭᐅᖅᑐᖅᑕᐅᐅᔪᑎᑦ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᔭᐃᓗᑎᒃ ᐱᔭᕆᐊᖃᑕᕐᓂᒃ ᐅᖃᖃᑎᒋᔭᐅᒍᕕᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒃᓴᓄᑦ ᐊᐱᖅᓱᕐᓂᕐᒧᓪᓘᓐᓃᑦ ᐊᑲᐅᓈᖁᔭᐅᓪᓗᑎᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᕙᓪᓕᐊᓂᕐᒥ.
ᐱᔪᓐᓇᕋᔭᕐᓂᖓᓂ: ᐊᔪᙱᑎᑕᐅᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᑎᑎᕋᖅᓯᒪᔪᑦ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᓱᖅᑕᐅᑐᐃᓐᓇᕆᐊᓖᑦ ᐱᓇᔪᒃᑐᓂ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᑦ ᐃᓐᓄᖁᔭᐅᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᓯᕗᓂᒃᓴᒥ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᓚᐅᑲᒐᔭᖅᑐᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᖑᐃᓐᓇᕐᓂᐊᖅᑐᓄᑦ ᐃᓂᓄᑦ.

ᐅᑯᐊ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᓄᑦ ᐊᑦᑕᓇᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓇᓪᓕᐅᒃᑯᒫᓂᒃ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑏᑦ (WSCC) ᐱᓇᓱᐊᒐᖃᕐᑐᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᕐᕕᒃᒥᓐ ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖅᑖᕆᔭᐅᔭᑦᑐᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐋᓐᓂᕈᑎᐅᔭᑦᑐᓂᒃ. ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒃᓴᕆᔭᕗᑦ ᐃᒪᐃᑦᑑᕗᑦ ᓴᖅᑭᔮᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᕐᕕᖕᒥ ᖃᓄᐃᙱᑦᑎᐊᕈᑎᓂᒃ ᐊᑦᑕᕐᓇᖅᑕᐃᓕᒪᓂᕐᒧᓪᓗ ᐱᑎᑦᑎᓯᒻᒫᑦ ᐱᔾᔪᑎᖃᙱᑦᑐᒥ ᓇᓪᓕᐅᒃᑯᒫᓂᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᑦᑎᔨᓄᑦ ᑲᒪᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐸᖅᑭᓂᐅᔪᒥ ᐋᓐᓂᖅᓯᒪᔪᓄᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᑎᓄᑦ. ᐊᑐᐊᒐᕆᔭᕗᑦ ᐃᑉᐱᒍᓱᑦᑎᐊᕐᓂᖅ, ᐱᖃᑕᐅᑎᑦᑎᓂᖅ, ᓱᓕᑦᑎᐊᕐᓂᖅ, ᒪᑐᐃᖓᑦᑎᐊᕐᓂᖅ, ᐱᖅᑯᓯᓄᑦ ᐊᑦᑕᓇᖏᑦᑐᒥ, ᐱᐅᔪᒻᒪᕆᒻᒥᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᕐᕕᐅᔪᒥᑦ.

title: Vice President, Customer Experience
description:
At MOO, we believe Customer Experience can be a genuine point of difference - and an important driver of how we grow.

We’re looking for a VP, Customer Experience to lead the next evolution of our customer and commercial strategy. This role will own the growth of our Managed Services business, lead our Customer Service and Revenue Operations organisations, and set the strategy for how we create a differentiated MOO experience across the end-to-end customer journey.

Reporting to our Chief Commercial Officer, you’ll lead an organisation of approximately 120 people across the US, UK and South Africa, with senior leaders across Sales, Customer Service and Revenue Operations.

What You’ll Do

Grow Managed Services

You’ll own the strategy and performance of MOO’s Managed Services business.
  • Deliver Managed Services revenue growth through customer acquisition, retention and expansion.
  • Define the target customers, industries and segments where MOO should focus.
  • Develop the proposition, strategy and capabilities required to win and grow high-value customers.
  • Determine where human interaction creates value and where AI, automation and self-service should play a greater role.
  • Ensure Demand Generation, Sales Enablement and lead generation support the growth strategy.

Make Customer Experience a MOO Point of Difference

You’ll own and lead MOO’s end-to-end Customer Experience strategy and capability.
  • Define what a differentiated MOO experience should be and the principles that underpin it.
  • Identify the biggest gaps and opportunities across the end-to-end customer journey.
  • Own the cross-functional CX roadmap and drive action across the business
  • Build customer insight and measurement into how MOO prioritises and makes decisions.

Lead and Evolve Customer Service

You’ll own the performance and future direction of Customer Service.
  • Ensure Customer Service delivers strong customer, operational and cost outcomes.
  • Own the strategy for the Service organisation, including how Service contributes to MOO’s premium experience and customer loyalty.
  • Determine where human interaction creates value and where AI, automation and self-service should play a greater role.
  • Ensure Service insight drives improvements beyond the Service team.

Build the Commercial Capabilities to Deliver the Strategy

You’ll own Revenue Operations, including customer systems, Managed Services Demand Generation and Sales Enablement.
  • Ensure our systems, partners,, data and processes enable effective customer management and growth.
  • Build the Demand Generation capability required to create the right Managed Services pipeline.
  • Ensure Sales teams have the tools, insight, processes and enablement required to perform.
  • Use data, technology and AI to improve Sales and Service effectiveness.

About You

  • You’re an exceptional strategic thinker. You can take a complex, ambiguous problem, work out what really matters and turn it into a clear strategy and set of choices. You’re highly numerate and use data and customer insight to get to the answer.
  • You are genuinely customer obsessed. You instinctively look at the business through the customer's eyes and have experience turning customer insight into changes in strategy, proposition, product, experience or operations.
  • You know how to find and shape opportunities for growth. You can think strategically about where to play and how to win, using customer needs, segmentation, economics and market opportunity to develop a compelling growth strategy.
  • You can lead strong, experienced functional leaders. You know when to challenge, when to coach and when to get out of the way, and can add strategic value without needing to be the deepest expert in Sales, Service or RevOps yourself.
  • You are exceptional at leading across organisational boundaries. You can create alignment, influence senior peers and drive meaningful change across teams you don't directly control, while bringing people with you.
  • You are excited by how technology and AI can reshape the customer experience. You can think strategically about where human interaction creates real value and where technology, automation and AI can make the experience better, simpler and more scalable.

title: Resident Care Assistants/ Med Techs (All Shifts)
description:
Resident Caregiver / Med Tech at Grand Villa of Ocala - Hiring All Shifts


Grand Villa of Ocala is dedicated to providing compassionate and high-quality care to our residents. We are currently seeking dedicated Resident Caregivers with a preference for Med Tech certification to join our team for the evening shift. If you are passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of seniors and thrive in a supportive, team-oriented environment, we encourage you to apply.


Key Responsibilities:

- Assist residents with daily activities such as bathing, dressing, grooming, and mobility

- Provide companionship and emotional support to residents

- Administer medications and treatments as directed, following all safety and compliance protocols (Med Tech certification preferred)

- Monitor residents’ health status and report any changes to nursing staff

- Maintain accurate and detailed documentation of care provided

- Ensure a clean, safe, and comfortable environment for residents

- Collaborate with team members to deliver personalized care plans


Skills and Qualifications:

- Prior experience in senior care or healthcare preferred

- Med Tech certification highly preferred; willingness to obtain certification is a plus

- Compassionate, patient, and respectful demeanor

- Strong communication and interpersonal skills

- Ability to work independently and as part of a team

- Flexibility to work the evening shift (7 - 3 Shift)

- Ability to follow detailed instructions and adhere to safety protocols


At Grand Villa of Ocala, we foster a warm, welcoming culture that values growth, teamwork, and excellence in care. We offer competitive pay, opportunities for professional development, and a supportive environment where your contributions truly make a difference. Join us in providing exceptional care and enriching the lives of our residents.

This position requires a background screening as mandated by Florida law. For more information on background screening requirements, please visit https://info.flclearinghouse.com.

title: SUPERINTENDENT OF PARK OPERATIONS
description:
JOB OPENING

CITY OF FARMINGTON

JOB POSITION #167: SUPERINTENDENT OF PARK OPERATIONS

NUMBER OF VACANCIES: 1

DEPARTMENT: PARKS & RECREATION/Parks Operations

WORK LOCATION: 901 Fairgrounds Road

HIRING RANGE: $69,572 - $95,000 salary

PAY GRADE: O

DAYS WORKED: Varied

HOURS WORKED: Varied

TYPE OF POSITION: Regular, Full-Time

APPLICATIONS WILL BE RECEIVED UNTIL: Until Filled

JOB DUTIES:

OVERVIEW:

This is a senior management position working with the Parks and Recreation Department, which is committed to growing a happy, healthy community through exceptional parks, programs, experiences, and customer focus. The Superintendent of Park Operations is responsible for the day-to-day management and operational leadership of the Park Operations Division. Under the direction of the Deputy Director of Parks and Recreation, the Superintendent oversees park maintenance, grounds maintenance, athletic fields, trails, medians, park facilities, equipment, special-event support, staffing, and resources. The position establishes and implements maintenance standards and manages the division's budget, personnel, facilities, and planning to ensure the City's park system is maintained safely, efficiently, and consistently.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES:

Works under the leadership, administrative guidance, and direction of the Deputy Director of Parks and Recreation.

Performs administrative and supervisory work necessary to coordinate and supervise the day-to-day operations of the Park Operations Division, including park maintenance, grounds maintenance, athletic fields, trails, medians, park facilities, equipment, special-event support, and related operations.

Exercises supervision over seasonal, temporary, and regular personnel; assigns, trains, and evaluates work; oversees in-service training; completes performance evaluations; and, in conjunction with the Deputy Director, makes recommendations regarding hiring, disciplining, and terminating seasonal, temporary, and regular employees. Assists with resolution of employee concerns and grievances.

Assists with developing Park Operations' conceptual and long-range plans and annual operating budget; develops and makes recommendations, monitors budgetary expenditures, and tracks the status of external vendor contracts.

Implements department policies, procedures, priorities, and operational standards within Park Operations.

Assists with evaluation of Park Operations' effectiveness; prepares and tracks budgets; and prepares division and department reports as requested.

Assists with preparation and administration of grant applications, implements grant requirements as assigned, and prepares related grant reports.

Responds to citizen complaints and requests for information related to Park Operations and ensures appropriate follow-up action is taken.

Actively participates in community organizations to foster a positive City image.

Prepares routine and special reports and presentations regarding Park Operations and development of plans as requested by the department, City Council, or other boards, commissions, or citizen groups.

Assists with capital improvement projects related to Park Operations, including design, budget development, contract preparation, and bidding procedures.

Coordinates Park Operations support for annual City and department special and seasonal events.

Establishes maintenance standards, manages staffing and resources, and ensures park facilities and grounds are maintained safely, efficiently, and consistently.

Works independently and exercises considerable judgment while leading and directing the management and operations of the Park Operations Division.

NON-ESSENTIAL DUTIES:

Assists with the planning and development of new parks, park facilities, buildings, and related infrastructure with knowledge of construction planning, design, and administration.

Other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:

This position is subject to the City of Farmington's Drug and Alcohol Testing Policy which includes: pre-employment testing, post-accident testing, reasonable suspicion testing, return to duty testing, and follow-up testing.

Working knowledge of current principles and practices used in the administration of park operations and services; applicable city, state, and federal regulations/guidelines pertaining to areas of responsibility; and overall city operations, including budgeting procedures.

Ability to effectively supervise and evaluate personnel and maintain effective professional relationships with the public, vendors, employees, management, City officials, and other government officials.

Excellent communication (verbal and written), organizational, and analytical skills.

Working knowledge of word processing and spreadsheet computer software; ability to operate computer and other standard office equipment.

Ability to prepare and maintain records and reports. Knowledge of budget preparation and office management.

Bachelor's degree in Parks Administration, Turfgrass Management, Horticulture, Landscape Architecture, or related field. Master's Degree preferred. Five (5) years supervisory experience.

Valid driver's license with acceptable driving record for the past three years is required.

Ability to work varied hours including evenings and weekends.

TOOLS AND EQUIPMENT USED:

Personal computer, including MS Word software; calculator; copy and fax machine; phone; mobile or portable radio; automobile.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to walk; use hands to handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls; and reach with hands and arms.

The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, and the ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Work is performed outside in all types of weather conditions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee frequently works near moving mechanical parts and in outside weather conditions. The employee is occasionally exposed to wet and/or humid conditions and lightning. The employee frequently works in high, precarious places and is frequently exposed to wet/dry and extreme hot and cold weather condition, fumes or airborne particles, toxic or caustic chemicals, and vibration. The employee is occasionally exposed to the risk of electrical shock.

The noise level in the work environment is usually loud.

WE ARE AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER, M/F/D/V

title: Property Tax Specialist
description:
This position is responsible for participating in assigned fiscal functions, including ensuring the integrity and accuracy of the accounting system; auditing, reconciling, and analyzing all accounting transactions; preparing spreadsheets and reports; and preparing journal entries.

MAJOR DUTIES



  1. Coordinate property tax sales.
  2. Prepare property tax notices -delinquent notices, etc.
  3. Prepare yearly property tax statements
  4. Prepare property tax refund checks, as needed.
  5. Assist with annual audit preparations.
  6. Perform all other duties as assigned.
  7. Audit payables, purchase orders, and invoices for accuracy and compliance with policies and procedures.
  8. Provide updated balances to various tax service companies, mortgage companies, and attorneys as requested.
  9. Responds to all correspondence relating to property taxes.
  10. Serves as a back-up to Accounts Payable.
  11. Performs all other duties as assigned.



KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED BY THE POSITION



  1. Knowledge of state and federal tax laws.
  2. Knowledge of Governmental Accounting Standards Board guidelines.
  3. Knowledge of Department of Labor and Department of Revenue guidelines.
  4. Knowledge of utility billing policies and procedures.
  5. Knowledge of delinquent property tax guidelines.
  6. Knowledge of computers and job-related software programs.
  7. Skill in the management of financial records.
  8. Skill in the preparation of financial reports.
  9. Skill in oral and written communication.



SUPERVISORY CONTROLS



The Finance Director assigns work with very general instructions. The supervisor spot-checks completed work for compliance with procedures and the nature and propriety of the results.

GUIDELINES



Guidelines include the municipal code, Governmental Accounting Standards Board guidelines, federal and state accounting guidelines, city financial policies, and city and department policies and procedures. These guidelines require judgment, selection, and interpretation in application.

COMPLEXITY/SCOPE OF WORK



  • The work consists of various accounting duties. Strict guidelines and the need for accuracy contribute to the complexity of the position.
  • The purpose of this position is to participate in assigned department accounting functions. Success in this position helps to ensure the city’s fiscal viability and contributes to the efficiency and effectiveness of city operations.

CONTACTS

  • Contacts are typically with co-workers, other city personnel, bank representatives, elected and appointed officials, representatives of county and state agencies, and members of the public.
  • Contacts are typically to provide services, give or exchange information, motivate persons, or resolve problems.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS/ WORK ENVIRONMENT



  • The work is typically performed while sitting at a desk or table or while intermittently sitting, standing, stooping, or walking. The employee occasionally lifts light objects.
  • The work is typically performed in an office.

SUPERVISORY AND MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITY



  • None

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS



  • Associates degree required; and
  • More than three years of related experience required; or
  • Any equivalent combination of education, experience, and training which provides the knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the work.

title: SPS Water Sampling Technician – Manchester, NH
description:
SPS Water Sampling Technician – Manchester, NH
Part-Time / On-Call

I-2-I Solutions is seeking a qualified Water Sampling Technician to support an ANSI/AAMI ST108 Sterile Processing Service (SPS) water-quality program at a federal healthcare facility in Manchester, New Hampshire.

The technician will be responsible for performing on-site water sample collection from Sterile Processing equipment and water systems. Routine sampling will occur approximately once per month, with additional quarterly testing and occasional re-sampling as required.

Responsibilities

  • Perform on-site water sampling in the Sterile Processing Service department in accordance with ANSI/AAMI ST108 procedures.
  • Collect samples from Critical Water, Utility Water, and Steam/condensate sampling points, including RO systems, sinks, washer/disinfectors, Medivators, ultrasonic equipment, and related SPS equipment.
  • Perform on-site pH measurements within 15 minutes of sample collection.
  • Follow aseptic sampling procedures and facility infection-control requirements.
  • Properly label, document, cool, package, and prepare samples for same-day overnight shipment to the laboratory.
  • Complete chain-of-custody and sampling documentation accurately.
  • Wear required PPE, including protective coveralls, shoe covers, gloves, hair covering, and other required infection-control equipment.
  • Coordinate sampling visits with I-2-I project staff and facility personnel.
  • Be available for occasional re-sampling requests, which may require collection within 48 hours of notification.

The Manchester requirement includes monthly Critical Water sampling and quarterly Utility Water and Steam testing, with a total of 12 routine site visits per year. The technician will perform field collection and pH testing; the remaining laboratory analysis is performed separately by the accredited laboratory.

Qualifications

  • Background in laboratory science, medical laboratory science, sterile processing, environmental health, water sampling, or a related field.
  • Knowledge of aseptic technique and proper sample collection procedures.
  • Comfortable working within a hospital Sterile Processing environment.
  • Strong attention to sample identification, documentation, and chain-of-custody requirements.
  • Ability to independently travel to the Manchester, NH facility for scheduled sampling.
  • Reliable transportation and ability to meet scheduled collection times.
  • Ability to complete I-2-I’s required ST108 sampler training and competency assessment before independent sampling.

Preferred Qualifications

  • CBSPD or other Sterile Processing Technician certification.
  • Medical Laboratory Scientist/Technician background.
  • Previous healthcare, environmental, or water-quality sampling experience.
  • Familiarity with ANSI/AAMI ST108.
  • Experience working in VA, military, or other federal healthcare facilities.

Normal sampling activities are performed during the facility’s coverage hours of 7:00 AM–4:30 PM, Monday through Friday, unless otherwise authorized. The work requires strict PPE, aseptic sampling, cold-chain handling, and same-day shipment procedures.

Location: Manchester, New Hampshire
Schedule: Approximately one scheduled visit per month, with quarterly expanded sampling and occasional on-call re-sampling

Work Location: In person

title: Sjuksköterska,  Medicinsk vårdenhet C
description:
Höglandssjukhuset

Välkommen till ett härligt team där vi tillsammans arbetar i specialiserad medicinsk och geriatrisk vård. Välkommen till medicin C!

Rollen som sjuksköterska
Som sjuksköterska hos oss ansvarar du för omvårdnad, medicinsk vård, läkemedel och den sociala planeringen kring patienten. I sjuksköterskans arbete ingår även att administrera läkemedel, handha medicinteknisk apparatur samt utföra delegerade medicinska arbetsuppgifter.

Hos oss kommer du att arbeta i ett team bestående av undersköterskor, sjuksköterskor och läkare i gott arbetsklimat.

Våra specialiteter är lungmedicin mag-tarm och allmän invärtes medicin. Spännande utvecklingsarbete sker kontinuerligt på mottagningen. 

Din blivande arbetsplats
Medicin- och geriatrikkliniken på Höglandssjukhuset i Eksjö är en utvecklande verksamhet där vi vårdar patienter som är i behov av specialiserad medicinsk och geriatrisk vård. Kliniken har en historia av innovativt, systematiskt och evidensbaserat kvalitetsarbete med stort patientfokus. Sedan 2014 är klinikens ledningssystem certifierat enligt ISO 9001:2014.

Att kliniken är ISO-certifierad är något som vi alla är mycket stolta över. Detta innebär kort och gott att vi har ordning och reda i vår verksamhet. Det skapar goda förutsättningar för oss som arbetar på kliniken att veta vad, när och hur. Det bidrar till att våra processer kvalitetssäkras så att patienterna ges god och säker vård.

Vi vet att steget från utbildning till verklighet kan kännas stort. Vi vill ge dig som nyutbildad sjuksköterska en bra start i arbetslivet där du får växa in i din nya yrkesroll. Därför erbjuder vi alla våra anställda sjuksköterskor som fått sin legitimation de senaste 12 månaderna att delta i ett av Sveriges bästa introduktions- och utvecklingsprogram för nyutbildade sjuksköterskor - RIU. Programmet omfattar 20 heldagar fördelade på åtta månader, och det startar varje år i februari och september. Här kan du läsa mer om RIU och följ oss gärna på Instagram @medicineksjo_c (https://www.instagram.com/medicineksjo_c/) och @regionjkpgriu (https://www.instagram.com/regionjkpgriu/).

Din profil
Vi söker dig som är legitimerad sjuksköterska med ett stort intresse för ditt yrke och ständig vill utvecklas!

Vi söker dig som är trygg i din roll som sjuksköterska. Du är initiativtagande, självgående och har lätt för att anpassa dig efter ändrade omständigheter. Du har en god förmåga att strukturera ditt arbete och är självständig, samtidigt som du samarbetar bra med andra människor. Vidare är du stabil och behåller lugnet i stressade situationer. Du har även en god förmåga att kommunicera med andra och sätta dig in i deras perspektiv.

Vårt erbjudande till dig
Hos oss får du arbeta på en avdelning där vi värnar om ett gott arbetsklimat. För oss är det en självklarhet att samarbeta och hjälpas åt, och dessutom tycker vi det är viktigt att ha roligt på jobbet! Vi erbjuder en arbetsplats där vi arbetar enligt modellen för personcentrerad och patientnära vård. Det är arbetssätt som sätter patientens berättelse, behov och delaktighet i centrum och ger bättre arbetsmiljö för personalen. Som medarbetare på medicin- och geriatrikkliniken erbjuds du stora möjligheter till kompetensutveckling och fördjupning. 

Vi tror på att god vård alltid sker i samverkan med såväl våra patienter och närstående som andra samarbetspartner inom specialistsjukvården, primärvården och kommunerna på Höglandet. Hög kvalitet på vården är något vi systematiskt arbetar för varje dag på alla nivåer i organisationen på mottagningarna, avdelningarna och på akutmottagningen. I detta arbete har patientsäkerhetsfrågorna en viktig roll.

Tjänsten avser heltid med tjänstgöring dag, kväll och helger. Tillträde sker enligt överenskommelse, men vi ser gärna att du kan börja så snart som möjligt.

Som medarbetare i Region Jönköpings län gör du skillnad för många – på riktigt. Oavsett yrke har vi alla samma uppdrag – att bidra till att göra livet bättre, roligare och friskare för länets alla invånare. I en stor organisation finns också stora möjligheter där vi samarbetar över gränserna och lär av varandra. Hos oss är kompetensutveckling inte bara utbildning, det är en del av det dagliga arbetet.

Som medarbetare hos oss inom Region Jönköpings län får du tillgång till våra anställningsförmåner. En del av dem ökar din grundtrygghet, andra sätter lite guldkant på vardagen. Läs mer om våra förmåner här: Förmåner (http://www.rjl.se/jobb-och-karriar/Jobba-hos-oss/Formaner/)

Har du frågor om tjänsten?
Har du frågor om tjänsten är du välkommen att kontakta vårdenhetschef Ann-Catrin Bringner, 010- 243 80 05.

Vår rekryteringsprocess
Sista ansökningsdagen är den 31 oktober 2026. Urval och intervjuer kan komma att ske löpande, så vi ber dig att skicka in din ansökan så snart som möjligt.

Läs mer om Region Jönköpings läns rekryteringsprocess på vår hemsida: Vår rekryteringsprocess, Region Jönköpings län (https://rjl.se/jobb-och-karriar/Lediga-jobb/Var-rekryteringsprocess/)

Välkommen med din ansökan!

Vi undanber oss all kontakt med annonsförsäljare och rekryteringsföretag.

title: Director, External Corporate Communications
description:
About Us:

Eupraxia is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing locally delivered, extended-release products that have the potential to address therapeutic areas with high unmet medical need. DiffuSphere™, a proprietary, polymer-based micro-sphere technology, is designed to facilitate targeted drug delivery of both existing and novel drugs. The technology is designed to support an extended duration of effect and delivery of drugs in a hyper-localized fashion, targeting only the tissues that physicians want to treat. We believe the potential for fewer adverse events may be achieved through the precision targeting and the stable and flat delivery of the active ingredient when using the DiffuSphere™ technology, versus the peaks and troughs seen with more traditional drug delivery methods. The precision of Eupraxia's DiffuSphere™ technology platform has the potential to augment and transform existing FDA-approved drugs to improve their safety, tolerability, efficacy and duration of effect. The potential uses in therapeutic areas may go beyond pain and inflammatory gastrointestinal disease, where Eupraxia currently is developing advanced treatments, also to be applicable in oncology, infectious disease and other critical disease areas.


Eupraxia's EP-104GI is currently running both a Phase 1b/2a and Phase 2b trial, the RESOLVE trials, for the treatment of EoE. EP-104GI is administered as an injection into the esophageal wall, providing local delivery of drug. This is a unique treatment approach for EoE. In addition, Eupraxia is developing a pipeline of later and earlier-stage long-acting formulations. Potential pipeline indications include candidates for GI diseases, inflammatory diseases and oncology, each designed to improve on the activity and tolerability of currently approved drugs. For further details about Eupraxia, please visit the Company's website at: .


Scope:

Corporate and Brand Messaging

Content Creation

  • Develop and draft external communications materials, including corporate website content, press releases, R&D Day and investor materials, working with the appropriate functional subject matter experts. Where materials contain scientific, clinical or medical content, work closely with the CMO and designated Clinical/Medical subject matter experts, who retain accountability for the scientific and medical content and interpretation.


Investor Relations and Public Relations

  • Contribute to the production of press releases, earnings releases, corporate updates, and clinical trial milestone announcements, in close coordination with the CFO, General Counsel, and CEO.
  • Prepare briefing materials for quarterly earnings calls, investor conference presentations, and the annual report / MD&A narrative, working with IR counsel and the executive team.

  • Coordinate with IR the external messaging calendar around clinical catalysts, ensuring alignment with continuous disclosure obligations and coordination with the company's disclosure committee.

Scientific and Medical Communications

  • Provide writing and communications support, as requested, for scientific and medical materials including congress materials, advisory board materials, KOL communications, publications and disease-state education. Scientific and medical strategy, content and interpretation remain the responsibility of the Clinical/Medical organization.
  • Ensure external communications containing scientific, clinical or medical information are appropriately reviewed and approved by the accountable Clinical/Medical and other relevant functional leaders before external use.
  • Maintain working fluency in the disease areas and competitive landscape, drawing on market research and competitive analysis of the competitive and scientific landscape to sharpen external messaging and anticipate questions from analysts and media.

Commercial

  • Supporting the commercial function in defining key messages and supporting proof points for each priority audience: gastroenterologists, allergists/immunologists, pediatric subspecialists, patients and caregivers, payers, investors, and internal stakeholders. Ensure messaging is consistent across all external-facing touchpoints and tailored to each audience’s clinical, economic, or experiential lens.



Requirements

  • Bachelors’ degree in Life Sciences or related field; additional communications and/or journalism qualifications are an asset.
  • 8–10+ years of progressively senior communications, investor relations, or public relations experience, with at least 5 years in biotech, pharma, or life sciences.
  • Understanding of the healthcare ecosystem, including clinical workflows, regulatory landscapes, reimbursement environments, and therapeutic areas (e.g., GI, Immunology and/or specialty therapeutics).
  • Excellent writing and editing skills, and the ability to translate clinical and scientific data into clear, accurate, non-promotional external messaging.
  • Experience with developing and executing communication strategies and tactics.
  • Demonstrated experience in public-company investor relations and financial communications, including press release drafting, disclosure coordination, and earnings-related materials.
  • Working knowledge of Canadian and/or U.S. securities disclosure requirements and familiarity working with a disclosure committee.
  • Strong relationship-management skills with analysts, and agency partners; sound judgment under time pressure and during high-stakes or sensitive situations.
  • Proven ability to work with and effectively influence leadership teams while operating in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial, decisive/deadline-oriented environment, heavily regulated industry; strong interpersonal skills and ability to work with others in a positive, collaborative manner.
  • Excellent planning and organizational skills, with a keen ability to multi-task.

title: Shop Technician
description:
At DPS in Salt Lake City, Utah, we don't just manufacture skis-we build the tools that fuel adventure. Every ski that leaves our facility represents precision, craftsmanship, innovation, and countless powder days waiting to happen.

We're looking for a Shop Technician who enjoys working with their hands, takes pride in quality craftsmanship, and wants to be part of a team obsessed with building extraordinary products and service.

If you can appreciate the difference between "good enough" and "perfect," keep reading.

Pay: $20.00/hr

Schedule: Full Time, Days 9–5, Monday–Friday (Seasonal Role through April 2027)

What You'll Be Doing

As the Shop Service Technician, you'll manage all aspects of the service shop in a fast-paced factory setting. You'll help deliver extraordinary products and service to customers while maintaining the highest shop service quality and safety standards.

Your day may include:

  • Performing ski tuning, mounting, base treatment, repair, binding assembly/mounting, and finishing tasks with high accuracy and attention to detail

  • Inspecting products throughout the shop work process to ensure compliance with DPS quality standards and specifications

  • Maintaining a clean, safe, and organized work area, tools, equipment, and machinery

  • Assisting with ski fulfillment preparation, packaging, labeling, and shipping of finished goods

  • Managing shop work tickets and interacting directly with fulfillment and shipping

  • Supporting inventory management activities by organizing materials, components, and finished products

  • Identifying and reporting equipment issues or process improvements to supervisors

  • Collaborating with manufacturing, warehouse, quality, and service teams to meet production goals

  • Supporting special projects, product testing, prototyping, and continuous improvement initiatives

  • Performing a variety of shop, warehouse, and production-related duties based on business needs

  • Mounting and preparing R&D skis and demo fleet for on-snow testing

  • Cross-training to assist in ski production departments during non-peak shop season

This is an active role where you'll spend most of your day on your feet, working with tools, machinery, and a team that cares deeply about quality.

What Makes You A Great Fit

  • You enjoy solving problems and figuring out how things work.

  • You like working with your hands and seeing the results of your efforts.

  • You take pride in craftsmanship, have high attention to detail, and strive to produce race-worthy work.

  • You bring a high degree of energy, self-motivation, flexibility, and a positive, collaborative spirit.

  • You thrive in a high-intensity, time-sensitive, multi-task-oriented environment.

  • You participate in and have a passion for snow sports and stay up-to-date on ski and snowboard industry products and trends.

Qualifications

  • High School diploma or equivalent preferred

  • 1 year of service technician, ski/snowboard tuning, or retail ski shop sales experience preferred

  • Working knowledge of ski tuning, base repair, edge finishing, waxing, and binding mounting procedures preferred

  • Ability to safely operate hand tools, power tools, tuning equipment, and shop machinery

  • Ability to read and interpret work orders, production documentation, and basic technical instructions

You'll Also Bring

  • Demonstrable, excellent race-worthy tuning skills

  • Mechanical aptitude with strong attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality work

  • Basic computer skills to access work orders, inventory information, or production systems

  • Demonstrated willingness to learn multiple production processes and become cross-trained across shop functions

  • Professional and effective communication skills across all levels of employees, management, executives, vendors, customers, and external partners

What To Expect

  • Hands-on work managing all aspects of the service shop in a manufacturing environment

  • A collaborative team focused on continuous improvement

  • Opportunities to cross-train, learn new equipment, and assist across production departments

  • A company passionate about innovation and outdoor adventure

  • The satisfaction of helping build and maintain some of the most respected skis in the industry

A Few Things To Know

This position requires:

  • Standing for long periods of time and moving throughout the workday in a production environment

  • Performing detailed hand work requiring fine motor skills, visual precision, and repetitive wrist, hand, or finger movements (grasping, pushing, reaching)

  • Working safely with machinery, tools, and equipment while adhering to company safety and environmental policies

  • Wearing required personal protective equipment (provided), which may include facemasks, gloves, and safety glasses

  • Regular lifting and moving of materials and products up to 20 lbs

Ready to Build Something Amazing?

Whether you're an experienced ski tech looking for your next seasonal role, a passionate tuner, or someone who loves high-quality craftsmanship, we'd love to hear from you.

Come help us deliver skis that people dream about all summer and chase all winter.

title: Interim Paycom Administrator (Independent Contractor)
description:
Interim Paycom Administrator (Independent Contractor)

Auberle

Auberle is a faith-based human services organization serving children, youth, and families across Pennsylvania. Together with our affiliates, Ward Home and the Pauline Auberle Foundation.

Auberle is engaging an independent contractor to provide Paycom system administration services during a temporary gap in internal coverage. The scope has two parts. Continuity services keep the system running day to day, centered on position management and on maintaining employee data accuracy so that accruals calculate correctly and payroll processes cleanly. Project work covers discrete improvements, configuration changes, and system edits assigned during the term. Payroll processing is performed by Auberle staff and falls outside this scope.

Scope of Services

Continuity Services

Recurring work performed throughout the term:

• Position management module maintenance, including new position setup and reclassifications, position seat adjustments, and organizational chart changes

• Employee record changes, including new hires, status and rate changes, transfers, leaves, and terminations

• Accrual verification, including accrual profile assignment, eligibility dates, and hours-based accrual triggers

• Pre-payroll data review, with discrepancies identified and resolved before each payroll cycle

• Standard and ad hoc reports as requested

• Review of monthly Paycom releases, with downstream effects audited and improvement opportunities documented

• Configuration support within the notification center, talent management (PAFs and PDFs), Benefits Administration, and Talent Acquisition modules

• Consultation with the HR team and Paycom specialists on system issues, with resolutions determined and applied by the contractor

• A written log of issues, decisions, and configuration changes, delivered at the close of the engagement

Project Work

Discrete assignments issued during the term, which may include:

• Targeted configuration changes and system edits within existing modules

• Testing and deployment of new Paycom features and configurators

• Workflow refinements, including notification rules and approval routing

• Data cleanup, report library organization, and documentation of existing configurations

The contractor determines the methods, tools, and sequence used to complete all work described above.

Jireh is looking for an entry level Process Integration Engineer. We are looking for those newly graduated with advanced degrees (Master's or PhD) in Electrical Engineering. This focus of this position is to work with device/process module/product engineering group to develop silicon power device process technology and improve existing technology yield. Primary responsibilities are to process flow implementation, electrical characterization (failure analysis), and wafer level testing yield monitoring.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Focus on Power Device (MOSFET/TVS etc.) technologies development in Jireh Semiconductor
    Development:
  • Perform process simulation, Create technology process flows with process specifications

  • Design statistical experiments and analyze results to optimize device architecture and/or process modules. Perform device characterization and report on the results
  • Collaborate with design groups within the company to troubleshoot device related problem, provide documentation and expertise to maximize the efficient use of process technologies
  • Develop devices that ensure the highest level of reliability for products. Work with the Product Engineering and Reliability group to test, characterize and evaluate device and process
  • New Product Introduction

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS

The ideal candidate will have knowledge of semiconductor device physics and experience with device processing and integration, test structure definition, design rule generation, DOE, failure analysis, process control document (PCD) generation, and device characterization. Experience with discrete power devices is preferred

title: System Administrator (Azure)
description:
Expression is seeking an experienced Systems Administrator with expertise on Azure Cloud Operations to support the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) Federal Spectrum Data Systems (FSDS) program within the Department of Commerce.

NTIA's Office of Spectrum Management manages electromagnetic spectrum use for the Federal Government and operates national security and unclassified systems used to assign frequencies, maintain spectrum-use databases, review Federal telecommunications systems, and perform spectrum engineering assessments. The FSDS program supports NTIA's modernization of its spectrum-management systems through improved technologies, architectures, automation, and interoperability.

The Systems Administrator will provide Azure cloud operations and maintenance support for Secret and Unclassified spectrum IT systems, helping maintain their security, availability, performance, recoverability, and operational functionality. The position will work across Azure Commercial, Government, and Secret cloud environments and support NTIA's transition of additional systems into production.

Clearance: Active Secret clearance required

Location: Hybrid/on-site up to 3 days per week, or as required for classified work, at the Herbert C. Hoover Building, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform day-to-day operations and maintenance of Azure environments supporting NTIA Secret and Unclassified spectrum systems.
  • Perform system and application patching, backup validation and testing, account troubleshooting, licensing activities, scripting, and routine system administration.
  • Implement and maintain applicable Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and support remediation of identified security findings.
  • Monitor Azure dashboards to identify infrastructure health issues, application or system performance degradation, and site-wide alerts.
  • Configure and maintain Azure Log Analytics Workspaces to support centralized log aggregation, alerting, dashboards, operational reporting, and troubleshooting.
  • Support security-focused implementations and technical initiatives across Azure environments.
  • Assist the Task Order security team with technical information and updates required to maintain Authority to Operate (ATO) documentation.
  • Support POA&M remediation activities and resolution of identified vulnerabilities and security deficiencies.
  • Utilize SIEM capabilities to collect, correlate, monitor, and analyze security events supporting threat detection, troubleshooting, and incident response.
  • Apply cloud networking knowledge to troubleshoot connectivity and performance issues and support infrastructure enhancements.
  • Operate and maintain authentication and authorization infrastructure, including Microsoft Entra ID, conditional access policies, Virtual Networks, and associated service infrastructure.
  • Support Azure environment enhancements and configuration changes.
  • Maintain data backups and recovery procedures for mission-critical systems and periodically validate recoverability.
  • Support database and data-management activities associated with operational systems.
  • Support operations across Azure Commercial, Government, and Secret cloud environments.
  • Support data movement across security domains using the Azure Data Transfer Cross-Domain tool.
  • Support classified systems and SIPR network operations as required.
  • Conduct periodic Azure environment cost analysis and develop recommendations for cost optimization.
  • Maintain operational functionality and availability for critical NTIA applications, including Spectrum XXI, IRACnet, FMRS, EL-CID Online, FWDP, and IQLink.
  • Work independently and collaboratively within an Agile/Scrum environment to resolve incidents, implement changes, and sustain production services.
  • Maintain accurate operational, configuration, security, and technical documentation.
  • Contribute to required contractual reporting and technical deliverables.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a relevant field and 10+ years of systems administration experience.
  • 5+ years of database and data-management experience.
  • Azure Expert-level certification, such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert, or equivalent.
  • Demonstrated expertise supporting Azure Commercial, Government, and Secret cloud environments.
  • Demonstrated expertise with the Azure Data Transfer Cross-Domain tool.
  • Experience supporting SIPR networks and classified systems operations.
  • Experience administering Microsoft Azure infrastructure and services.
  • Experience with Microsoft Entra ID, authentication, authorization, conditional access, Virtual Networks, and related Azure service infrastructure.
  • Experience with Azure monitoring, logging, alerting, and Log Analytics Workspaces.
  • Experience performing patching, backup/recovery, vulnerability remediation, system troubleshooting, and security hardening.
  • Experience implementing and maintaining STIG-compliant systems.
  • Experience using SIEM technologies for security monitoring, event analysis, and incident-response support.
  • Experience supporting ATO documentation and POA&M remediation activities.
  • Experience with cloud networking and troubleshooting.
  • Experience with scripting and systems-administration automation.

Certifications:

  • Must satisfy DoD 8140 IAT Level II requirements.
  • CompTIA Security+ certification required.
  • Azure Expert-level certification, such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert, or equivalent.

Program Deliverables

The Systems Administrator may support preparation, maintenance, and technical inputs for:

  • Weekly Activity Reports (WARs)
  • Contract Monthly Reports (CMRs)
  • Monthly Risk Matrix
  • Interim Progress Review (IPR) briefing materials

title: IT Endpoint Administrator
description:

title: Assistant Product Owner, CCA Mission Autonomy (Platform Integration) (R5849)
description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit . Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

Job Description:

The Assistant Product Owner (APO) supports Shield AI's delivery of mission autonomy (MA) to the U.S. Air Force (USAF) Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program — the first time that USAF has decoupled, for procurement purposes, MA from the airframe as a standalone capability. In this context, the ‘product’ is the Autonomy Implementation package, including Mission Autonomy itself, the Human Machine Interface (HMI) software, A-GRA compliance, mission systems, training, cybersecurity, and the full suite of implementation/installation software.

Shield AI’s CCA programs adopt an agile framework and are organized as a leadership tier overseeing multiple shoals (from platform integration to autonomy capabilities), each with multiple feature crews. In the first instance, the APO will support the Platform Integration and Support shoal (Shoal 1), which is responsible for integrating MA with multiple platforms and with the operator interface. The APO will work in collaboration with the Shoal Lead, Systems Engineering Lead, and four Feature Crew Leads and report directly to the Product Owner/Manager, who is part of the program leadership team. The APO owns the day-to-day health of the Shoal 1 product backlog in Jira (and Confluence), and is expected to maintain an integrated picture of how customer priorities, epics, interfaces, dependencies, and milestones relate, and to make ‘product’ legible and accessible to the broader team.

What you'll do:

  • Work with the Product Owner and Chief Engineer to understand customer product needs (across the CCA program office, platform providers, and operational end users) and to determine priority, separating must-have capability from deferrable scope
  • Elicit and validate needs and priorities from the customer, including official guidance and scoping documents, and from operational subject matter experts or surrogate end users as available
  • Translate customer intent into customer needs into user stories and epic descriptions — including value proposition, success criteria, acceptance criteria, expected effort and timeline, dependencies, risks, and preconditions for success — against which feature crews can execute their sprints
  • Own day-to-day management of the Shoal 1 epic backlog across feature crews, including maintaining traceability with customer requirements, refining the backlog, and monitoring backlog updates to ensure changes in priority or scope are surfaced and their rationale documented appropriately
  • Provide a product perspective to feature crews at Shoal 1-specific sprint planning and review ceremonies, by maintaining an informal integrated product map of epics, interfaces, dependencies, and program milestones
  • In collaboration with the Shoal Lead, manage dependencies across shoals, and carry integration decisions and associated implementation implications through to the respective shoal or feature crew leads, or collaboration partner
  • In collaboration with the Shoal Lead, support development and integration of the operator interface, primarily through the backlog — the HMI feature crew owns delivery, the Shoal Lead owns requirements and acceptance, and the APO owns description, communication, and prioritization of epics
  • Keep protected weekly hands-on time in the operator interface, so that HMI-specific epics and instructions can be written from first-hand use rather than second-hand reports
  • Support the platform integration crew in their interaction with vendors
  • Act as translator across disciplines — normalize preferred terminology and make specialist discussion accessible to the whole team, ensuring general consistency
  • Support other shoals (e.g., Systems Engineering, T&E) through observation of operator-in-the-loop (OITL) activity and by providing feedback in review sessions

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, aerospace engineering, cognitive systems engineering, human factors, or a related technical field; or equivalent military or operational experience
  • 3+ years in product ownership or a related field (e.g., customer experience, human factors, cognitive systems engineering, human-machine teaming, systems engineering, or technical program management for complex software or aerospace systems)
  • Hands-on proficiency with Jira and Confluence as systems of record, including demonstrated experience authoring and managing epics, user stories, and acceptance criteria in an agile environment
  • Demonstrated ability to hold an integrated view of a complex product across distributed documentation and multiple engineering disciplines
  • Willingness to become a hands-on user of the operator interface, independently installing, configuring, and running mission scenarios
  • Working technical fluency in mission autonomy, autonomous systems, flight software, ground control systems or HMIs, or avionics interfaces
  • Exceptional written and oral communication, and proven ability to translate information across technical audiences without diluting technical accuracy
  • Strong problem solving skills, including sound decision making and judgment under ambiguity with minimal supervision
  • Ability to work effectively, both independently and as part of a team
  • Must be a U.S. person as defined under ITAR
  • Active U.S. DoD Secret security clearance is required at time of hire. Must be eligible for, and capable of obtaining and maintaining, Top Secret, SCI, and/or Special Access Program (SAP) level clearance/access
  • Ability to travel domestically approximately 15–25%

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience supporting a U.S. Air Force, Navy, or joint aviation program of record involving uncrewed or autonomous collaborative platforms
  • Familiarity with the A-GRA, A-GRI, UCI messaging, or other modular open systems architectures
  • Experience with airworthiness, functional safety, or assurance-driven software processes and certification artifacts
  • Exposure to flight autonomy, vehicle management systems, or aircraft-level integration and flight test campaigns
  • Experience with C2 or HMI products for uncrewed systems (e.g., STANAG 4586, MAVLink, CoT, TAK)
  • Formal grounding in product, human factors, or cognitive systems engineering methods
  • Experience supporting OITL evaluations, test and evaluation campaigns, or functional check flight activity as a product or human factors representative
  • Proficiency with systems and process modeling tools (e.g., Cameo), and with reading interface control documents (ICDs)
  • Experience establishing decision logs, change control, or product governance in a program that previously lacked them
  • Experience coordinating directly with platform manufacturers, primes, or government program offices
  • Military aviation, flight test, or uncrewed aircraft systems operational experience
  • Advanced degree in engineering, business (e.g., MBA), or related field (e.g., computer science, aerospace, cognitive systems engineering, human factors)
  • Current or prior Special Access Program (SAP) or Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access

title: Physiotherapist
description:
Physiotherapist - Sarnia, ON

Position Type: Freelance, Casual

About Therapia:

Founded in 2015, Therapia is redefining physiotherapy by delivering care directly to patients’ homes. Guided by our mission to deliver high-quality, personalized care that meets people where they are, we aim to improve accessibility, connect the healthcare system, and shift the focus from sick care to true health care through prevention, healthy lifestyles, and compassionate support.

By joining our growing network of motivated Registered Physiotherapists, you will be part of a team that shares your dedication to helping people achieve their best health. With Therapia, you will enjoy the freedom to set your own schedule, earn more than traditional clinic settings, and use technology that makes the experience seamless for both you and your patients.

Your Role at Therapia:

As a physiotherapist at Therapia, you will conduct in-home physiotherapy assessments and treat a range of acute and chronic conditions, while also focusing on wellness and prevention to help patients maintain their health and stay active long term. Working independently, you will use our platform to communicate with patients, while being supported by our administrative team who will manage marketing and scheduling for you.

What’s In It For You?

  • Earn more money with a higher compensation split!
  • Set your own schedule: Take on as many or few clients as you’d like – hassle free!
  • Focus on patient care: Booking, billing, marketing – leave it up to us!
  • Be your own boss: Streamline your practice with our easy-to-use intuitive online platform designed for efficient caseload management!

What We Expect From You:

  • Conduct Assessment and Develop Care Plans: Perform comprehensive in-home physiotherapy assessments to evaluate mobility, strength, pain and function. Use clinical reasoning to develop personalized, goal-orientated treatment plans.
  • Deliver Evidence Based Treatment: Provide hands on and/or virtual physiotherapy including manual techniques, therapeutic exercises and active rehab interventions tailored to each patient’s needs
  • Monitor Progress and Adjust Plans: Track outcomes, update treatment goals and be adaptable to patients changing needs to ensure they are progressing and reaching milestones
  • Ensure Safety and Compliance: Assess home environments for safety risks, follow infection control protocols and adhere to regulatory documentation standards.
  • Manage Your Caseload Independently: Use Therapia’s convenient platform to manage clinical notes and coordinate directly with patients in your preferred service area.
  • Educate and Empower Your Patients: Instruct patients and families on home exercise programs, and post-operative care to support recovery and independence.
  • Collaborate with our Administrative Team: Coordinate your schedule and availability with the team to ensure seamless operation for patient bookings.

Requirements:

  • Registered and in good standing with the College of Physiotherapists in the region for which care is provided
  • New grads welcome (also accepting physiotherapy residents)
  • Strong communication and organizational skills
  • Experience in orthopedic, post-surgical, Pediatric or geriatric physiotherapy is considered a strong asset
  • Flexibility to travel at least 30 minutes to patients’ homes is highly preferred

If you are a motivated self-starter with a passion for collaboration and innovation, and you are eager to be part of a forward thinking health tech company transforming care delivery, we want to hear from you. Apply now!

Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:
We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all races, ethnicities, religions, genders, sexual orientations, gender identities or expressions, ages, disabilities, and protected veteran status. Accommodation is available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

description:

title: Bilingual Intake Specialist
description:
About the organization: Compass Family Services is a 100+ year old nonprofit working on the front lines of San Francisco’s homeless crisis. We provide families experiencing or at risk of homelessness with comprehensive support to address immediate needs and ensure long-term success.

About the team: The Intake Specialist is part of the Compass Family Resource Center team. The Resource Center supports homeless and at-risk families through access to basic goods (diapers, food, clothing), service referrals, case management, job search support, drop-in childcare, and family-centered support groups and classes.

Compensation: $27 - $31 hourly

Schedule: Monday - Friday, 9 am - 5 pm

Location: 37 Grove St, San Francisco

Organizational Core Competencies: Accountable I Adaptable I Client-centered I Collaborative I Committed to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging I Resourceful

Responsibilities:
The Bilingual Intake Specialist will spend most of their time conducting initial intake interviews with families who come to Compass’ office in need of support. During the intake, they determine which programs families are eligible for and provide families with information and referrals. They also work closely with the rest of the Family Resource Center team to ensure that the Center is running smoothly.

Specific responsibilities include:

  • Welcome families as they arrive at Compass Family Services. Conduct initial assessment to understand their needs, provide information about available services, and guide them through their options within Compass Family Services and in the community.
  • Screen families for eligibility across various programs, complete Navigation Forms during drop-in intakes, and provide direct referrals to connect families to resources.
  • Collaborate with Office Manager/Receptionist to maintain smooth family flow within the building, ensuring they are directed to the appropriate program.
  • Train and mentor interns and volunteers on intake and drop-in best practices and protocols for family service delivery.
  • Work closely with colleagues to assess emerging family needs, identify trends and maintain updated resources and information.
  • Ensure accurate, up-to-date records gathered through Navigation Forms, other documents as applicable in Compass' Salesforce database, adhering to best practices in data management.
  • Organize and manage client records/information to support consistency and quality assurance across the team.
  • Support Distribution Center operations including inventory management, restocking, volunteer support, and distribution of basic needs items such as food, diapers, baby wipes, and hygiene products.

    Qualifications:

    • Fluency or high level of professional proficiency in Spanish and English required
    • Understanding of trauma-informed care and issues facing homeless families.
    • Knowledge of San Francisco social service resources.
    • Experience working in crisis situations; ability to assess and de-escalate situations quickly
    • Strong computer skills with proficiency in Microsoft programs (Outlook, Word, Excel, etc.). Salesforce experience is a plus.
    • Outstanding work habits: strong communication skills, reliable, team-oriented, organized
    • Demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging work.
    • Able to lift at least 25 pounds (essential for working with a team to handle diaper/food/clothing deliveries).

    Compensation, Benefits and Location:

    • Salary range: $27 - $31 per hour, 7.5 hours per day / 37.5 hours per week. Non-exempt.
    • Paid time off: 4 weeks of vacation your first year, 5 in your second. Also paid holidays, sick time, family leave.
    • Insurance: health, dental and vision insurance are fully covered by Compass for employees and dependent children. We also provide long term disability and life insurance.
    • Retirement: after one year of work, Compass contributes an amount equal to 5% of your salary into a retirement account; this vests during years 2-6.
    • Location: 37 Grove St, San Francisco. Fully on site, no remote days.
    • Membership in OPEIU/Local 29 union.

    To Apply:

    Please apply through our online application. No phone calls, please.

    Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We are an equal opportunity employer and actively seek to recruit a diverse workforce. Compass embraces the idea that Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging contribute to the success of our underserved communities, and therefore to shared prosperity in our city and region. Compass Family Services is committed to the continuous work of implementing specific actions that will disrupt systemic prejudice and improve equity across programs and departments, to become an example to partners who also believe in a culture of inclusion that leverages diversity.

    Consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act and California civil rights law, Compass Family Services will provide reasonable accommodation when requested by a qualified applicant or candidate with a disability, unless such accommodation would cause an undue hardship for the agency. Requests for reasonable accommodation apply to all aspects of the hiring process. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please use the answer box for the final question of the job application to let us know.

title: Software Engineer 2--M365 UIPilot team
description:
Overview

The UIPilot team at Microsoft builds an AI-powered computer-use platform that enables agents to interact with software and carry out tasks across applications and operating systems. We combine AI, cross-platform interaction, and cloud infrastructure to translate human intent into reliable execution—from individual actions to complex, multi-step workflows.

As a Software Engineer on the UIPilot team, you will build capabilities across agent planning and reasoning, application interaction, execution orchestration, and failure recovery. You will help make computer-use agents more capable, reliable, and scalable, enabling scenarios spanning productivity, workflow automation, and software validation.

We are looking for hands-on engineers with strong ownership, curiosity, and critical thinking. You should enjoy using AI to build software, exploring unfamiliar systems, and investigating problems deeply—while applying independent judgment and validating conclusions with evidence.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities
  • Advance AI-powered computer use: Develop agent capabilities for planning, interacting with applications, evaluating outcomes, and recovering from failures across web and desktop environments.
  • Build scalable platform capabilities: Design and deliver backend services, APIs, execution orchestration, and user-facing tools that support scenario onboarding and reliable execution across applications and operating systems.
  • Strengthen reliability and diagnosability: Investigate issues across AI behavior, agent execution, application interactions, and cloud infrastructure.
  • Establish root causes and improve evaluation, observability, performance, and recovery mechanisms.
  • Accelerate engineering with AI: Use AI-powered coding agents throughout development and identify opportunities to integrate AI into engineering workflows.
  • Validate solutions for correctness, security, reliability, and measurable impact.
  • Own end-to-end engineering outcomes: Drive features from problem definition and technical design through implementation and production validation.
  • Make thoughtful trade-offs and apply strong code review, testing, documentation, and operational practices.


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 2+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python OR equivalent experience.

Other Requirements:

Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 3+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 5+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • Solid ownership, curiosity, and critical thinking: Take responsibility for outcomes, seek to understand how systems work, and investigate beyond surface-level symptoms.
  • Question assumptions, consider alternative explanations, and validate hypotheses with evidence.
  • Follow through on resolution, collaborating and escalating when appropriate.
  • Proficiency with AI-powered coding agents: Effectively use agentic tools to explore codebases, plan and implement changes, generate tests, and investigate failures.
  • Recognize that AI-generated code and explanations may be incorrect or incomplete, and independently verify outputs through code inspection, testing, and runtime evidence.
  • Solid engineering fundamentals and troubleshooting skills: Build maintainable software using Python or another relevant language, with the ability to work effectively in a Python-based stack.
  • Understand APIs, automated testing, and service interactions, and reason clearly about system behavior and failure modes.
  • Independent execution and effective collaboration: Translate ambiguous problems into actionable plans, make sound technical judgments, and clearly communicate findings, decisions, risks, and next steps.
  • Experience building AI-powered agents, tool integrations, or computer-use capabilities, including planning, task evaluation, and execution recovery.
  • Familiarity with FastAPI, Playwright, Windows UI automation, or TypeScript/React.
  • Familiarity with iOS, Android, MacOS development and automation.
  • Experience with distributed execution, containers, Kubernetes/AKS, or Azure services, including CI/CD, observability, and production troubleshooting.

This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.

Our House empowers homeless and near-homeless families and individuals to succeed in the workforce, in school, and in life through hard work, wise decision-making, and active participation in the community. The Our House team has defined a set of seven Guiding Principles that characterize our culture and that we intentionally seek to uphold: Hard Work, Wise Decision-Making, Community, Initiative, Integrity, Safety, and Heart.

description:
About Agile Defense

Our vision is to bring adaptive innovation to support our nation's most important missions through the seamless integration of advanced technologies, elite minds, and unparalleled agility—leveraging a foundation of speed, flexibility, and ingenuity to strengthen and protect our nation’s vital interests.

Job Title: Programming Specialist
Location: Fort Huachuca, AZ On-Site

SUMMARY

Performs software development and maintenance of applications and systems for the organization. Plans and coordinates all activities related to the design, development, and implementation of the organization’s applications. Conducts software coding, testing, debugging, and installation of an organization’s application systems. Documents requirements for databases, applications, and systems. Ensures projects are completed on time and within budget. Assists in the formulation of procedures and best practices for users of applications and systems.

Performs a variety of complicated tasks. A certain degree of creativity and latitude is required. Works under general supervision. Typically reports to a project leader, supervisor, or manager. Must be adept at problem solving, identifying risk, and communicating results and recommendations to department management.

Duties include but are not limited to: Developing and implementing software solutions: Programming specialists design and create software applications to meet business requirements. Debugging and testing: They troubleshoot and test software to ensure it functions correctly and efficiently. Collaborating with teams: Programming specialists work with other team members to coordinate and execute specific projects. Providing program updates and reports: They provide regular updates and reports to management, helping to track the success of their programs. These duties highlight the importance of a programming specialist's technical expertise and their ability to work collaboratively and manage projects effectively.

REQUIREMENTS

Requires Bachelor’s degree; or an Associate’s degree with at least 4 years of experience; or a minimum of 60 semester hours of formal education working towards an associate or bachelor’s degree and at least 6 years of experience; or at least 8 years of experience is required. Additional certifications (other than those required for the position) in the area of specialization be substituted for experience or education but varies by certification. The degree must be in a relevant technical curriculum and experience must be related to the job duties.

Recommended Certifications: Microsoft Azure Developer, AWS Developer, Google Cloud Developer, CIW Web Developer, Oracle JAVA SE, Redhat, C++, C#, A+

WORKING CONDITIONS

Work is indoors collaborating with team members. Climb stairs, sedentary, lift up to 10 lbs.
Our Core Values
Employees of Agile Defense are our number one priority, and the importance we place on our culture here is fundamental. Our culture is alive and evolving, but it always stays true to its roots. Here, you are valued as a family member, and we believe that we can accomplish great things together. What makes us Agile? We call it the 6Hs, the values that define our culture and guide everything we do. Together, these values infuse vibrancy, integrity, and a tireless work ethic into advancing the most important national security and critical civilian missions. It's how we show up every day. It's who we are.
  • Happy - Be Infectious. Happiness multiplies and creates a positive and connected environment where motivation and satisfaction have an outsized effect on everything we do.
  • Helpful - Be Supportive. Being helpful is the foundation of teamwork, resulting in a supportive atmosphere where collaboration flourishes, and collective success is celebrated.
  • Honest - Be Trustworthy. Honesty serves as our compass, ensuring transparent communication and ethical conduct, essential to who we are and the complex domains we support.
  • Humble - Be Grounded. Success is not achieved alone, humility ensures a culture of mutual respect, encouraging open communication, and a willingness to learn from one another and take on any task.
  • Hungry - Be Eager. Our hunger for excellence drives an insatiable appetite for innovation and continuous improvement, propelling us forward in the face of new and unprecedented challenges.
  • Hustle - Be Driven. Hustle is reflected in our relentless work ethic, where we are each committed to going above and beyond to advance the mission and achieve success.
