title: Clinical Product Lead
description:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 75,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 1 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About the Role

At Headway, we're building the future of behavioral health — and increasingly, that means shipping products that providers and patients rely on every day. We're hiring a Clinical Product Lead to own the clinical judgment behind how risk gets detected, escalated, and closed out across our platform, and to make sure every product surface we build is connected to the safety systems behind it.

Headway already has real safety capability through risk detection, human triage, a 24/7 crisis partner, and more. However as our platform expands, particularly into AI tooling, so does our need for a single coherent system and point of ownership for patient safety across product surfaces.

This role sits on our Clinical Product team, partnering daily with engineering, product, and clinical operations. You'll also carry the clinical safety bar for our AI surfaces.

This is a first-of-its-kind role. You'll help define what "safe" means for a behavioral health platform operating at the scale of our network — and then build the products and systems that make it true rather than aspirational.

You will:

  • Own the clinical requirements for how patient risk is detected and mitigated through our platform surfaces including the patient portal, support chat and phone, clinical assessments, conversational intake, and more. Drive us toward one shared severity taxonomy and routing model.

  • Serve as the Clinical Product Patient Safety partner for product features that carry the potential for risk disclosure. Define safety requirements and safeguards, integrate the product into existing escalations structures, and red-team the failure points. Stay with the feature after launch to review how the safeguards performed.

  • Audit our product surfaces to identify patient safety gaps. Collaborate within the clinical team and with cross functional partners to close those gaps.

  • Support us in holding the clinical safety and quality bar for our AI surfaces such as AI-generated clinical notes, treatment planning, and conversational tools. Write rubrics, label the gold-standard cases our models learn from, and audit model output against your own clinical assessment.

  • Resolve risk-ownership questions and ensure that our policies and the platform clearly and accurately reflect that position.

  • Communicate tradeoffs clearly to non-clinical stakeholders — including when speed, scale, or automation must be balanced against clinical rigor — and push back constructively when product or technical decisions conflict with sound clinical judgment.

You will love this role if:

  • You are an Independently Licensed Therapist (LPC, LCSW, PhD, or PsyD) with 3+ years of post-graduate clinical experience.

  • You have worked inside a safety or quality system and feel extremely confident in risk assessment and safety planning, and crisis response.

  • You are a systems thinker. You can look at a set of disconnected escalation paths and see the single model underneath.

  • You thrive working quickly and cross-functionally with engineers, product partners, and operations teams. You're comfortable saying "what you’re proposing carries some risk, and here's the clinical reason why," and you know how to make that feedback actionable for people who don't share your clinical training.

  • You are a first-principles thinker who can break down fuzzy clinical concepts (therapeutic alliance, medical necessity, risk assessment, patient safety) into something concrete enough to label, evaluate, and ship against.

  • You have a working understanding of how AI models are evaluated — concepts like precision, recall, and false positive rates don't intimidate you, and you can connect them to real clinical consequences (e.g., what it means for a model to miss a safety concern vs. over-flag one).

  • You are flexible and energized by ambiguity. Headway's clinical AI roadmap will shift across the next year, and you're excited to flex across quality, safety, and product AI projects as our needs evolve.

  • You are motivated by the opportunity to improve access to high-quality behavioral healthcare at scale.

Compensation and Benefits:

The expected base pay range for this position is $127,840 - $188,000, based on a variety of factors including qualifications, experience, and geographic location.

We are committed to offering a comprehensive and competitive total rewards package, including robust health and wellness benefits, retirement savings, and meaningful ownership opportunities through equity. Compensation decisions are made holistically, ensuring fairness and alignment with market benchmarks while recognizing individual contributions and potential.

Benefits offered include:

  • Equity Compensation

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage

  • HSA / FSA

  • 401K

  • Work-from-Home Stipend

  • 16-week parental leave for eligible employees

  • Carrot Fertility annual reimbursement and membership

  • 13 paid holidays each year as well as a Holiday Break during the week between December 25th and December 31st

  • Flexible PTO

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

  • Training and professional development

We believe a team's strength is in its people, and we cannot achieve this mission without a team that reflects the diversity of this problem – across race, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, age, national origin, religion, family status, disability, military status, and experience. Headway is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Headway will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodations. title: Research Scientist, Contextual AI and Multimodal Agents

title: Senior Security Engineer (Remote, EU/CET)
description:
About Maze

Maze is the user research platform that helps companies build the right products faster by making user insights available at the speed of product development.

In most companies, research demand far exceeds supply. Time, cost, and lack of access to expertise hold teams back. In today’s AI-powered world, anyone can build a product fast. The real challenge? Deeply understanding user needs and building the right product. That’s where Maze comes in.

We believe companies shouldn’t have to choose between building fast and building right. Maze makes research accessible, intuitive, and fast so product teams can put user insights at the center of every decision.

Our platform enables researchers, designers, and product managers to quickly recruit participants, run studies autonomously, and surface insights that actually drive product decisions. Our AI capabilities automate the busywork and add depth and direction to the insights themselves.

That’s why Maze was recently named the #1 user research platform in UX Tools’ Design Tools Survey—and why we’re scaling fast across industries like B2B SaaS, e-Commerce, Financial Services, Retail, and Automotive, supporting world class customers such as Uber, Amazon, Atlassian, Anthropic & more.

Maze is a Series B company backed by top-tier investors (Felicis, Emergence & Amplify). We operate a global remote workforce driven by our core values.

Senior Security Engineer

Location: Remote, preference for Netherlands, United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain or Portugal. Key engineering and product teams are based in these locales.

About the Role

We’re hiring a Senior Security Engineer to take the lead on security at Maze. You’ll own two closely connected areas:

  • The corporate IT foundation every Maze employee relies on

  • The security controls that keep our cloud, code and SaaS environment secure and auditable

Identity, devices and access sit right at the intersection of IT and security. This is an opportunity to own that space end to end. Your job is to automate the IT side so well that most of your time goes to corporate security engineering. You own the budget and tooling to automate the IT layer, and the helpdesk scope stays deliberately small, so the role stays an engineering role.

You’ll report to our Senior Manager, Platform Engineering and work closely with teams across Maze.

As a Senior Security Engineer at Maze, you will:

  • Own identity and SSO in Google Workspace, including groups, SCIM provisioning, MFA and access policies

  • Run our macOS fleet through Iru, including enrolment, configuration, patching and compliance

  • Automate joiner, mover and leaver flows from Rippling so new hires are fully provisioned on day one and leavers lose access within hours

  • Own SaaS licensing and app provisioning, while keeping internal support lightweight through automation and self-service

  • Own security controls across AWS, GitHub, Kubernetes and our SaaS environment, including role based access, IAM hygiene, cloud guardrails, network boundaries and secrets management

  • Run vulnerability management end to end, taking findings from Intruder, Socket and pentests through remediation and verification with clear owners and SLAs

  • Run regular access reviews and generate audit evidence through Vanta, making compliance thorough, timely and low effort

  • Bring a security perspective to incidents and post-incident reviews, turning what we learn into stronger controls

  • Use AI-assisted and agentic workflows to reduce manual work and investigate issues faster

What you won’t own

Application code review and threat modelling, sales questionnaires, customer security calls or other customer-facing security work. These sit with our Senior Manager, Platform Engineering today and will move into the Infosec function as business needs grow.

What we’re looking for

  • You have a strong software, infrastructure or security engineering background and are comfortable using code and infrastructure as code to automate repetitive work

  • You’ve owned identity, MDM and joiner and leaver automation at a remote company and can speak to the impact your automation had

  • You’ve secured a modern AWS or GCP environment and can explain the trade-offs behind your IAM decisions

  • You’ve run vulnerability management or access reviews in an environment with external audits

  • You have experience with SOC 2 or ISO 27001 controls and know how to turn a control into an automated check

  • You care about the employee experience and are comfortable saying no when needed while providing context and a better path forward

  • You’re excited about AI-assisted development and actively use modern AI tools in your work

Our stack

  • Identity and people systems: Google Workspace, Rippling

  • Devices: Iru (formerly Kandji), macOS

  • Cloud and infrastructure: AWS, GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, Docker

  • Security and compliance: Vanta, Intruder, Socket, Datadog Security, Riot

  • Network: Cloudflare Zero Trust

  • CI/CD: GitHub Actions, Depot CI, Argo CD

  • Observability: Datadog

  • Collaboration: Slack, Notion, Linear, GitHub, Zoom

  • Application: TypeScript, Node.js, React

You don’t need experience with every technology in our stack. We care more about strong fundamentals, an engineering approach to both IT and security and excitement about making Maze secure by default as we scale.

Inclusivity and Pay

At Maze, we are dedicated to building an equitable, inclusive, and authentic workspace. Unique and diverse perspectives are welcomed, and continuous growth is encouraged. We believe that people are more than their resumes, so if your past experience looks different than the criteria listed, we'd still love to hear from you. We appreciate and celebrate non-traditional life routes and encourage you to apply should you connect with a job description or the Maze culture.

Maze values transparency and it enables us to approach compensation equitably across the world. We are informed by data and regularly check our salary ranges (either United States or Rest of World) against other venture backed companies. Additionally, we are proud of our holistic and generous benefits offerings, included in every compensation package.

Your salary is dependent upon many factors, including years of experience, expertise, etc. During your first interview, you can expect to have an open conversation with your recruiter regarding your compensation expectations.

Why Maze is unique

  • Early-stage startup: You will join an early-stage startup with less than 150 team members. This means you'll have the unique opportunity to directly impact success and help shape the future of Maze.

  • Market disruption: We believe that the way companies build products is fundamentally broken and the user research market is ripe for disruption. For too long, companies have been forced to choose between rapid development without user insights or investing months into research before bringing products to market. But there's finally a groundswell building around a path forward that eliminates this compromise - and Maze is leading the charge.

  • Product-market Fit: Maze is used by 100,000+ brands across 4,000 companies, from SMB to enterprises, and in the last fiscal year, we saw 6.5M questions answered, supporting 25K decisions

Benefits

  • Health insurance with international coverage, vision, and dental: 100% of the team member premium paid

    • For some locations, coverage options vary, please see our benefits pages for more information

  • Free access to proper mental health care, unlimited virtual therapy sessions (with a human) and 24/7 access to resources

  • Life and Disability Insurance, 100% of the team member premium paid

  • Flexible time off

  • Meaningful equity

  • Company retreats, fully paid for by Maze

  • New MacBook (laptop), paid for by Maze

  • Paid Family leave: 16 weeks for birth or adoptive parents

  • $500/month to be used for dependent health insurance coverage

    • If you don't have dependents to add to your plan, you will still get access to this money to be used at your discretion to get the benefits that matter to you with our flexible a-maze-ing benefits - gym memberships, co-working spaces, food, travel, whatever!

  • $1,500 remote work setup fund to ensure you can set up a productive work space

  • Flexible work schedule where you manage your own working hours

  • Monthly points that are awarded to others to recognize teamwork, dedication and helpfulness - points can be cashed out for gift cards and more

  • Virtual social engagements randomly throughout the year

  • SWAG, we have some really cool swag

  • Open, transparent culture that includes virtual: coffee chats, bi-weekly all-hands meetings, and more

Check out all of our a-maze-ing benefits here.

Outreach Notice

We understand you might be excited about the job you’re applying for, we are excited you are interested! However, please refrain from reaching out to our current team members on LinkedIn for referrals. Our policy is that referrals can only be provided by team members who personally know the candidate. With the high volume of interest in our roles, contacting our team members who are not involved in recruitment can be overwhelming. Additionally, please avoid submitting support tickets regarding your application, as our support team is not involved in the hiring process. Rest assured, our recruitment team is diligently reviewing all applications and will reach out directly if there is a match.

A qualified candidate for this position would be responsible for network modification, operation, integration, maintenance, security, and implementation of services for the as-fielded Agency network.

title: Great Springs Project: Operations Intern
description:
Great Springs Project
2026 Summer Internship

ABOUT GREAT SPRINGS PROJECT
Great Springs Project (GSP) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization working to create a greenway of contiguous protected lands between San Antonio and Austin over the Edwards Aquifer recharge zone. This green corridor will include an additional 50,000 acres of protected lands across four counties and be connected by a network of spring-to-spring trails, linking four of Texas' Great Springs: Barton Springs, San Marcos Springs, Comal Springs, and San Antonio Springs. Great Springs Project envisions unifying existing local efforts to address the most critical water, land, wildlife, and public health challenges facing the Central Texas region.

In a state where less than four percent of the land is public, by preserving open space and developing a spring-to-spring trail for the benefit of all, GSP addresses social, health, and recreational equity.

GSP INTERNSHIP OVERVIEW
Position

title: GL&C Performance and Execution Leader
description:
Description

Who We Are

Liberty Mutual's Global Legal & Compliance (GL&C) organization is in a defining period of transformation. Executing against our 2030 vision, we serve as both a protector of the enterprise and an accelerator of Liberty Mutual's ability to win in the markets where we compete.

GL&C sits at the intersection of risk, regulation, capital, and execution. As our industry faces increasing pressure around AI governance, consumer data privacy, digital claims transformation, cybersecurity resilience, and evolving global insurance regulations, we are choosing to lead.

To fulfill our vision, we are reshaping how legal work is performed, by whom, and with what technology, as generative and agentic AI fundamentally alter legal service delivery. We are deliberately positioning legal and compliance expertise as a strategic differentiator that helps Liberty Mutual adapt faster, operate smarter, and lead confidently in a rapidly changing global landscape.

About the Role

Reporting to the Chief Legal Officer as a full member of the GL&C Leadership Team, you will lead GL&C's operational engine: the shared legal services teams, centralized Home Office paralegal organization, business process outsourcing, performance intelligence, and work evolution capability that make the department scalable, measurable, and continuously improving.

You will oversee an estimated 4–6 senior leaders and approximately 50–100 professionals across shared services, the Home Office paralegal organization, and outsourced delivery — and serve as co-architect of how GL&C evolves.

Key partners include: Strategy, Intelligence & Integration (SII) Leader; GL&C Leadership Team; GL&C Data Office Leader; and People, Purpose & Brand.

What You'll Do

  • Own and operate the work evolution decision engine. Design and continuously run the framework that decomposes GL&C work by intrinsic characteristics, assesses technology maturity, selects the optimal delivery model, and governs re-evaluation triggers as the landscape evolves. Maintain a single, coherent view of how the department's work gets done, ensuring delivery model decisions are data-driven, defensible, and continuously updated.

  • Lead scaled shared services delivery and the centralized Home Office paralegal organization. Own and operate GL&C's centralized legal shared services, outsourced delivery programs, and Home Office paralegal organization as a unified operating model — driving volume, quality, cycle time, and cost outcomes from a single platform. Define and enforce consistent professional standards, career architecture, and AI adoption requirements across the paralegal population, ensuring a single bar for quality, development, and performance. Expand the scope and sophistication of centralized delivery as technology and organizational readiness allow.

  • Drive productivity and affordability outcomes. Own accountability for productivity improvements within the Performance & Execution portfolio, contributing toward GL&C's sustained 3–4% annual productivity improvement. Translate affordability commitments into operational plans that harvest savings through work model shifts, technology adoption, and optimized leverage across delivery models. Provide credible, measurable evidence of value delivery, connecting operational execution to financial impact with the rigor expected by the CLO and enterprise leadership.

  • Build and govern performance intelligence. Establish the measurement infrastructure that gives GL&C leaders visibility into delivery performance, capacity utilization, cost to serve, and work evolution progress — enabling leaders to manage with data rather than anecdote. You will define what GL&C measures and the standards behind it.

  • Partner with advisory, litigation, and compliance groups to transform work. Serve as the enterprise-wide partner to practice groups in identifying work suitable for delivery model shifts — AI automation, paralegal leverage, BPO, shared services, and self-service — challenging inertia constructively with data and an outside-in perspective. Develop deep understanding of peer priorities and business rhythms so that shared delivery teams continuously meet, adjust to, and anticipate practice group needs while driving transformation forward.

  • Integrate and scale technology-enabled delivery. Ensure the function is AI-native, embedding generative and agentic AI into core processes as standard practice. In partnership with SI&I's Data Office, identify and operationalize automation that measurably accelerates process time, reduces cost to serve, or frees capacity for higher-judgment work. Define and advocate for the technology enablement priorities of the portfolio — technology or funding decisions affecting delivery models or productivity commitments do not move forward without this function's sign-off on operational feasibility and sequencing.

  • Build a high-performing, integrated organization. Integrate previously separate teams into one cohesive function with shared vision, aligned KPIs, and a unified operating model. Serve as the department's performance truth-teller, surfacing delivery data, productivity trends, and capability gaps with clarity and candor. Build leadership capability within the function, recruit operational, analytical, and change management talent, and drive work evolution as a leadership requirement across GL&C.

  • Establish governance and decision rights. Define clear decision rights for delivery model selection, work migration, shared service delivery, paralegal standards, and performance measurement — governance that allows teams to move at pace while remaining rigorous enough to be defensible. Operate shared prioritization governance with SI&I, with neither portfolio making material decisions without the other's input.

What You'll Bring

  • Operational rigor and execution discipline at scale. You think and operate as a scaled delivery leader — building systems, processes, and measurement frameworks that produce repeatable results, managing through metrics, and connecting operational decisions to financial impact. You are skilled at integrating previously separate teams into a unified operating model, and at managing the dynamics of professionals who are organizationally centralized but operationally deployed to client groups.

  • Performance measurement and data-driven leadership. You use data as the primary language of leadership for prioritization, performance management, and investment decisions. You design measurement infrastructure, define the standards and quality thresholds that create consistency at enterprise scale, and translate complex performance data into executive-ready narratives that drive action.

  • Change leadership and cross-functional influence. You credibly challenge how work has always been done, using data, constructive framing, and respect for domain expertise. You are particularly skilled at moving service delivery from embedded to centralized while building trust that centralized models can meet practice group needs — earning the right to drive change through demonstrated results, including with groups outside your reporting line.

  • Workforce development. A track record building career architectures, development programs, and professional communities that attract, retain, and grow paralegal, operations, and analytics talent as a strategic workforce asset.

  • Legal industry fluency and technology depth. You do not need to be a lawyer, but you must be credible enough to distinguish work that carries genuine legal, regulatory, or reputational risk from work that can be safely delivered through alternative models — earning the trust of senior legal professionals who will scrutinize those decisions. You bring an operator-level understanding of how generative and agentic AI reshape legal work delivery, translating capability into operating model decisions, along with regulated-industry experience in financial services or insurance.

  • Partnership and interdependent leadership. You are comfortable with shared accountability and mutual dependency, maintaining clear lanes while collaborating deeply as one half of a leadership dyad.

Qualifications
  • Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree (MBA, J.D., or equivalent) preferred
  • Generally requires 15+ years of progressive experience in operations, shared services, business process outsourcing, transformation or professional services delivery leadership,
  • Demonstrated experience leading organizations of comparable scale, including managing leaders-of-leaders
  • Proven experience owning a scaled service delivery operation — shared services, managed services, BPO, or centralized professional services delivery — with accountability for cost, quality, and cycle time outcomes
  • Demonstrated experience leading operating model transformation and AI-enabled work evolution in a large, complex, matrixed organization
  • Experience in a regulated industry — financial services, insurance, or legal services — strongly preferred
  • Legal industry experience valued (not required)
About Us

Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Some roles at Liberty Mutual have a corresponding compensation plan which may include commission and/or bonus earnings at rates that vary based on multiple factors set forth in the compensation plan for the role.

At Liberty Mutual, our goal is to create a workplace where everyone feels valued, supported, and can thrive. We build an environment that welcomes a wide range of perspectives and experiences, with inclusion embedded in every aspect of our culture and reflected in everyday interactions. This comes to life through comprehensive benefits, workplace flexibility, professional development opportunities, and a host of opportunities provided through our Employee Resource Groups. Each employee plays a role in creating our inclusive culture, which supports every individual to do their best work. Together, we cultivate a community where everyone can make a meaningful impact for our business, our customers, and the communities we serve.

We value your hard work, integrity and commitment to make things better, and we put people first by offering you benefits that support your life and well-being. To learn more about our benefit offerings please visit:

Liberty Mutual is an equal opportunity employer. We will not tolerate discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, age, disability, veteran's status, pregnancy, genetic information or on any basis prohibited by federal, state or local law.

title: Senior Data Analyst (Product Analyst)
description:
About Thunkable

Thunkable is the leading no-code and AI platform that empowers anyone to design, develop, and deploy powerful, native mobile applications without writing a single line of code. Our mission is to make app development accessible to everyone—transforming passive consumers into active creators of technology.

Founded in 2016 by Arun Saigal and Weihua Li, former members of the MIT App Inventor and MIT Scratch team, Thunkable now supports millions of users across 184 countries, including a quarter of Fortune 500 companies. We’re backed by Lightspeed, NEA, Owl Ventures, SV Angel, and Y Combinator.

Role Overview

Thunkable is seeking a Senior Data Analyst to join our Data & Analytics team. In this role, you'll turn product and business data into actionable insights that influence product strategy, growth, and customer experience. You'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Design, Marketing, and Leadership to define success metrics, measure impact, identify opportunities, and support experimentation.

Beyond analysis, you'll help improve the quality and accessibility of our data by working with engineering on event tracking, integrating data from multiple systems, and ensuring our analytics foundation supports better decision-making across the business.

Key Responsibilities

  • Partner with Product, Marketing, and Leadership to identify opportunities, influence product strategy, and drive business decisions through data.

  • Drive end to end product and growth analyses including funnel analysis, cohort analysis, retention, segmentation, monetization, and experimentation.

  • Define success metrics and evaluate the impact of new features, experiments, and product initiatives.

  • Develop dashboards, recurring reports, and self-service analytics to enable data-informed decision making.

  • Collaborate with engineers to design, implement, validate, and maintain product event tracking within React-based interfaces.

  • Improve data reliability by identifying and troubleshooting tracking issues that impact data integrity.

  • Work with data from multiple sources (Amplitude, Google Ads, Meta Ads, payment systems, CRM, etc.) to create a unified view of the business.

  • Document key metrics, tracking plans, and data definitions to improve organizational understanding.

Required Qualifications

  • BA/BS degree or above in a related field or equivalent experience required.

  • 3+ years of work experience in data science, data analytics or other quantitative roles, with a track record of successfully delivering data analytics projects.

  • Experience with product analytics, experimentation, funnel analysis, retention, and user behavior analysis.

  • Experience with event tracking instrumentation and collaborating with engineering teams to validate and maintain analytics implementations.

  • Experience with handling real-time and historical data from the ground up, including data cleaning, data processing, analyzing, modeling, insights delivery and execution strategy.

  • Experience in data queries and statistical programming tools (SQL, R, Python, etc.)

  • Experience with product and marketing analytics tools (Amplitude, Google Analytics, etc.)

  • You have strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a keen attention to detail.

  • You are a good communicator and can explain complex analyses using visualization and storytelling to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • You are a self-starter who thrives in a start-up environment and has a strong follow-through.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with improving data pipelines, data storage and analytical frameworks.

  • Event tracking (eg. Javascript, Google tag manager)

title: L1/L2 IT DESKSIDE & FIELD TECHNICIAN
description:
The L1/L2 IT Deskside & Field Technician provides Tier 1 routine break-fix and Tier 2 hands-on support for end-user devices, peripherals, and local hardware. This role focuses on PC deployment, IMACD (Installs, Moves, Adds, Changes, De-installations), local software/OS troubleshooting, physical hardware maintenance, and "smart hands" support for network and server room equipment under remote instruction.

Tasks

1. Deskside & End-User Support

  • Resolve desktop, laptop, printer, scanner, card reader, and VoIP desk phone hardware/software issues for local end users.
  • Image, deploy, and configure desktops and laptops using approved enterprise tools; set up standard operating systems, core applications, BIOS, disk encryption, and VPN settings.
  • Perform IMACD activities, including setting up new workstations, equipment relocations, drive wiping, and staging devices for disposal or redeployment.
  • Execute routine hardware break-fix and component replacements (RAM, drives, screens) using onsite spare parts.
  • Provide priority deskside support for VIP users as needed.

2. Smart Hands & Onsite Hardware Support

  • Perform physical "smart hands" tasks in server rooms/data centers: racking and stacking servers, switch installation, device restarts, cable patching, and disk/memory swaps.
  • Carry out physical checks on network LEDs, cabling, and Wireless Access Points (WAPs up to 3 meters height).
  • Execute basic network port and connectivity checks under remote guidance from Tier 3 infrastructure teams.

3. Ticket & Asset Management

  • Log, update, and close incident/request tickets in real-time; capture end-user sign-offs upon completion.
  • Track local inventory, manage onsite spare parts, pack RMA items, and coordinate hardware warranty repairs with OEM vendors.
  • Document common issue resolutions for the internal knowledge base.

Requirements

Required:

  • Experience: Minimum 2–3 years in IT end-user support, field service, or deskside technician roles.
  • Technical Skills:
  • Active Directory user administration (passwords, group membership) and OS imaging tools.
  • Hands-on Windows OS troubleshooting, Microsoft Office/365, and PC hardware diagnostics.
  • Basic TCP/IP network troubleshooting, Wi-Fi connectivity, and NTFS/share permissions.
  • Setup and hardware support for printers, handheld scanners, and VoIP desk phones.
  • General understanding of server hardware, switches, and patch panels for physical handling.
  • Soft Skills: Clear communication skills with the ability to explain basic technical steps to non-technical users.
  • Process: Ability to follow standard operating procedures, multitask, and manage ticketing queues effectively.

Preferred:

  • Experience working in manufacturing or factory environments.
  • Diploma or degree in Information Technology or computer hardware.
  • Entry-level certifications: CompTIA A+, ITIL Foundation, or Microsoft Desktop Support certifications.

title: Patient Flow Coordinator
description:
Founded in 1933 by Pasadena residents dedicated to women's health, PPPSGV is not only among the oldest of Planned Parenthood affiliates—we're also one of the fastest growing. Today, we see over 60,000 patient visits per year and deliver over 15,000 opportunities for sex and relationship education in our schools and colleges.

Planned Parenthood Pasadena and San Gabriel Valley (PPPSGV) is an affiliate or member of Planned Parenthood Federation of America (PPFA) – one of 67 across the country. PPPSGV provides on-the-ground reproductive health care, health education and advocacy for local people across Pasadena and the San Gabriel Valley.

PPFA is a national organization and does not provide direct medical services in local communities, but serves as a resource for policymakers, media and health care providers. PPFA does set medical standards for all Planned Parenthood affiliates in the United States and, in so doing, ensures the high quality healthcare offered by its affiliates.

The local and national organizations conduct independent fundraising campaigns, but work to coordinate these efforts.

To learn more about us, please click on the links below:

About Us | Planned Parenthood Pasadena and San Gabriel Valley, Inc.

Annual Reports | Planned Parenthood Pasadena and San Gabriel Valley, Inc.

Responsible for the daily health center patient flow. Serve as the subject matter expert in center efficiency and productivity. Develop and maintain center specific systems that meet productivity performance benchmarks, reduce patient wait times and ensure a positive patient experience. Triage waiting patients and manage daily staff and patient schedules. Delegate roles and responsibilities to center staff as needed.

As a Patient Flow Coordinator, you will save lives while you:

  • In partnership with the Center Management, develop and maintain a system for optimal center flow
  • Responsible for flow facilitation that meets productivity performance benchmarks, reduces patient wait times and encourages a positive patient experience
  • Ensure Clinicians maximize productivity by arranging patient charts to keep all rooms filled
  • Monitor and prioritize waiting patients. Ensure appropriate triage and delegate duties and responsibilities as necessary especially during heavy traffic hours
  • Monitor and minimize wait times, offering options to patients and make adjustments to services as necessary
  • Monitor and adjust daily patient and staff schedules. This includes the authority to make changes in daily staffing patterns and/or duties to assure optimum flow and patient satisfaction
  • Make decisions regarding accommodation of walk-ins, late patients, emergency appointments, etc.
  • Assist in resolving in-person patient complaints. Triage concerns, forward phone calls and complex and time-consuming complaints to the Center Management
  • Provide regular and on-going feedback to Center Management regarding flow and scheduling issues
  • Promote continuous communication between front and back office staff that creates and maintains a teamwork approach
  • Ensure daily communication with Contact Center to adjust schedules when necessary for walk-in availability and other appointment changes as needed
  • Communicate with staff if they are not keeping up with required center flow
  • Communicate and prioritize daily center assignments
  • Coordinate next-day readiness including collaborating to ensure rooms are stocked, etc.
  • Regularly monitor cancellations and no-shows in order to fill available slots
  • Facilitate translation services, referral processes and mandatory reporting as needed to manage center flow.
  • In absence of Center Management, Clinician and Patient Flow Coordinator will partner to solve urgent operational issues as they arise
  • Assist Center Management in tracking daily productivity
  • Provide input on staffing needs to Center Management
  • Assess and provide input towards training needs and ensure applicable staff is trained to provide flow facilitation as needed
  • Partner with the Clinicians and Center Management to share in operational leadership decisions to ensure the provision of high-quality client care
  • Provide Center Management feedback for staff evaluations

Non-Essential Functions:

  • As a mandated reporter, proactively communicate and identify risks to supervisor or appropriate agency in order to minimize risk when possible
  • Comply with PPPSGVs Code of Conduct and maintain the highest level of professional and ethical standards and act in compliance with both the letter and spirit of all applicable laws and regulations
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned

We are looking for the following:

Education:
  • High School level education and above are welcomed to apply
Experience:
  • Two years’ experience in a health, medical or social service setting or one year demonstrated supervisory experience
  • Planned Parenthood or family planning experience preferred
Other:
  • Make changes in staffing patterns and duties and to utilize resources effectively
  • Create and maintain a team work approach to center flow and morale
  • Maintain composure under stress
  • Establish rapport with all clients
  • Take initiative and utilize resources effectively
  • Multi-task and be detailed orientated
  • Maintain relevant knowledge about anatomy and physiology, methods of contraception, STDs, pregnancy, adoption, abortion, early prenatal care, community resources, Agency protocols and referral procedures and all Planned Parenthood programs
  • Perform venipuncture and give injections
  • Work independently and as part of a team
  • Understand insurance and FPACT contract guidelines
  • Work schedule requires some Saturdays and/or evening hours
  • Work and travel to other centers as needed, based on health center patient demand
  • Communicate effectively with clients and co-workers of all backgrounds
  • Excellent computer skills with knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and the Internet
  • Adapt to change including advances in technology
  • Commitment to and support for the mission and goals of Planned Parenthood, including but not limited to, increasing access to abortion and decreasing abortion stigma
  • Commitment to quality healthcare
  • Excellent customer service and commitment to providing the highest level of customer satisfaction
  • Commitment to personal and/or organizational Diversity, Equity and Inclusion work, including the proficiency and/or strong willingness to use non-binary pronouns

PPPSGV is committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace. We offer a series of workshops during employee onboarding and throughout the year. We also provide additional opportunities to get involved in our diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) work through various task forces, conferences, and staff retreats.

We are a prominent team of passionate health experts who adhere to the highest standards as we collaborate and care for people without judgment. As we stand in solidarity with communities of color, we demand greater diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) within our organization.

Join our team and be part of a powerful movement to shape the future of sexual and reproductive health!

title: Assistive Technology Professional (ATP)
description:
At Mobius Mobility, we're not just building technology, we're redefining what freedom can look like. Our mission is to empower individuals with mobility challenges to access more of their world with confidence and independence. The ibot® Personal Mobility Device (PMD) is our breakthrough solution: a single, versatile device that eliminates the need to have multiple mobility aids. With six unique modes — including stair‑climbing, 4‑wheel, and balance mode — the ibot® enables users to move beyond the limits of ADA standards and experience a new level of freedom and confidence in their daily lives.

We are seeking a dedicated, mission‑driven Assistive Technology Professional (ATP) to join our team as we build our outreach and presence across the country. In this role, you'll build relationships with clinicians and support clients through the evaluation, delivery and comprehensive training process on the ibot® PMD. You'll be a key ambassador for the Mobius Mobility brand, bridging users and clinicians with engineers and technicians, advancing innovation in mobility.

This is an on-site role based at our office in Manchester, NH. Travel will be primarily be focused on supporting clients in the New England region.

Key Responsibilities
Client and Clinical Support
  • Partner with clinicians to evaluate client needs and recommend appropriate ibot® configurations
  • Conduct Complex Rehab Technology assessments and home environment evaluations
  • Deliver devices, ensure proper equipment fit, and provide hands‑on user training
  • Demonstrate product operation and ensure safe, effective use of the ibot® PMD
Territory Growth & Relationship Building
  • Develop and maintain strong referral relationships with clinicians, rehab facilities, and community partners
  • Identify new opportunities to expand awareness and adoption of the ibot® PMD
  • Conduct in‑services, product demonstrations, and educational sessions
Operational Excellence
  • Review seating specifications and orders for accuracy
  • Collaborate with operations and service teams to ensure smooth configuration, delivery, and follow‑through
  • Assist with insurance documentation and processes as needed
  • Attend trade shows, conferences, and industry events
  • Uphold RESNA's Code of Ethics and all company policies
Qualifications
Required:
  • Bachelor's Degree in a related field
  • Current ATP Certification (RESNA) or scheduled to take the test
  • Hands-on experience working with individuals with disabilities
  • Valid driver license
Preferred:
  • Bachelor's degree in health sciences, Occupational Therapy or Physical Therapy
  • 1–3 years of experience as an ATP or therapist in rehab technology, a rehab facility, clinic, DME environment, or other applicable environments
  • Experience with CRMs (Atlas, Salesforce or HubSpot)
Physical Requirements
  • Ability to physically train new users for basic ibot® operation and ibot® stair climbing
  • Ability to use standard office equipment and computer systems
  • Ability to lift items up to 30 lbs.
  • Ability to travel as needed domestically by car and plane
Benefits:
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Company-subsidized medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Life and disability insurance
  • Paid time off, including paid vacation, sick leave and holidays

title: Broadcast Engineer
description:
New Hampshire Public Radio (NHPR) is seeking a Studio Broadcast Engineer to join our Engineering Team. This hands-on position will provide daily technical support for NHPR's studios, control rooms, broadcast systems and staff end users. The engineer will troubleshoot on-air and studio issues, support computers and audio workstations, perform routine maintenance, assist with installations and upgrades and help keep our broadcast facilities reliable and ready for air.

This position will also assist with NHPR's 14 transmitter and translator sites across New Hampshire, including routine maintenance, troubleshooting, equipment installations, and field work as needed. The ideal candidate is dependable, technically curious, service-oriented, and comfortable working directly with staff in a fast-paced broadcast environment. Occasional evening, weekend, emergency, and statewide travel will be required. This IT/IP-driven role requires a strong knowledge of Windows OS and the aptitude to manage and troubleshoot various broadcast and software systems. Living within a 45-minute commute radius of Concord is optimal.

This is a full-time, exempt, on-site role based in Concord, NH, reporting to the Senior Engineer. The starting salary range for this position is $72,000-$83,000, based on experience. We also consider internal equity, among other factors, when deciding compensation.

Essential Duties Include:

  • Support operation and maintenance of RF transmission systems, studio equipment, and IP-based distribution.
  • Assist with preventative maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair at transmission and studio facilities.
  • Provide first-response technical support for on-air and studio issues.
  • Collaborate with content and digital teams to support smooth broadcast operations.
  • Participate in an on-call rotation to respond to after-hours issues. Ability to travel to the NHPR facility for emergency issues in a timely manner.

Other Duties Include:

  • Participate in remote broadcast setup and execution across multiple locations.
  • Learn and assist with regulatory record-keeping and FCC compliance.
  • Support transmission systems (power, HVAC, security) under direction of the Senior Engineer.
  • Maintain equipment documentation and inventory records.



Qualifications:

  • 1–3 years of broadcast engineering experience, or 2–5 years equivalent technical experience.
  • Higher education in broadcast technology, electronics, or a related field is highly valued.
  • Understanding of signal flow and audio chains.
  • Familiarity with IP networking (basic routing, subnets, DHCP, device configuration).
  • Exposure to broadcast equipment such as Comrex, Tieline, Wheatstone, Axia Livewire, Telos, Nautel, or Barix is a plus.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively across teams.
  • Valid NH driver's license and ability to safely drive in all conditions.
  • Flexibility to work within a 24/7/365 operation.
  • Strong interpersonal skills; openness to mentorship and skill development.

However, we know there are great candidates who may not have all these qualities or who have important skills we may not have outlined above. If this is you, do not hesitate to apply and tell us about yourself

Compensation & Benefits:

This is a full time, exempt position and the salary range for this role is $72,000 to $83,000 annually.

NHPR offers a generous benefits package that includes health and dental insurance; company-paid short and long-term disability; flexible spending accounts; 403(b) savings plan with a company match; and a free on-site fitness center. Employees are entitled to three weeks of vacation time and 14 paid holidays, as well as paid sick and parental leave.

Things to Know About Us:

NHPR is the state's foremost news organization, focused on producing accountability journalism and engaging deeply with the diverse communities and people of the Granite State. For 40 years, NHPR has produced incisive local news on the radio and emerging audio platforms, complementing the national and global reporting of our partners at NPR. NHPR is the winner of multiple National Edward R. Murrow Awards for overall excellence from 2015 through 2023 and a finalist for the 2024 Pulitzer in Audio Journalism. We make nationally prominent podcasts - including Bear Brook, Outside/In, Civics 101 and Document - and have a fast-growing footprint in digital and social media. We have over 23,000 member households, over 60% of which are sustaining members.

We seek people who are approachable, collaborative, empathetic, optimistic, and solution-minded. Together, we are building a culture based on earned trust, transparency, equity and inclusion. We hold ourselves accountable to our goals and our values. NHPR is intent on being public radio for all of New Hampshire, and to expanding our audience and advancing our mission and vision by deepening our engagement with diverse people and communities across the state and beyond our borders.

Please apply on the job opportunities page of our website, NHPR.org, or through this link: https://nhpr.applicantpro.com/jobs

title: Technical Program Manager II
description:
Overview

The IP Group (IPG) is seeking a Technical Program Manager to support the execution, coordination, and operational readiness of business-critical technology initiatives across engineering, security, compliance, operations, and business teams.

In this role, you will work closely with senior technical, program, and business leaders to translate established priorities into actionable plans and help coordinate activities across multiple technical workstreams. You will support program planning and tracking, security and compliance activities, operational readiness, release coordination, vendor engagement, documentation, risk and dependency management, and stakeholder communication.

This position is well suited for an organized and technically capable program manager who enjoys working across teams, bringing structure to complex initiatives, and helping technical and business stakeholders move work forward. You will provide the coordination, visibility, and follow-through needed to support reliable technology operations and successful delivery of approved initiatives.

The role is focused on execution and operational support rather than ownership of portfolio strategy or long-term program direction. You will partner with senior leaders and technical owners to help ensure priorities are effectively coordinated, risks and dependencies remain visible, and technical, operational, security, and compliance commitments progress toward completion.



Responsibilities

As a Technical Program Manager supporting IPG Technical Operations, you will provide program management, coordination, and execution support for business-critical technology initiatives across engineering, security, compliance, operations, and business teams.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Support the execution of technical programs and initiatives by helping translate established priorities into actionable plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, and measurable outcomes.
  • Coordinate activities across engineering, business operations, security, compliance, and other technical stakeholders to help programs progress from requirements through implementation, testing, release, and operational handoff.
  • Maintain project plans, schedules, backlogs, risks, dependencies, decisions, and delivery status, identifying potential issues and coordinating with appropriate owners on resolution or escalation.
  • Support the operational health and readiness of IPG applications, platforms, and technical services by coordinating deployments, releases, service improvements, incident follow-up, and remediation activities.
  • Assist technical and program owners with execution of security, privacy, risk, and compliance requirements, including vulnerability remediation, technical assessments, audit and compliance actions, SFI/S360 commitments, threat-model reviews, penetration-testing follow-up, and related evidence and reporting.
  • Facilitate requirements definition, backlog refinement, sprint planning, user acceptance testing, production-readiness reviews, releases, and operational transitions in partnership with engineering and business stakeholders.
  • Track technical debt, security findings, operational improvements, compliance obligations, and other commitments, providing visibility to owners and stakeholders and supporting timely completion.
  • Coordinate activities performed by vendors, contractors, and external delivery partners, including deliverables, schedules, dependencies, access requirements, knowledge transfer, and operational readiness.
  • Develop and maintain program documentation, operational procedures, runbooks, decision records, and knowledge repositories that support service continuity and effective technology operations.
  • Support established communication and operating rhythms by preparing status reporting, risk and dependency assessments, executive summaries, meeting materials, and decision-support information.
  • Identify opportunities to improve execution, operational processes, documentation, automation, and service readiness, and work with appropriate owners to evaluate and implement improvements.
  • Partner with senior technical, program, and business leaders to support execution of approved priorities with appropriate visibility, coordination, accountability, and follow-through.


Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 2+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development OR equivalent experience.
  • 1+ year(s) of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 5+ years experience engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development OR equivalent experience.
  • 4+ years of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.
  • 1+ year(s) of experience reading and/or writing code (e.g., sample documentation, product demos).
  • Experience supporting enterprise applications, cloud services, operational platforms, or other business-critical technology environments.
  • Experience working with Agile, Scrum, Kanban, or similar modern technology delivery methodologies.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft cloud and enterprise technologies such as Azure, Power Platform, SharePoint, Power BI, or related services.
  • Experience supporting security, compliance, privacy, audit, vulnerability remediation, or technology risk-management initiatives.
  • Familiarity with work-management and engineering tools such as Azure DevOps, Jira, Planner, or similar platforms.
  • Experience coordinating vendors, contractors, consulting partners, or distributed technical delivery teams.
  • Experience supporting technology environments involving operational readiness, releases, service transitions, incident follow-up, or technical remediation activities.
  • Familiarity with legal, intellectual property, licensing, or other regulated or compliance-focused business environments is a plus.

To be considered for this role, candidates must reside within approximately 45 minutes of our Northern California offices in San Rafael or Emeryville. This role is Hybrid with an expectation to be in-office 1 to 2 days a week on average with travel to our San Diego office 1 to 2 times per year.

In this role, you will be responsible for:

Service Desk

  • Own the intake, triage, management and resolution of employee support requests.

  • Maintain ticket hygiene throughout the lifecycle of all requests.

  • Troubleshoot Windows endpoints, mobile devices, file collaboration platforms, printing and Microsoft 365 (including SharePoint, OneDrive, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc)

  • Provide general break/fix services for WRA-issued assets.

  • Provide on-site support in our offices as required, including (but not limited to) hardware swaps, replacing peripherals, supporting conference room equipment and providing AV support for quarterly on-site meetings.

  • Engage with our specialized teams who may report connectivity or performance issues.

  • Participate in on-call rotation for critical but rare IT outages and other emergent duties.

Identity & Access Management

  • Own employee onboarding and offboarding end to end, including account creation, group memberships, device deployment, license management, etc, so that new employees are ready on day one and departing employees are properly decommissioned.

  • Administer basic IAM functions, including creating and managing Guest accounts, MFA recoveries, change of group memberships, etc.

  • Assist the Director with the administration of security awareness training programs, including follow-ups and remediation assignments.

Asset Management

  • Maintain asset inventory including general inventory management, loaner pools, peripherals, and e-waste.

  • Continuously ensure WRA-issued devices are compliant with our hardware lifecycle and warranty policies; coordinating and planning hardware upgrades with minimal disruption to our employees.

Documentation & Ongoing Improvement

  • Help identify areas of improvement in our processes which you are responsible for executing.

  • Participate in performing root-cause analyses (RCA) of system issues.

  • Author knowledge base articles designed to enable employee self-service.

  • Assist in documenting services that you provide. Documentation must be considered a deliverable – not a “nice to have.”

To be successful in this role, you will need:

Experience & Location

  • 3 to 5 years of direct experience supporting a hybrid or remote workforce of at least 50 employees, with at least 2 years performing Tier 2 duties.

  • Be able to demonstrate a history of performing duties in a high-trust role.

  • Be local to the Bay Area and be able to be on-site at our San Rafael, Emeryville and Petaluma offices.

Technical Skillset

  • Understand endpoint administration with Microsoft Intune or a comparable MDM platform, supporting Windows devices and mobile devices.

  • Be competent in core networking principles, including DNS, DHCP, VPN connectivity, and Wi-Fi connectivity, with the ability to isolate connectivity issues utilizing these concepts.

  • General understanding of cloud-hosted virtual desktops and ability to pinpoint performance and connectivity issues.

  • Must understand when it’s appropriate to escalate an issue and when to ask for help.

    • How You Work

    • Ability to operate independently where appropriate as part of a lean team.

    • A zero-trust security mindset and demonstrate that through the methods you provide IT service.

    • Strong customer service skills and the ability to translate complex technical issues into plain language that anyone can understand.

    Physical Requirements

    • Able to perform physical duties, that may include lifting up to 50 lbs, climbing ladders indoors, crawling under furniture and reaching behind wall-mounted equipment.

    Bonus Points for

    • Familiarity with industry standard frameworks, such as CMMC L1/L2, NIST SP 800-171, CCPA, SOC 2, ITSM, or ITIL.

    • Holding industry-standard certifications, including ITIL Foundation, CompTIA A+, Network+, Security+ or any relevant Microsoft certifications.

    • Experience administering Unifi Network and Protect.

    • Supporting CAD and GIS applications, such as AutoCAD, Civil3D, ArcGIS or spatial datasets.

    • Supporting markup tools, including Bluebeam and Adobe Acrobat.

    • Experience supporting Egnyte, VantagePoint or Elevia.

WRA has an established internal leveling system for our staff that maps to salary bands that have been informed by market data. Our leveling system is dependent on years of relevant industry experience, education, and the level of responsibility and autonomy at which you’re expected to operate.

We have posted a salary range that corresponds to the appropriate level for this position. In your first conversation with our recruiter, we will discuss leveling and compensation with you to make sure that our expectations are aligned.

*The salary range for this position is $70,000-$80,000.

Who are we?

WRA’s an employee-owned environmental consultancy. We are a tenacious team of planners, engineers, and scientists, and we aim to leave the lands we love better than we found them.

Our clients and partners hire us because we’re skilled at navigating through challenging projects involving wildlands, parks, community spaces, and infrastructure. As an organization, we believe that independence and interdependence are not mutually exclusive. We invest in systems, processes, and employee programs to support our staff’s collective engagement and success. At the same time, we encourage our employees to operate with an ownership mindset, taking responsibility for outcomes and being true to our commitments.

WRA’s company vision is to cultivate a sustainable future where people and the environment thrive, and that effort starts first with our staff. We are committed to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive work environment, and we have developed flexible policies, internal practices, and are investing in programs that prioritize learning and sustainability. We aim to create conditions that allow employees to prioritize their families, lead healthy and balanced lives, and to bring their authentic selves to work every day. We believe that by creating an exceptional workplace, our employees will be able to do their best work and be able to meaningfully contribute to the sustainability of the environment and the communities in which we live.

title: System Administrator
description:
Overview

Position Title: Lead System Administrator

Location: Aberdeen, MD

Reports To: Deputy Program Manager

Job Type & Status: Full-time; Onsite 5 days per week

Clearance Requirement: Active TS/SCI clearance

Summary:

We are seeking a Systems Administrator to manage, maintain, secure, and troubleshoot Linux-based infrastructure in a DOW (Department of War) environment. The ideal candidate will have strong hands-on experience with Red Hat Enterprise Linux and related distributions, system administration, automation, networking, virtualization, and security.

The Linux Systems Administrator will be responsible for maintaining system availability, deploying and configuring Linux servers, implementing system hardening and security controls, troubleshooting complex infrastructure issues, and automating repetitive administrative tasks.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Team lead duties managing a team of 2-3 cyber security and system administrators in direct support of customer efforts.
  • Customer service and support including engagement and interface with customers
  • Install, configure, maintain, and troubleshoot Linux servers, primarily RHEL/Rocky Linux environments.
  • Install, configure, maintain, and troubleshoot Microsoft (MS) Windows, MS Active Directory, and associated MS technologies.
  • Perform system administration tasks including user and group management, permissions, storage, filesystems, services, processes, networking, and system performance.
  • Deploy and maintain physical and virtual Linux systems in enterprise environments.
  • Configure and troubleshoot network services including DNS, DHCP, SSH, HTTP/HTTPS, NTP, and TCP/IP networking.
  • Manage system updates, patches, repositories, packages, and software deployments using tools such as DNF/YUM/RPM.
  • Develop and maintain automated provisioning and deployment solutions using technologies such as Kickstart, PXE, Cobbler, and Ansible.
  • Develop and maintain Ansible playbooks and automation scripts to standardize system configuration and deployment.
  • Implement Linux security hardening in accordance with organizational security requirements and applicable security standards.
  • Configure and manage SELinux, firewalld, SSH, sudo, system permissions, and authentication mechanisms.
  • Monitor system health, performance, availability, and resource utilization.
  • Troubleshoot hardware, operating system, application, networking, and configuration issues.
  • Manage system logs and troubleshoot services using tools such as systemd, journalctl, and log management platforms.
  • Support containerized workloads using technologies such as Podman and Docker.
  • Develop scripts and automation using Bash and Python to improve operational efficiency.
  • Perform system backups, recovery procedures, and disaster-recovery activities.
  • Maintain system documentation, configuration baselines, procedures, and technical diagrams.
  • Participate in incident response, root-cause analysis, and remediation of infrastructure issues.
  • Collaborate with network, cybersecurity, software development, and systems engineering teams.
  • Support infrastructure migrations, upgrades, and new system deployments.
  • Provide technical support for production and development environments as required.

Qualifications

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • 6+ total years of experience with 3+ years working on Linux Systems and 3+ years of experience working on Windows systems.

Skills:

  • Strong experience administering RHEL or RHEL-compatible Linux distributions.
  • Strong understanding of Linux system architecture, networking, storage, and security.
  • Experience with Ansible and infrastructure automation.
  • Experience with Bash scripting and/or Python.
  • Experience troubleshooting Linux systems from the command line.
  • Experience with systemd, SSH, cron, package management, filesystem management, and Linux networking.
  • Understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, routing, and firewall concepts.
  • Experience with virtualization technologies such as VMware, VirtualBox, or similar platforms.
  • Experience with Git and configuration/version-control practices.
  • Ability to troubleshoot complex technical issues independently.
  • Management and leadership experience is a highly desirable
  • Must have experience with DOD Risk Management Framework.

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to travel between 10-25% to customer location or Aberdeen Proving Ground

Why Join Us?

  • Impactful Work: Contribute to critical national security initiatives and make a real difference in protecting our nation.
  • Cutting-Edge Technology: Work with the latest advancements in SIGINT and related fields.
  • Career Growth: Opportunities for professional development, training, and advancement within a growing company.
  • Collaborative Environment: Join a team of highly skilled and supportive engineers who are passionate about their work.
  • Comprehensive Benefits: Competitive salary, generous PTO, health/dental/vision insurance, 401K matching, tuition reimbursement.

Compensation and Benefits:

  • Competitive Pay: Annual salary ranges from $135,000 to $175,000. Salaries depend on labor category, years of experience, education, skills relevant to the position, and type of contract.
  • Benefits: Including Paid Time Off; 401K Contribution and Employer Match Contributions; and Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage.

title: Mechanical Estimator
description:
About the Company

Our client is the largest design-build mechanical contractor in the Sacramento area, providing comprehensive HVAC, plumbing, and piping services to commercial and industrial facilities throughout Northern California.

With expertise in both design-build and traditional plan-and-spec delivery methods, the company offers employees the opportunity to work on diverse, technically challenging projects while contributing to a growing organization with a strong regional presence.

About the Position

Our client is seeking an experienced Senior Mechanical Estimator to lead the development of accurate, competitive estimates and proposals for commercial and industrial mechanical construction projects.

This individual will be responsible for assembling all aspects of estimates for both prime contract and subcontract bids, utilizing design-build and plan-and-spec delivery methods. The ideal candidate will have strong technical estimating capabilities, a thorough understanding of mechanical construction, and the ability to collaborate effectively with internal teams, general contractors, and subcontractors.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Prepare comprehensive estimates and develop final proposals for prime contract and subcontract opportunities.
  • Analyze construction drawings, specifications, and project manuals to determine material, labor, subcontractor, and general conditions costs.
  • Develop accurate estimates using traditional plan-and-spec delivery methods.
  • Conceptualize project scopes and establish cost estimates for design-build opportunities.
  • Review site visit videos, preliminary sketches, and project information to establish project scope and pricing.
  • Collaborate with internal engineering teams to develop design-build estimates and budgets.
  • Evaluate subcontractor scopes and coordinate pricing to ensure complete and accurate proposals.
  • Maintain current knowledge of labor rates, material costs, and market conditions.
  • Communicate professionally and effectively with Project Managers, subcontractors, and General Contractors throughout the estimating process.
  • Ensure all estimates and proposals are prepared with accuracy, integrity, and attention to detail.

Requirements

  • 5–10 years of relevant estimating experience in mechanical construction, supported by applicable technical training.
  • Strong understanding of mechanical construction, including HVAC, plumbing, and piping systems.
  • Knowledge of current labor rates, material costs, and construction pricing.
  • Experience preparing estimates for both design-build and plan-and-spec projects.
  • Ability to interpret construction drawings, technical specifications, and project manuals.
  • Understanding of conceptual estimating, budgeting, and scope development.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office applications.
  • Experience with QuickPen estimating software is preferred.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with internal teams, subcontractors, and general contractors.

Benefits

  • Competitive base salary of $130,000–$160,000, depending on experience.
  • Opportunity to join a leading mechanical contractor in the Sacramento market.
  • Exposure to diverse commercial and industrial projects throughout Northern California.
  • Opportunity to contribute to both design-build and traditional mechanical construction projects

title: Lead Electricians
description:
Pay Rate: $27.00 - $42.00

About RANDALL

RANDALL is a premier self-performing $100M+ subcontractor providing integrated Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing, Fire Protection, Architectural Metals, and Offsite Construction/Manufacturing solutions across Florida and the Southeast. With 35+ years of operational excellence and a team of 500+ professionals, we combine the grit and dedication of our grassroots origins with the innovation of a modern industry leader. Our 100,000 sq. ft. fabrication facility in Apopka, FL serves as a strategic logistics hub, supporting major commercial, industrial, and aeronautical projects across the Southeast and beyond.


RANDALL Construction's Electrical Division is seeking experienced, driven, and safety-focused Lead Electricians to join our growing team on projects throughout Orlando and Central Florida. The ideal candidate is a skilled commercial electrical professional with proven field leadership experience, a strong commitment to safety and quality, and the ability to effectively lead crews while maintaining project schedules and customer satisfaction.


Position Summary:

The Lead Electrician is responsible for planning, coordinating, and overseeing daily electrical installation activities in the field while actively performing electrical work. This individual serves as a working leader who provides direction to Journeyman Electricians and Apprentices, ensures adherence to project schedules, maintains high-quality workmanship, and promotes a culture of safety, accountability, and teamwork.


Essential Functions:

  • · Lead and coordinate daily activities of electrical crews on commercial construction projects.
    · Plan work assignments and ensure labor, materials, tools, and equipment are utilized efficiently.
    · Install, maintain, and repair commercial electrical systems in accordance with the National Electrical Code (NEC), local codes, and project specifications.
    · Read and interpret blueprints, one-line diagrams, electrical schematics, specifications, and construction documents.
    · Install conduit systems including EMT, Rigid, PVC, MC Cable, and associated raceway systems.
    · Install, terminate, and troubleshoot electrical equipment including switchgear, panels, transformers, lighting systems, controls, and power distribution equipment.
    · Perform electrical testing, commissioning, troubleshooting, and startup activities.
    · Coordinate work activities with Project Managers, Foremen, Superintendents, inspectors, vendors, subcontractors, and other trades.
    · Monitor project progress and proactively identify scheduling conflicts, material shortages, or field issues.
    · Ensure all installations meet RANDALL quality standards and project specifications.
    · Mentor and train Journeyman Electricians and Apprentices on proper installation techniques, productivity expectations, and safe work practices.
    · Conduct daily safety meetings and enforce OSHA and company safety requirements.
    · Utilize company technology to document field progress, complete reports, track productivity, and communicate project updates.
    · Maintain clean, organized, and safe job sites.
    · Represent RANDALL professionally with customers, inspectors, owners, contractors, and team members.
    · Promote a positive team culture focused on excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Desired Qualification Requirements and Attributes:

  • · Journeyman Electrician License (where required) or equivalent verifiable experience.
    · Minimum of 7+ years of commercial electrical experience, including demonstrated leadership or crew supervision experience.
    · Proven ability to lead field personnel, coordinate workflow, and maintain project productivity.
    · Thorough knowledge of the National Electrical Code (NEC) and applicable local building codes.
    · Strong understanding of commercial electrical construction methods, means, and best practices.
    · Ability to read and interpret blueprints, electrical drawings, specifications, one-line diagrams, and electrical schematics.
    · Experience coordinating manpower, scheduling work activities, and managing field productivity.
    · Proficient with tablets, smartphones, and construction management software for reporting, documentation, and communication.
    · Strong troubleshooting, critical thinking, and problem-solving abilities.
    · Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

    · Ability to pass all required pre-employment screenings, including background check and drug screening.
    · OSHA 30 Certification preferred.

    · Experience working on healthcare, education, multifamily, hospitality, industrial, aviation, or large commercial construction projects.
    · Experience operating aerial lifts, forklifts, and other construction equipment.
    · Demonstrated ability to mentor and develop team members.
    · Strong organizational, leadership, and time-management skills.
    · High level of integrity, professionalism, and accountability.
    · Customer-focused mindset with a commitment to delivering exceptional project results.

Physical Requirements:

This is primarily a Shop or Field Jobsite job. You must be able to lift a dead weight of at least 50 pounds and stand on your feet for several hours at a time. You must also be able to bend, stretch, crouch, and lift as required by the job, be able to respond quickly to sounds, see and respond to dangerous situations, and properly wear personal protective gear.

Our selection will be driven by the qualifications above as well as the ability to develop relationships with clients and co-workers to maximize your professional opportunities.



Benefits

Why Join the RANDALL Team? Success at RANDALL is driven by our culture of Professional Trade Excellence: pairing technical mastery with a practical, hardworking mindset. We seek professionals who are motivated by challenge and the opportunity to build lasting relationships with our clients and our colleagues. We don't just hire for the next project; we invest in long-term careers built on a foundation of quality and craftsmanship.
