title: Software Engineer, Consumer Shopping Quality, Commerce, Recommendations, Rankings, Predictions
description:
Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

Our team sits at the intersection of advanced AI agents and next-generation commerce at Google.

We focus on three core pillars:

  • Subagent Orchestration and framework: Building platforms where specialized agents are spawned and coordinated to handle complex commerce intents at scale.
  • Visual Shopping: Pushing AI search boundaries to create seamless visual and text experiences. We bridge the gap between deep infrastructure and rapid consumer product iterations. Teams are focusing on product experience both on AIM and AIO.
  • Agentic Exploration: Pioneering self-optimizing systems. We want our systems to dynamically allocate resources and learn from their own execution trajectories to continuously improve.

People shop on Google more than a billion times a day - and the Commerce team is responsible for building the experiences that serve these users. The mission for Google Commerce is to be an essential part of the shopping journey for consumers - from inspiration to to a simple and secure checkout experience - and the best place for retailers/merchants to connect with consumers. We support and partner with the commerce ecosystem, from large retailers to small local merchants, to give them the tools, technology and scale to thrive in today’s digital world.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $147000 - $210000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

title: Lead Production Director (One Church)
description:
SUMMARY

This position serves on the One Church Worship team and provides leadership and direction for Production Ministry across all Pinelake campuses. The Lead Production Director is responsible for developing a clear and unified philosophy for live production, leading and developing Production staff, and building systems and structures that help our teams thrive.

This role will lead the One Church Production team, work closely with Campus Production Directors, and provide oversight for production across weekend services, One Church events, and other ministry initiatives. The goal is to build a healthy, unified, and multiplying Production Ministry that is marked by discipleship and development culture. Where staff and servant leaders are equipped to lead, campuses are well supported, and everything we do serves the mission and vision of Pinelake.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

Learn

  • Pursue a growing relationship with Jesus through consistent time in God’s Word and prayer
  • Continually grow in your understanding of the Jesus-Centered Life (salvation, identity, life, and authority in Christ).
  • Remain teachable and hungry, seeking feedback, learning from others, and developing both spiritually and professionally.
  • Cultivate awareness of God’s presence in everyday life, listening to the Holy Spirit and responding in obedience.

Live

  • Practice and model the rhythms of Be the Church (Grow, Pray, Connect, and Share).
  • Pursue emotional health by engaging in self-awareness, addressing past wounds, and cultivating honest, healthy relationships.
  • Practice healthy rhythms, prioritizing your relationship with Jesus and your family
  • Embody a life of integrity and surrender, allowing your private life with God to shape your work.

Lead

  • Take ownership of disciple-making by supporting and strengthening environments where people can take their next step toward a Jesus-Centered Life.
  • Leverage your role, systems, and responsibilities to remove barriers and create clarity, helping both staff and the church move forward in the Discipleship Pathway (Essentials → JCL → Be the Church).
  • Contribute to life-change by bringing your skills, organization, and follow-through to your work, knowing that what you build and manage helps others lead and shepherd more effectively.
  • Build people through your influence—encouraging, supporting, and serving teammates and Servant Leaders in ways that help them grow and thrive.
  • Measure success not only by task completion, but by how your work contributes to disciples being formed and multiplied across the church.

Embrace the Culture

  • Value and embody the staff values, which we call the 7 H’s: Humility, Honor, Honesty, Hunger, Holy Spirit, Health, and Harmony
  • Communicate clearly, honestly, and proactively in a way that builds trust, unity, and momentum.
  • Work in alignment with the church vision and leadership
  • Participate fully in the life of your campus or team, contributing to the unity, health, and shepherding of the faith family.

    SPECIFIC LIST OF DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

    • Develop and lead a clear, unified philosophy for live production across all Pinelake campuses, establishing expectations for quality, preparation, execution, and team culture.
    • Provide leadership, coaching, and development for the One Church Production Director and additional Production staff as the team grows.
    • Work closely with Campus Production Directors to provide support, strengthen leadership, and ensure alignment across campuses.
    • Model our value of discipleship with staff and servant leaders in the context of Production ministry.
    • Lead strategies for a systematic approach to recruiting, onboarding, discipling, and developing Production staff and servant leaders.
    • Develop and oversee consistent systems, standard operating procedures, training resources, and best practices that support healthy and sustainable Production Ministry.
    • Provide oversight for weekend production across all campuses, regularly evaluating effectiveness, identifying needs, and helping teams implement solutions.
    • Establish healthy rhythms of communication, collaboration, and accountability between One Church Production and campus teams.
    • Provide overall leadership for production at One Church events, empowering the One Church Production Director to manage planning, staffing, preparation, and execution.
    • Partner with the Director of Worship Technology to identify equipment needs, prioritize improvements, and plan for future growth.
    • Other duties as assigned

      SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

      Supervises One Church Production team, with monitoring and coaching of the Campus Production Directors.

      QUALIFICATIONS

      To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

      EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIRED

      • Bachelors Degree is preferred
      • 10 Years of Production Leadership in a Multi-site Church setting


      LANGUAGE SKILLS

      The individual must be able to understand written or oral instructions; read, analyze and interpret documents, instructions manuals, and policies and procedures. Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work with a diverse group of people, communicate clearly and effectively on the telephone, email and in person, demonstrating tact and diplomacy.

      COMPUTER AND MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

      The individual must have demonstrated skill in the use of Windows/MacOS to complete tasks (including word processing and spreadsheets) and the ability to use the internet for information retrieval. The individual must be able to apply basic mathematical concepts and operations to such tasks as accounting, budget management, and financial expense monitoring.

      REASONING ABILITY

      The ability to simultaneously conceptualize and plan multiple tasks; project outcomes using different implementation strategies; and apply creative and innovative thinking to problem situations is required. The ability to work effectively and efficiently under stressful conditions to ensure deadlines are met is essential.

title: Project Manager 1
description:
Project Manager

Hyperscale Data Center Program

At Network Connex, you can experience meaningful career growth while delivering complex infrastructure projects with an experienced team. We offer competitive compensation, benefits, and opportunities to build your skills and take ownership of your work. Our people excel in fast-paced environments, adapt to change, and take the initiative to solve problems within and beyond their roles.

This Opportunity:

The Project Manager is responsible for day-to-day delivery of assigned structured cabling projects within a hyperscale data center program, from planning and mobilization through customer acceptance and closeout. The PM owns project schedules, cost forecasts, change management, customer reporting, and coordination with field leadership, Procurement, subcontractors, and QA/QC.

Reporting to a Senior Project Manager or Program Manager, the PM works independently within established program standards and delegated authority to deliver safe, high-quality installation services that meet contractual scope, budget, and milestone commitments. The PM proactively resolves execution issues and escalates risks requiring program-level decisions or support.

Job Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Promote and follow the Company's Safety program and customer site policies. Partner with field leadership to address unsafe conditions and ensure schedule or cost pressures do not compromise safe execution.

  • Uphold Company Core Values and policies, and establish clear expectations for accountability, collaboration, and professional conduct.

  • Plan and manage assigned projects, including scope review, execution planning, mobilization, resource coordination, installation, testing, customer acceptance, and closeout.

  • Direct assigned Field Engineers and Project Coordinators, establish priorities, delegate tasks, and track completion. Coordinate field execution with Field Supervisors and Project Superintendents.

  • Develop and maintain project schedules, milestone plans, and short-term look-ahead schedules. Coordinate dependencies such as site readiness, customer access, preceding work by other trades, materials, equipment, and workforce availability.

  • Monitor daily production and labor productivity with field leadership. Identify deviations from planned performance and lead corrective actions and recovery planning when schedule or budget commitments are at risk.

  • Own the preparation and accuracy of monthly job cost forecasts, cost-to-complete estimates, progress billings, and supporting financial documentation. Review variances with program leadership and act within established approval limits.

  • Partner with Procurement and Field Operations to track material and equipment requirements, lead times, deliveries, and workforce needs against the project schedule.

  • Maintain accurate and current project records, including RFIs, submittals, change requests, decisions, risks, issues, and action items.

  • Identify and document changes to scope or execution conditions promptly. Prepare complete change request estimates, scope narratives, schedule impacts, and supporting documentation; obtain required approvals before implementing changes in accordance with contract and program procedures.

  • Manage subcontractor and vendor performance against agreed scope, schedule, quality, and documentation requirements. Escalate performance issues and coordinate corrective actions.

  • Serve as the day-to-day customer contact for assigned projects. Lead project status meetings and provide timely, accurate reporting on progress, milestones, financial status as appropriate, risks, decisions, and required actions.

  • Escalate risks affecting safety, quality, cost, or committed milestones promptly, with a clear assessment of impacts, recommended actions, and decisions or support needed.

  • Review project deliverables prepared by assigned team members for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with contract and customer requirements before submission.

  • Partner with QA/QC and field leadership to implement project quality requirements, including installation inspections, cable labeling, testing, test-result documentation, and resolution of deficiencies.

  • Manage punch lists, as-built documentation, turnover packages, and other required closeout deliverables. Coordinate customer acceptance and obtain documented signoff against agreed acceptance criteria.

  • Support contract and change order negotiations with technical, schedule, and cost information, within delegated authority.

  • Capture lessons learned and implement practical improvements to project execution and reporting.

Skills Abilities and Competencies:

  • Ability to independently manage day-to-day project delivery, prioritize competing demands, and recognize when escalation or approval is required.

  • Working knowledge of construction safety practices and the ability to apply Company and customer site requirements in coordination with field leadership.

  • Understanding of structured cabling systems, including fiber and copper installation, labeling, testing, and acceptance documentation in data center or comparable mission-critical environments.

  • Ability to interpret detailed design drawings, specifications, contracts, and related documents to identify scope, deliverables, dependencies, and acceptance requirements.

  • Understanding of construction cost estimating, labor productivity, forecasting, cost-to-complete analysis, billing, and change management.

  • Ability to develop and maintain schedules, assess milestone impacts, and coordinate recovery plans across multiple teams.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to lead customer meetings, communicate risks clearly, and maintain accurate action and decision records.

  • Ability to build effective working relationships with customers, field teams, management, subcontractors, and vendors.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Outlook, Word, and PowerPoint, and experience with construction project management and document control tools. Experience with Bluebeam, Procore, and Textura is preferred.

  • Ability to work effectively under time constraints, adapt to changing requirements, and manage multiple priorities.

  • Commitment to continuous improvement, professional development, and team leadership.

Experience and Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in construction management, engineering, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of training, education, and relevant work experience.

  • Minimum of three years of relevant construction industry experience, including demonstrated responsibility for managing project scope, schedules, costs, customer communication, and closeout. Experience solely in estimating or field leadership must include comparable project delivery responsibilities.

  • Experience delivering structured cabling installations in data centers or comparable mission-critical facilities is required. Hyperscale data center experience is preferred.

  • OSHA 30-hour training is required within the first six months of employment if not completed before hire. Any training or credentials required for site access must be completed before the applicable site assignment.

Supervisory Responsibility:

This position may direct assigned Field Engineers, Project Coordinators, and other project resources on a project-by-project basis. The PM coordinates field execution with designated field leadership and manages delivery through the established project reporting structure.

Work Location and Travel:

This position is performed primarily on active construction project sites or at customer-operated facilities. Work-related travel may be up to approximately 25%.

Note: This job description outlines the general nature of the responsibilities and duties executed by this position. Other responsibilities and duties may be assigned as needed or required.

title: Mechanical Utility Engineer I
description:
Job Title: Mechanical Utility Engineer I
Department: Facility Technology Team
Shift: Core business hours are Monday-Friday, 8am-5pm
Direct Report: Maintenance Unit Manager
Type: Full-time; Exempt

About the position

We are looking for a reliable Mechanical Engineer to learn, understand, and actively support the execution of a professional maintenance system to achieve world class status in tire manufacturing: Eliminate forced deterioration of equipment and prevent accelerated deterioration > Reverse deterioration of equipment using breakdown analysis > Establish concise maintenance standards > Develop countermeasures against equipment weak points > Build a periodic maintenance system > Build a predictive maintenance system > Establish a cost management based Planned Maintenance System.

Supporting Metrics: Reduction of machine faults/ Improved OEE/ Improved Planned Maintenance activities/ Reduction of labor and material costs/ Improved product quality through a robust error-proofing process/ Improved ergonomics and safety at work-stations/ Extended useful life of equipment/ Reduction in set-up and change-over times/ Increased percentage of Planned Maintenance/ Reduced equipment life-cycle costs/ Elimination of conditions for accidents.

Responsibilities are:

  • Work with a “Safety Always” mindset through supporting and promoting continuous improvement of safety and health in the workplace
  • Perform all duties with a “Quality First” mindset through improvement of work processes and procedures to eliminate and prevent defects
  • Develop and maintain a “big picture” focus and understanding of the complete tire manufacturing process within the first 3-months of employment
  • Establish good rapport and build working relationships and networks with peers, technicians and other employees to develop a strong network/ support base
  • Develop and maintain effective working relationships with suppliers and other third parties
  • Remain current with professional practices and maintain a high awareness of new products and procedures in the industry. Monitor trade publications and actively participate in professional organizations

  • Interpret engineering specifications and solve routine problems by applying defined procedures with proven precedent
  • Systematically identify causes of problems and identify possible solutions in a Plan – Do – Check – Act methodology

title: Senior Complex Casualty Claims Resolution Specialist - Northwest Region
description:
Description

Senior Complex Casualty Claims Resolution Specialist - Northwest Region

Lead With Expertise. Deliver Impact That Matters. Grow With a Company That Invests in You.

At Liberty Mutual, we show up for people in their toughest moments, and we show up for our employees with the same commitment. We are seeking a Senior Complex Casualty Claims Resolution Specialist for our Northwest Region who brings deep technical expertise, sharp critical thinking, and a passion for doing what’s right.

If you’re energized by the challenge of managing high‑exposure, complex, and catastrophic injury claims, and you want to work in an environment where professionalism, integrity, and empathy guide everything we do, this is the role for you.

🌟 What Makes This Role Special:

You Own the Complex Work

You’ll be the point person on severe and catastrophic auto and homeowner’s casualty claims, navigating litigation, partnering with counsel, and driving strategy.

Your Expertise Is Valued

Your judgment plays a key role in shaping outcomes. You’ll influence decisions on some of our most significant claims, backed by leaders who respect your experience.

Flexibility Meets Purpose

This role is remote or hybrid depending on location, with only a modest two days a month expectation if you live near a hub.

You’ll Keep Growing

From advanced technical training to mentorship opportunities, we’re dedicated to helping you expand your impact.

Competitive Bonus Opportunity

External candidates with an active FL or TX All‑Lines Adjuster License (CEs current) may qualify for a $2,500 sign‑on bonus.

What You’ll Do:

  • Manage the investigation, evaluation, and resolution of complex auto and homeowner’s casualty claims.
  • Assess coverage, liability, and damages; recommend settlement strategies and escalate appropriately for authority review.
  • Identifies potential suspicious claims and refers to SIU and identifies opportunities for third party subrogation.
  • Collaborate closely with trial counsel; attend mediations, arbitrations, trials, hearings, and conferences.
  • Prepare detailed litigation and trial reports for local management and Home Office.
  • Communicate effectively with policyholders, witnesses, attorneys, and claimants to gather information and provide guidance.
  • Responds to various written and telephone inquiries including status reports.
  • Maintain accurate reserves, recommending increases on cases in excess of authority.
  • Safeguard financial and confidential information across all claim files.
  • Oversee billing practices of outside and in‑house counsel to ensure compliance and cost efficiency.
  • May assist as a resource to the team, stepping in for the Claims Team Manager when needed or mentoring colleagues; or representing the company on matters involving state or federal regulatory agencies.
  • Participate in special projects at the direction of leadership.

Ideal Experience Includes:

  • 5+ years managing complex and litigated casualty claims
  • Deep expertise handling severe to catastrophic injuries and fatalities
  • Strong analytical thinking, negotiation skills, and sound judgment
  • Ability to thrive in a fast‑paced, high‑stakes environment
  • Professionalism, empathy, and exceptional communication skills

Where You Can Work:

If you live within 50 miles of one of our hub locations, the role is hybrid (2 days in office). Otherwise, it may be fully remote. Candidates located in the Central, Mountain, or Pacific time zones would be most ideal as this position supports claims located in the Pacific/Mountain Time Zones.

Hub Locations:
Chandler, AZ
Clifton Park, NY
Columbus, OH
Indianapolis, IN
Lake Mary, FL
Liberty Lake, WA
Marlton, NJ
Plano, TX
Suwanee, GA
Warrenville, IL
Westborough, MA

Travel: 10% for mediations, arbitrations, trials, or in‑person events.

Training That Sets You Up for Success:

Your growth begins on day one. Active engagement and reliable attendance during training are mandatory and crucial to your success in this high‑impact role.

Qualifications
  • Must have an expert knowledge of coverage, liability, and complex claims handling procedures.
  • Must be able to effectively handle claims at the highest technical and complexity level.
  • Must be knowledgeable of state and federal laws in the adjuster's jurisdiction.

description:

JOB DESCRIPTION

Critical Solutions is seeking a Network Engineer - Network Management Systems (NMS) and Automation to support our federal customer.

The NMS team member must possess expert command of the monitoring ecosystem, leveraging specific tools to deliver core organizational advantages:

  • Functional Domain Tool Mechanics / Features Business & Operational Benefits Fault & Performance Monitoring
  • Continuous SNMP/ICMP polling
  • Real-time alerting mechanisms
  • Synthetics & packet analysis • Minimizes MTTR: Faster root-cause isolation lowers Mean Time to Resolution.
  • Reduces Downtime: High-availability metrics prevent outages before they cascade
  • Configuration & Change Control •
  • Automated backups of device configs
  • Real-time configuration drift detection
  • Mass configuration deployments • Ensures Compliance: Restores safe baseline settings rapidly during bad changes.
  • Secures Network: Flashes alerts on unauthorized or rogue configuration alterations.
  • Traffic Analytics & Planning • NetFlow / sFlow / IPFIX collection
  • Historical data trending charts
  • Dynamic topology mapping • Cost Optimization: Validates bandwidth usage patterns for smarter capacity planning.
  • Uncovers Bottlenecks: pinpoints bandwidth hogs and abnormal traffic spikes.

PRIMARY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • RHEL 8 Back-End Operations & System Administration:
    • Operating System (OS) Lifecycle Management: Provision, configure, and maintain RHEL 8 servers hosting the core NMS applications across physical, virtual, and air-gapped environments.
    • Kernel & Performance Tuning: Optimize Linux kernel parameters, memory allocation, and storage subsystems to handle massive telemetry and configuration data intake (SNMP, NetFlow, Syslog, SSH, SCP) without data loss.
    • Patching & Vulnerability Mitigation: Leverage Red Hat Satellite or custom repositories to manage package rollouts, applying routine security errata and OS updates.
    • Automation & IaC: Write and maintain Ansible playbooks and other language scripts to automate server provisioning, user management, and repetitive operational tasks related to NMS tool objects.
    • Security & Compliance: Enforce security Linux policies, access rules, and STIG compliance to ensure the monitoring platform resists compromise.
    • Storage & File System Management: Configure and expand LVM (Logical Volume Manager) structures to manage high-write NMS databases and syslog partition scaling.
  • NMS Application & Tool Support
    • Platform Administration: Deploy, upgrade, and troubleshoot enterprise-grade NMS applications (Open Text NNMi, Open Text Network Automation, Cisco Catalyst Center, Arista Cloud Vision, Aruba Airwave and others).
    • Data Integration: Architect and maintain integrations between NMS engines, CMDB asset databases, and ITSM platforms like ServiceNow via APIs.
    • Polling & Telemetry Management: Configure polling intervals, customize SNMP MIBs and traps, and set up NetFlow collectors to build clear network matrices.
    • Fault Isolation & Alerting: Construct alerting logic, thresholds, and notification profiles to minimize alert fatigue while ensuring critical outages surface instantly.

  • Active Secret clearance
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in computer science, IT, Network Engineering, or an equivalent technical field.
  • OS Specialization: Hands-on experience administering RHEL 8 environments (RHCSA or RHCE certifications preferred).
  • Core Linux Skills: Advanced knowledge of systemd, system logging (rsyslog, journald), and native RHEL troubleshooting utilities (top, iotop, netstat, tcpdump).
  • Protocols: Deep knowledge of networking protocols including SNMP (v3), Syslog, SSH, ICMP, NetFlow, and TACACS+/RADIUS.
  • Automation: Proficiency in Ansible and scripting languages (Python, Bash) to run configuration infrastructure as code
  • Core Technical Skills
    • Network Engineering: Functional understanding of advanced multivendor routing and switching network environments. (Cisco, Arista, Brocade, Juniper, McAfee and others)
    • Network Security: Functional understanding of enterprise firewalls and robust Access Control Lists (ACLs).
    • Infrastructure Administration: Comprehensive lifecycle management and administration of diverse network nodes.
  • Automation & DevOps
    • Network Scripting: Proficiency in modern scripting languages like Python, PowerShell and YAML for network task automation.
    • Infrastructure as Code: Proficiency in Ansible playbook development, testing, and deployment.
    • Network Automation: Hands-on experience with network nodes configuration management and automated provisioning.
    • Automated Policy Management: Ability to design and deploy automated policy enforcement mechanisms across network infrastructure.
    • Network Management Systems (NMS) & Operations
    • NMS Administration: Expert-level administration, configuration, and end-to-end support of complex Network Management Systems like, Cisco Catalyst Center, OpenText Network Automation (NA), OpenText Network Node Manager (NNMi), and Arista CloudVision.
    • Linux & Container Infrastructure: Hands-on RedHat 8 administration, support, and Kubernetes orchestration for modern NMS deployments.
    • Performance Optimization: Continuous monitoring and proactive tuning of network nodes for peak performance.
  • Analytical & Leadership Skills
    • Advanced Problem Solving: Deep analysis of complex, ambiguous technical situations to drive root-cause resolution.
    • Executive Communication: Synthesis of complex technical data into concise, high-level summaries for executive decision-making.
    • Collaboration & Communication
    • Cross-Regional Collaboration: Proven experience working effectively with distributed, cross-functional teams located across the United States.
    • Remote Team Synergy: Skill in utilizing modern collaboration tools to bridge geographical gaps and maintain project alignment.
    • Workplace Adaptability: Demonstrated reliability and productivity managing a flexible 40-hour workweek schedule.

LOCATION:

  • On-site 100%. Norfolk, VA
  • Other acceptable work location: Jacksonville, FL or Pearl Harbor

CLEARANCE REQUIREMENT: Must possess an active DoD Secret Clearance. In addition, selected candidate must undergo background investigation (BI) and finger printing by the federal agency and successfully pass the preceding to qualify for the position. US CITIZENSHIP IS REQUIRED.

title: Exam & Audit Lead
description:
We are building a governance, risk, and compliance function to enable our company to build products that can withstand regulatory scrutiny, and to ensure Meta continues to meet global regulatory requirements and manage risk. We are seeking a candidate to serve as E&A's most senior technical authority on control identification, technical response development, and evidence production across Meta's external audit portfolio. This is a portfolio-level role: rather than owning a single engagement, you will set the technical strategy that determines how Meta evidences regulatory compliance across multiple concurrent audits and regulatory regimes, and you will be accountable for whether that strategy holds up under independent testing.

This is both a technical program and project management role. You should be able to read a system design, follow a data flow, and reason about whether a given log, pipeline, config, or metric can withstand independent testing — then drive the cross-functional work to make it so. At this level you are expected to do that at scale: establishing the evidence and control standards other teams build to, resolving the hardest and most ambiguous testability problems, and acting as the authoritative translation layer between external auditors and the engineering organizations whose systems are under examination.

title: Clinical Study Administrator
description:
The Clinical Study Administrator (CSA) assists in the coordination and administration of the study activities from the start up to execution and close out, and within the Local Study Team (LST) to ensure quality and consistency of interventional study deliverables to time, cost and quality objectives. Provides solutions to a variety of issues relating to the conduct of a study of moderate scope and complexity.

Typical Accountabilities:

  • Assists in coordination and administration of clinical studies from the start-up to execution and close out.
  • Collects, assists in preparation, reviews and tracks documents for the application process. Assists in timely submission of proper application/documents to EC/IRB and, where appropriate to Regulatory Authorities for the duration of the study.
  • Interfaces with Investigators, external service providers and CRAs during the document collection process to support effective delivery of a study and its documents.
  • Serves as local administrative main contact and works closely with the CRAs and/or the LSAD for the duration of the study.
  • Operational responsibility for the correct set-up and maintenance of the local eTMF and ISF including document tracking in accordance with ICH-GCP and local requirements.
  • Ensures essential documents under their responsibility are uploaded in a timely manner to maintain the eTMF “Inspection Readiness”.
  • Ensures that all study documents are ready for final archiving and completion of local part of the eTMF and supports the CRA in the close out activities for the ISF.
  • Contributes to the production and maintenance of study documents, ensuring template and version compliance.
  • Creates and/or imports clinical-regulatory documents into the Global Electronic Management System (e.g. ANGEL) ensuring compliance with the AstraZeneca Authoring Guide for Regulatory Documents.
  • Contributes to electronic applications/submissions by handling clinical-regulatory documents according to the requested technical standards i.e., Submission Ready Standards (SRS), supporting effective publishing and delivery to regulatory authorities.
  • Sets-up, populates and accurately maintains information in AstraZeneca tracking and communication tools (e.g. CTMS such as VCV, SharePoint, etc) and supports others in the usage of these systems (with the exception of countries where there is a specific role dedicated to set up and update the systems).
  • Prepares and/or supports contract preparation at a site level (with the exception of countries where there is a specific role dedicated to preparing site contracts).
  • Prepares/supports/performs Health Care Organisations (HCO)/Health Care Professionals (HCP) payments in accordance with local regulations.
  • Manages and contributes to coordination and tracking of study materials and equipment.
  • Coordinates administrative tasks during the study process, audits and regulatory inspections, according to company policies and SOPs.
  • Leads the practical arrangements and contributes to the preparation of internal and external meetings e.g., study team meetings, Monitors’ meetings, Investigators’ meetings. Liaises with internal and external participants and/or vendors, in line with international and local codes.
  • Prepares, contributes to and distributes presentation material for meetings, newsletters and web sites.
  • Responsible for layout and language control, copying and distribution of documents. Supports with local translation and spell checks in English to/from local language, as required.
  • Responsible for printing and distribution of documents such as letters and meeting minutes, and for handling and archiving of study/country related e-mails.
  • Interfaces with Data Management Centre and/or Data Management, Global Clinical Solutions representatives to facilitate the delivery of study related documents/material.
  • Ensures compliance with AstraZeneca’s Code of Ethics and company policies and procedures relating to people, finance, technology, security and SHE (Safety, Health and Environment).
  • Ensures compliance with local, national and regional legislation, as applicable.

Education, Qualifications, Skills and Experience:Essential:

  • Scientific degree that supports skills and capabilities of the position and ensures successful conduct of responsibilities and appropriate interactions with internal and or external customers.
  • Previous administrative experience preferably in the medical/ life science field.
  • Proven organizational and administrative skills.
  • Computer proficiency (Veeva Clinical Vault, SAP S/4HANA, Coupa)
  • Good knowledge of spoken and written English.

Desirable:

  • Working knowledge of the Clinical Study Process and an understanding of the range of working procedures relating to it, together with an understanding of the ICH-GCP guidelines.
  • Ability to develop advanced computer skills to increase efficiency in daily tasks.
  • Good verbal and written communication.
  • Good interpersonal skills and ability to work in an international team environment.
  • Willingness and ability to train others on study administration procedures.
  • Excellent organization and time management skills, excellent attention to detail, and ability to multi-task in a high-volume environment with shifting priorities.
  • Team oriented and flexible; ability to respond quickly to shifting demands and opportunities. • Integrity and high ethical standards.

title: Senior Android Developer, Launcher - HYBRID
description:

At ReachMobi, there are no ceilings. You are the owner and architect of your career path, with no one-size-fits-all model. You’ll be responsible for designing and optimizing a high-performance SDK, collaborating with other teams to seamlessly integrate it into apps, all while pushing the boundaries of what's possible in memory management and performance. title: Senior Business Process Consultant
description:
Make a difference here.

UltraViolet Cyber is a leading platform-enabled unified security operations company providing a comprehensive suite of security operations solutions. Founded and operated by security practitioners with decades of experience, the UltraViolet Cyber security-as-code platform combines technology innovation and human expertise to make advanced real-time cybersecurity accessible for all organizations by eliminating risks of separate red and blue teams.

By creating continuously optimized identification, detection, and resilience from today’s dynamic threat landscape, UltraViolet Cyber provides both managed and custom-tailored unified security operations solutions to the Fortune 500, Federal Government, and Commercial clients. UltraViolet Cyber is headquartered in McLean, Virginia, with global offices across the U.S. and in India.

UVCyber seeks a Senior Business Process Consultant for the United States Secret Service (USSS) contract supporting the Department of Homeland Security. This strategic, transformation-focused role offers a unique opportunity to drive national security outcomes by bridging technology innovation and operational excellence within the USSS Office of the Chief Information Officer.  
As the Business Process Consultant, you'll be the critical link between mission operations, technology transformation, and AI-enabled innovation. You'll analyze current-state processes, identify improvement opportunities, and translate business needs into actionable technology requirements and AI use cases—particularly where artificial intelligence can drive efficiency, automation, and better decision-making. You'll play a vital role in standing up the USSS AI Team by identifying and documenting AI use cases, building the AI Use Case Repository, supporting the AI-PMO through change management and stakeholder engagement, and ensuring AI initiatives align with mission needs.
Working across OCIO divisions and with field stakeholders, you'll document workflows, develop change management strategies, create transformation playbooks, and design frameworks enabling successful adoption of AI capabilities. This role requires analytical rigor combined with organizational change expertise and stakeholder empathy for a program of national importance. 

What You'll Do:

  • Analyze business processes and operational workflows across OCIO divisions and field operations to identify opportunities where AI can improve efficiency, decision-making, automation, and mission outcomes 
  • Identify, document, and prioritize AI use cases through stakeholder interviews, workshop facilitation, and operational analysis; build and maintain comprehensive AI Use Case Repository 
  • Translate business needs into prioritized AI use cases, requirements, and measurable outcomes to inform the AI Strategy, 3-Year Roadmap, and AI Team priorities 
  • Develop business cases for AI initiatives quantifying expected benefits, resource requirements, implementation timelines, and success metrics 
  • Support AI-PMO operations by providing business analysis, stakeholder engagement, and change management expertise for AI initiatives -Document as-is and to-be process maps, create business cases, and define KPIs to track AI implementation and transformation outcomes 
  • Support organizational change management activities including impact assessments, readiness evaluations, and adoption planning for AI and technology transformation initiatives -Facilitate cross-functional engagement with Cyber, Infrastructure, Mission Delivery, Business Support, and field stakeholders to ensure AI initiatives align with mission priorities 
  • Facilitate workshops, design thinking sessions, AI ideation sessions, and collaborative problem-solving activities 
  • Create communications materials, training content, and knowledge transfer assets supporting AI adoption; incorporate user feedback and lessons learned into playbooks 
  • Support AI governance activities by documenting AI use case approval processes, decision criteria, and prioritization frameworks

What You've Done:

  • Master’s degree + 7 years of experience in business process consulting, business analysis, or organizational change management; equivalencies considered (16 years of experience with no degree, AA + 12 years' experience, BA/BS + 10 years)
  • Ability to obtain a Public Trust clearance
  • Demonstrated expertise in business process analysis, process improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma), and workflow optimization
  • Proven experience translating business requirements into technology solutions and use cases
  • Strong change management capabilities with experience developing and executing change strategies
  • Experience facilitating workshops and engaging diverse stakeholders to identify improvement opportunities
  • Excellent facilitation, communication, and stakeholder management skills * Ability to document complex processes and requirements in clear, actionable formats  Desired
  • Professional certifications (CBAP, Lean Six Sigma, PMP)
  • Experience supporting federal government or DHS transformation initiatives
  • Familiarity with AI/ML technologies and how they enable business process automation
  • Experience identifying and documenting AI use cases in enterprise or government environments
  • Experience with Agile business analysis techniques and user story development
  • Prior experience in law enforcement, protective services, or national security environments
  • Knowledge of AI ethics, responsible AI principles, and federal AI guidance

What We Offer:

  • 401(k), including an employer match of 100% of the first 3% contributed and 50% of the next 2% contributed
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance (available on the 1st day of the month following your first day of employment)

If you want to make an impact, UltraViolet Cyber is the place for you!

title: Software Asset Management Product Owner - Enterprise SaaS
description:
About Us:

AdNet/AccountNet, Inc. is a WOSB, MBE and WBE owned human capital management firm, founded in 1990. We blend the best in people with the ongoing demands of the workplace by providing high-quality teams and subject matter experts.

Software Asset Management Product Owner – Enterprise SaaS

We are seeking an experienced Software Asset Management Product Owner – Enterprise SaaS to oversee and optimize a portfolio of enterprise SaaS applications, including collaboration solutions, productivity applications, and other enterprise-level cloud software platforms.

This position brings together SaaS product ownership, IT Asset Management, application administration, security, automation, licensing, and financial optimization. The successful candidate will take ownership of both the business and technical health of assigned SaaS applications, helping ensure they are secure, integrated, compliant, cost-effective, and easy to manage.

The role works across multiple disciplines and partners closely with teams responsible for Security, Identity, Procurement, Finance, Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, and Support. A key focus will be establishing strong governance and auditable access controls while using automation, AI, APIs, scripting, and low-code solutions to minimize manual administrative work.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

Product Ownership & Value Delivery | ~35%

  • Take ownership of the roadmap and backlog for assigned SaaS applications and/or ITAM technologies.
  • Continuously improve operations through automation, process standardization, and effective governance.
  • Find the appropriate balance between compliance obligations and business productivity.
  • Serve as the central point of communication between business stakeholders and engineering/support resources.
  • Develop meaningful measures of success related to application adoption, cost efficiency, and risk.
  • Review and assess proposed SaaS solutions before implementation, considering security, technical compatibility, integration requirements, and administrative effort.

SaaS Administration & Security Engineering | ~35%

  • Provide hands-on technical administration for enterprise-approved SaaS applications.
  • Help ensure applications remain secure, scalable, reliable, and efficiently managed.
  • Work with Security, Identity, and related teams to implement and administer:
    • SSO and conditional access.
    • MFA, administrative roles, and SaaS security controls.
    • Automated provisioning/deprovisioning, role assignment, license assignment, and access review workflows.
  • Support least-privilege security practices for users, administrators, service accounts, service principals, secrets, and API permissions.
  • Manage and automate joiner, mover, and leaver processes so that access remains aligned with job responsibilities, policy requirements, and audit expectations.
  • Apply AI, APIs, scripting, low-code platforms, and other automation technologies to reduce repetitive administrative work.
  • Create and maintain standards for application administration, administrative ownership, access review frequency, and secure system configurations.
  • Provide advanced escalation support for application and access issues beyond the Tier 1 and Tier 2 support levels.

SaaS Financial & Lifecycle Management | ~30%

  • Oversee assigned SaaS applications throughout their lifecycle, including onboarding, active management, renewal, and retirement.
  • Analyze license utilization, user activity, and spending to identify:
    • Underused software and opportunities to reclaim licenses.
    • Opportunities to modify licensing models and right-size vendor contracts.
  • Coordinate renewal readiness with Finance and Procurement using historical usage patterns and projected future demand.
  • Maintain accurate SaaS inventory records for applications, license entitlements, users, administrators, and integrations.
  • Improve organizational visibility into SaaS spending, utilization, and risk.
  • Support internal and external audit activities through license compliance validation and periodic user access reviews.
  • Administer governance activities in accordance with established ITAM standards.

Required Qualifications

  • At least 3 years of experience in SaaS application administration or IT Asset Management, with demonstrated hands-on technical expertise.
  • At least 3 years of experience configuring, integrating, securing, and administering enterprise SaaS applications, including SSO, API connectivity, and application administration consoles.
  • Strong understanding of major software licensing models, including named-user, concurrent, consumption-based, and enterprise agreements.
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with the ability to combine utilization, entitlement, and spending data into practical business recommendations.
  • Experience maintaining reliable configuration and inventory information across multiple systems and using data analysis or system queries to detect discrepancies.

title: Post-Doctoral Fellow
company: University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus
description:
Department\: Obstetrics and Gynecology

Job Title\: Post-Doctoral Fellow

Position #00729150 – Requisition # 41236

Job Summary\:

The Division of Urogynecology and Reconstructive Pelvic Surgery in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology seeks a full-time qualified postdoctoral fellow to assist with basic and translational projects with a specific emphasis on urinary tract infections. The position will require collaboration with several labs focused on microbiology, endocrinology, cancer biology, materials science, and pharmacology, with a focus on understanding how the immune system, hormones, and bacterial physiology affect lower urinary tract pathophysiology.

Key Responsibilities\:

85% - Research Operations

· Serial dilutions, Gram staining, agar plating assays, and microscopy

· Developing and executing standard operating procedures, including performing general lab chores, making agar plates, autoclaving, ordering reagents, and maintaining regulatory requirements

· Loading nanoparticles with drugs and quantifying drug delivery kinetics

· Experience with microbiology assays and polymer-bacteria interactions

· Mechanical characterization of polymers and polymer composites

· Mastery of general microbiology including\: chemical management, biology of bacteria and microscopy

· Cell culture and colony identification and quantification

· Tissue and cell extraction of RNA/DNA and protein

· Proficiency in Western blot assay, PCR, immunohistochemistry

· Mouse handling and survival surgery

· Aseptic technique, disinfection, and sterilization

10%- Teaching

· Teach/supervise students, professional research assistants, and other lab members

5% - Administrative Duties

· Other duties as assigned.

Work Location\:

Onsite – this role is expected to work onsite and is located in Aurora, Colorado.

Why Join Us\:

The Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the University of Colorado is a world-class research enterprise, ranked 21st in the nation by the Blue Ridge Institute for federal funding. The Department currently has an impressive research portfolio of $32M in existing federal and foundation grants and contracts through the lifetime of the projects, increasing in budget annually by $9M. Departmental faculty provide a full spectrum of clinical care for women of all ages, participate in research, and educate students and residents.

Why work for the University?

The University of Colorado offers a comprehensive benefits package. To see what benefits are available for Post-Doctoral Fellows, please visit\:

· Payroll & Benefits Orientation for Post-Doctoral Fellows | University of Colorado (cu.edu)

· benefits guide cover-post-doc-2024 (cu.edu)

Qualifications\:

Minimum Qualifications\:

· PhD in relevant scientific area such as Microbiology, Immunology, Cell Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Physiology, Biophysics or Reproductive Biology

· Relevant previous post-doctoral experience (for applicants with a previous postdoctoral fellowship)

· Relevant technical skills, including experience with and routine laboratory experiments such as performance and analysis of real-time PCR, western blotting, biochemical assays, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence.

Preferred Qualifications\:

· Experience in cell culture, cytotoxicity assays and animal/mouse handling

· One year or more years of experience with bacterial assays, macromolecular synthesis, polymer synthesis and characterization

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities\:

· Both classroom and laboratory experience.

· Candidates should have the ability to work independently, identify and set priorities, and meet deadlines.

· Ability to communicate effectively, both in writing and orally.

· Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with employees at all levels throughout the institution.

· Outstanding customer service skills.

· Demonstrated commitment and leadership ability to advance diversity and inclusion.

· Above all, the candidate must have a positive, persevering attitude, willingness to learn, and aspire to be a contributing member of our scientific team.

Conditions of Employment\:

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship. We are unable to provide work visa sponsorship or employment authorization for this position now or in the future.

How to Apply\:

For full consideration, please submit the following document(s)\:

1. A letter of interest describing relevant job experiences as they relate to listed job qualifications and interest in the position

2. Curriculum vitae / Resume

3. Five professional references including name, address, phone number (mobile number if appropriate), and email address

Applications are accepted electronically ONLY at www.cu.edu/cu-careers.

Questions should be directed to\: Tammy Orton, tammy.orton@cuanschutz.edu

Screening of Applications Begins\:

Applications will be accepted until finalists are identified, but preference will be given to complete applications received by October 31, 2026. Those who do not apply by this date may or may not be considered.

Anticipated Pay Range\:

The starting salary range (or hiring range) for this position has been established as

$63,480 – $77,076

The above salary range (or hiring range) represents the University’s good faith and reasonable estimate of the range of possible compensation at the time of posting. This position is not eligible for overtime compensation unless it is non-exempt.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Colorado provides generous leave, health plans and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

The University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus is dedicated to ensuring a safe and secure environment for our faculty, staff, students and visitors. To assist in achieving that goal, we conduct background investigations for all prospective employees.

title: Center for Sundhed & Omsorg søger en Udviklingskonsulent med sygeplejefaglig baggrund (genopslag)
description:
Center for Sundhed & Omsorg søger en erfaren Udviklingskonsulent, der kan arbejde strategisk, samt facilitere og udvikle kerneopgaven i tæt samspil med ledelsen.

Guldborgsund kommunes kerneopgave:

"At styrke borgernes muligheder for at mestre egen tilværelse og, i samarbejde med borgeren, sikre at alle kan indgå i relevante fællesskaber."

Center for Sundhed & Omsorg er et ambitiøst og visionært center med et stærkt fokus på tværgående samarbejde og opgaveløsning, som målrettet arbejder med at skabe værdi for kommunens borgere.

Centret står overfor at skulle implementere Sundhedsreformen, hvor samarbejdet på tværs af sektorer udvikler sig markant. Samtidig skal vi forme fremtidens kommunale sygepleje og udvikle den borgernære sygepleje, som bliver en stadig vigtigere del af det nære sundhedsvæsen. Dette kalder på nye løsninger, analytisk skarphed og stærke sundhedsfaglige perspektiver. Centret arbejder derudover fortsat videre med Ældrereformen, hvor de kommunale sygeplejefaglige indsatser forventes at skulle inkluderes i løbet af 2027.

Link til information om Sundhedsreform

Link til information om Ældrereformen

VI TILBYDER

Vi tilbyder en stilling med høj kompleksitet, hvor dine erfaringer og kompetencer vil være efterspurgt og hvor dit faglige aftryk vil være tydeligt. Du indgår i et tværfagligt team med 16 kollegaer, hvor der er højt til loftet og værdifuld kollegial sparring.

Du får en central rolle i udviklingen af fremtidens kommunale sygepleje og i arbejdet med at omsætte Sundhedsreformens ambitioner til konkrete løsninger tæt på borgerne.

Der er tale om et job, hvor innovation, mening og partnerskaber er vigtige for at skabe de rette betingelser for udviklingen af det nære sundhedsvæsen. Det er samtidig en stilling, hvor du bidrager til at understøtte de politiske, strategiske og organisatoriske mål og beslutninger.

Du er en del af en helhed, hvor samarbejde, dialog og inddragelse er nøglebegreber i at få organisationen til at fungere.

HOVEDOPGAVER

  • Understøtte centrets strategiske arbejde.
  • Understøtte udviklingen af fremtidens kommunale sygepleje.
  • Udvikle og sikre fremdrift i at forbedre patientsikkerheden samt kvalitets- og forbedringsarbejde med fokus på sammenhængende borgerforløb.
  • Understøtte implementeringen af Sundhedsreformen og nye sundhedsfaglige indsatser.
  • Understøtte implementeringen af den kommunale demensstrategi.
  • Være uddannelsesansvarlig for sygeplejerskeuddannelsen i kommunalt regi og for specialuddannelsen i borgernær sygepleje.

OM DIG

  • Du har gerne erfaring med tilsvarende opgaver.
  • Du brænder for udviklingen af fremtidens kommunale sygepleje og motiveres af at omsætte nationale reformer til lokal praksis.
  • Du kan arbejde systematisk med kvalitetsudvikling, forbedringer og udvikling af nye sundhedsfaglige løsninger.
  • Du har viden om, og erfaring med, at være ansat i en politisk styret organisation.
  • Du kan facilitere processer og skabe dialoger og gode samarbejdsrelationer.
  • Du kan anvende IT-systemer og styringsredskaber.

KVALIFIKATIONER

  • Du er uddannet sygeplejerske og har en relevant master- eller kandidatuddannelse.
  • Du har erfaring med, eller interesse for, udvikling af kommunal sygepleje samt kvalitetsudvikling og implementering af nye sundhedsfaglige indsatser.
  • Du har indsigt i sygeplejefaglig praksis og erfaring med kvalitets-, udviklings- eller forbedringsarbejde.
  • Du er en god sparringspartner.
  • Du har kørekort.

Kan du se dig selv som en nøglespiller i udviklingen af fremtidens kommunale og borgernære sygepleje, er du i stand til at se helheder, navigere i komplekse opgaver og omsætte strategiske ambitioner til praksis, så vil vi meget gerne høre fra dig.

title: Program Administrator, Women's Recovery Program
description:
ABOUT THE MIDNIGHT MISSION

Since 1914, The Midnight Mission has served people experiencing homelessness in Los Angeles's Skid Row. Through emergency services, recovery programs, interim housing, and structured re-entry, the Mission offers a path to stability and self-sufficiency. Staff are expected to carry out that work with dignity, accountability, and respect for every person who comes through our doors.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Program Administrator oversees and guides the rehabilitation and housing transition plans of women enrolled in the Women's Recovery Program. The role combines direct case management for an assigned caseload with lead responsibility for program operations: intake and admissions, documentation and billing compliance, file and HMIS audits, staff scheduling, and training of case management staff. The Program Administrator works in partnership with the Program Manager and serves as the program's working expert on documentation standards, Community Health Worker (CHW) billing through Pear Suite, and housing navigation.

Participants are adult women, many with histories of chronic homelessness, trauma, serious psychiatric disabilities, and co-occurring substance use disorders. The work is delivered through trauma-informed, gender-responsive, and recovery-oriented practice consistent with Housing First principles.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The duties below are essential functions of the position. Percentages are approximate and reflect a typical month.

1. Assessment, Service Planning, and Case Management (approx. 30%)

  • Conducts program intake screening interviews, fields intake calls, screens prospective participants against program criteria, and recommends placement or referral; coordinates admissions with the Program Manager.
  • Conducts comprehensive screenings and assessments to gather functional, environmental, psychosocial, financial, employment, housing, educational, and health information.
  • Develops an Individualized Service Plan (ISP) with each participant that identifies priorities, desired outcomes, action steps, referrals, and the resources to be used; reviews and updates the plan at defined intervals and when circumstances change.
  • Leads service coordination for an assigned caseload, taking primary responsibility for developing and carrying out goals in collaboration with the participant and the care team, and providing support, guidance, and encouragement throughout her path to housing.
  • Provides service linkages and coordinates with outside providers (medical, behavioral health, SUD treatment, benefits, legal, employment) so identified needs are met; follows up on referrals to confirm connection.
  • Engages participants with histories of chronic homelessness, serious psychiatric disabilities, and co-occurring disorders respectfully, using motivational interviewing, harm reduction, and de-escalation techniques.

2. Housing Navigation (approx. 15%)

  • Conducts housing-focused sessions to assess and reassess housing needs, educate participants on housing options and tenancy expectations, and track progress of the plan toward resolving the participant's housing crisis.
  • Supports document readiness and completes paperwork required to place participants holding vouchers or other subsidies into housing, including coordination with housing authorities, landlords, and housing navigators.
  • Works with community partners to develop strategies that encourage participants to take steps toward permanent housing; participates in Coordinated Entry System (CES) processes as assigned.
  • Serves as secondary point of contact for housing-related communications, coordinating between housing partners and internal staff.

3. Groups, Health Education, and Recovery Supports (approx. 15%)

  • Facilitates workshops and discussion groups on anger management, conflict resolution, and life planning skills.
  • Facilitates health education groups in compliance with Medi-Cal Community Health Worker service and billing requirements, including documentation of attendance, content, and duration.
  • Serves as primary point of contact for scheduling and coordinating 12-Step panels and outside recovery meetings.
  • Manages and schedules telehealth center appointments for program participants.

4. Documentation, Billing, and Compliance (approx. 25%)

  • Prepares timely, accurate case notes and progress reports; documents participant interactions, care plans, and progress in the Pear Suite care coordination platform.
  • Maintains participant records in HMIS in accordance with funder data standards; reports participant progress monthly.
  • Oversees Pear Suite CHW claims for the program: reviews documentation before submission, identifies and corrects errors or denials, and escalates billing concerns to the Program Manager.
  • Conducts regular participant file audits and HMIS data-quality audits against program, funder, and TMM standards; reports findings and tracks corrective action to completion.
  • Audits medication logs for participant self-administration to confirm accuracy and completeness; reports discrepancies per TMM protocol. (This position does not administer medication.)
  • Collects urine specimens for drug and alcohol screening following TMM's chain-of-custody and privacy protocol, including same-gender observed collection where required; records and reports results.
  • Protects participant confidentiality under HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, and TMM policy; fulfills mandated reporter obligations under California law.

5. Staff Guidance and Program Operations (approx. 10%)

  • Trains, mentors, and provides day-to-day guidance to case management staff on program procedures, documentation standards, and best practices. This is a lead role; hiring, discipline, and performance evaluation decisions remain with the Program Manager.
  • Prepares staff schedules and monitors shift coverage for the program, following TMM overtime, meal and rest period, and timekeeping policies; escalates coverage gaps to the Program Manager.
  • Orders and tracks program supplies through TMM's requisition process.

6. Reporting, Outreach, and Special Projects (approx. 5%)

  • Produces program reports and PowerPoint presentations on program status and outcomes for staff, leadership, and the Board of Directors.
  • Assists the Program Manager with community engagement and program outreach.
  • Acts as liaison to partner agencies and community programs to maintain coordination of care.
  • Completes special projects and other related duties as assigned.

PERFORMANCE MEASURES

Success in this role is measured by, among other things:

  • Service plans completed and updated within required timeframes for 100% of assigned participants.
  • HMIS data completeness and timeliness at or above funder thresholds.
  • Pear Suite claim accuracy and a low, declining rate of denied or returned claims.
  • Participant housing placements and exits to permanent or stable housing.
  • Audit findings closed within agreed timeframes; no uncovered shifts attributable to scheduling.

title: U.S. Army Transition Course - Primary Instructor
description:
Are you looking for a Challenge? Looking for an innovative organization and the opportunity to learn and grow professionally? We can help! We are seeking a Primary Instructor to support Army University’s Army Strategic Education Program – Transition Course (ASEP-T), an executive career-transition program for retiring and separating U.S. Army General Officers and their spouses. This is a Key Personnel position. Courses are delivered in person in the National Capital Region (historically the AUSA Conference and Events Center in Arlington, VA) and online, with five (5) five-day courses per year, one (1) Introductory Transition Module, and up to eight (8) Four-Star Executive Sessions annually.

I’ve never heard of Terrestris. What do you do?

At Terrestris, we leverage technology to create better mission outcomes through better human performance. We form strong client and team relationships through transparency and strive to create an environment where our team can let their excellence shine through. By finding, developing, and incorporating new ideas, we provide memorable services. Rooted in the USMC values of honor, courage, and commitment, Terrestris seeks to deliver extraordinary value to the American people by helping the Government become more efficient and effective.

So, what will the Primary Instructor at Terrestris do?

The Primary Instructor serves as the lead instructor for ASEP-T, a five-day executive education course that prepares transitioning General Officers and their spouses to move from senior military leadership into the civilian workforce in accordance with the Veterans Opportunity to Work (VOW) Act, Transition Assistance Program (TAP), and Soldier for Life requirements. Using executive adult learning models and challenging experiential exercises rather than lecture, the Primary Instructor teaches, presents, or facilitates the majority of the curriculum, including pre-separation counseling, individual transition planning, resumes, networking, personal branding, interviewing, salary negotiation, and employment assistance.

Working alongside the Alternate Instructor and in coordination with the ASEP-T Course Director, the Primary Instructor also provides individual counseling to each participant, delivers customized transition sessions for retiring four-star generals, and drives continuous curriculum improvement through pre-course surveys, course evaluations, after action reviews, and longitudinal follow-up with course graduates.

What does a typical day look like for a Primary Instructor?

You will:

  • Serve as lead instructor for five (5) five-day ASEP-T courses per year (approximately eight hours per day) for up to 18 General Officers in person or 22 online, plus their spouses.
  • Develop and maintain a current, modular curriculum adaptable to face-to-face and online delivery (e.g., Zoom, Teams) that meets VOW Act, TAP, Soldier for Life, and Department of Labor requirements.
  • Present a five-to-ten-year vision of the executive landscape that helps General Officers determine where they best fit as executive leaders.
  • Guide participants in building individual transition plans, including pre-separation timelines, realistic career goals, interest/aptitude assessments, and translation of military experience into civilian terms.
  • Instruct on resumes/CVs and cover letters, networking plans, LinkedIn and social media, job search methods, personal branding, interviewing, civilian salary scales and negotiation, public and non-profit opportunities, and legal and ethical constraints unique to retiring General Officers.
  • Facilitate experiential exercises, including internet- and AI-enabled exercises, resume building, mock interviews, and mock offer negotiations.
  • Conduct individual counseling sessions with each participant (and spouse, as applicable), including in-depth resume critiques, transition plan feedback, strengths assessments, and networking plan reviews.
  • Help design and deliver an integrated spouse curriculum with spouse-specific break-out sessions.
  • Coordinate a Day 2 no-host networking event featuring at least three (3) recently retired General Officers.

Southern California Permanente Medical Group (SCPMG) is a physician-led partnership with strong values that support a patient-centered and evidence-based approach to medicine.

Riverside County encompasses an area known as the Inland Empire. It also includes the greater Palm Springs/Coachella resort area. Riverside features an extensive range of relatively affordable housing options, notable schools, and outdoor recreational opportunities. The county encapsulates a small-town feel with local attractions including seasonal fruit picking and local wineries.

Working here

Physicians are offered incredible variety—they can work in an urban setting or in rural locations with a small-town feel; at the main medical center or a satellite office; at the foot of the San Bernardino mountains or in the desert. With its exceptional growth rate—perhaps the highest in the region—the area is still evolving, with new talent and ideas arriving each week. This keeps keep the Riverside environment fresh, young, and exciting, with leadership opportunities being presented regularly.

title: Science Policy Internship
description:
Position Overview: Nonprofit organization is seeking a student currently enrolled in undergraduate- or graduate-level studies in public policy, government affairs, or a related field for a Spring 2027, unpaid, part-time, remote internship focused on advancing federal science and research policies that reduce and replace animal experimentation.

About the Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine

Industry: Nonprofit organization

The Physicians Committee's Mission and Vision: The Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine is dedicated to saving and improving human and animal lives through plant-based diets and ethical and effective scientific research. Our vision is to create a healthier world in which health and compassion are central values in science and medicine.

The Physicians Committee's Values:

  • Compassion: We encourage compassion for people and animals.
  • Health: We promote good health through good nutrition. We practice what we preach by having a vegan office environment, ongoing nutrition education, and a culture that supports health and wellness.
  • Truth: We base our recommendations on evidence, not on biases or what is commonly accepted.
  • Professionalism: We hold our work to the highest standards, down to the last detail. This shows up in our scientific publications, our campaign work, and our public communications, and also in our appearance, our work ethic, how we keep our workspaces and take care of our resources, our focus on professional development, and the courtesies we extend to others.
  • Action: We speak out against unhealthful, dangerous, and unethical practices. We push limits and persevere.
  • Innovation: We bring new approaches to solving problems and continually seek ways to be more effective. We are not afraid to take risks.
  • Urgency: Our problems are urgent, and so are our responses. We stay alert to issues that need our attention and stay in close touch with one another and with our members and partners so we're able to take immediate action whenever necessary.
  • Dedication: This is a cause, not just a job. We go the extra mile to bring about a healthier, more compassionate world.
  • Collaboration: Working together, everyone achieves more. We collaborate with each other, with our members, and with other organizations.
  • Positivity: We approach our work with optimism. We plan with the end in mind and envision success.

Location of Organization: Washington, D.C.

Organization Size: Approximately 100 employees

Learn More About the Physicians Committee: We invite you to visit our website at or our YouTube channel.

About the Internship

Position Title: Science Policy Intern

About the Research and Regulatory Affairs Team: The Physicians Committee's Research and Regulatory Affairs team is composed of experts in human-relevant research, education, and testing methods. We collaborate with regulatory, industrial, and academic scientists to develop, assess, and promote alternatives to the use of animals in science. We engage decision-makers in government and industry to make change.

About the Internship: The intern will learn about the federal appropriations process and how Congress and federal agencies shape science and research policy, with a focus on efforts to reduce and replace animal experimentation. The intern will gain hands-on experience researching policy issues, supporting congressional appropriations requests, and developing advocacy and educational materials. They will also learn how scientific evidence is used to inform policy and advocacy strategies.

Internship learning opportunities may include:

  • Researching federal science and research policy related to reducing and replacing animal experimentation
  • Supporting congressional appropriations requests and developing advocacy and educational materials
  • Attending congressional meetings, briefings, hearings, and other relevant events
  • Tracking relevant legislation and federal policy developments

All interns will receive an orientation at the start of their internship and ongoing support from their staff mentor. The Physicians Committee will assist the intern in obtaining course credit, if applicable.

Work Location: Remote. The Physicians Committee can accept applications only from people who will be living in and working from the following jurisdictions for the duration of the internship: California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Hawaii, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Dakota, Texas, Virginia, Washington state, and Washington, D.C. Interns located in the Washington, D.C., area may have the opportunity to visit our Washington, D.C., office and to participate in in-person activities and events. Please note that we cannot accept applications from applicants working in locations outside of the United States.

Required Travel: None

Time Frame and Work Schedule:

  • Time frame: 3.5 months starting approximately January 2027
  • Work Schedule: 8–10 hours per week between the hours of 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, ET.

*The start and end dates and hours can be somewhat flexible to accommodate the intern's academic program.

Compensation: This unpaid volunteer internship is not available as employment.

Reports To:

  • Internship Mentor: Advocacy and Policy Program Manager
  • Department Director: Director of Research Policy

Qualifications

Education:

  • Required: Pursuing an undergraduate degree or above, with an interest in public policy, animal advocacy, government affairs, or a related field.

Work Experience:

  • Required: None
  • Preferred: Experience in advocacy or lobbying is preferred.

Additional Qualities:

  • Required: Alignment with the Physicians Committee's mission to reduce and replace animal experimentation in scientific research.
  • Preferred:
    • Interest in or familiarity with science, research, or STEM-related topics.
    • Located in the Washington, D.C., metropolitan area and available to attend occasional in-person events.

How to Apply

Application Materials: We require a formal cover letter and resume to apply. In your cover letter, please tell us about your interest in science and research policy, your interest in the Physicians Committee's mission to reduce and replace animal experimentation, your related experience and accomplishments, and your professional goals. Please also include a writing sample. You may be asked to respond in writing to screening questions.

Application Deadline: Applications are being accepted on a rolling basis.

Application Process:

  • Step 1: 45-minute Zoom interview with our Advocacy and Policy Program Manager
  • Step 2: Follow-up 30-minute Zoom interview with our Director of Research Policy
  • Step 3: Reference checks with the two most recent direct mentors or supervisors

For More Information: Contact the Physicians Committee's human resources department at careers@pcrm.org.

title: Senior Healthcare Integration Engineer (Remote Opportunity)

The engineer will support EHR, claims, public-health, HIE, and other healthcare data sources while performing data mapping, transformation, routing, interface deployment, troubleshooting, and production support.

The role operates in a highly collaborative environment, working with senior integration engineers, FHIR engineers, onboarding teams, testers, vendors, and facility technical teams to resolve integration issues, support successful deployments, and maintain reliable, secure, and scalable healthcare integrations.

The candidate must reside within the continental US.

Responsibilities

  • Develop, implement, configure, deploy, and support source-system interfaces, integration configurations, data pipelines, and exchange services across healthcare integration environments.
  • Evaluate source-system requirements, interface specifications, data flows, and integration dependencies to configure and maintain reliable, secure, and scalable integrations.
  • Perform data mapping, transformation, message routing, interface configuration, defect resolution, integration testing, and production-support activities.
  • Support integrations involving EHR, claims, public-health, HIE, FHIR, HL7, MLLP, and other healthcare data sources and technologies.
  • Support facility and vendor onboarding by coordinating interface deployments, testing, troubleshooting, and technical implementation activities.
