Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Healthcare Informatics, or a related field and 10+ years of related professional experience.
  • Extensive experience with healthcare interoperability, source-system integration, interface configuration, and enterprise application integration.
  • Strong experience with data mapping, transformation, message routing, interface deployment, and troubleshooting across complex healthcare data flows.
  • Experience with healthcare integration technologies and standards such as HL7, FHIR, MLLP, APIs, and data pipelines.
  • Strong analytical and debugging skills with the ability to identify and resolve complex integration defects and data-flow issues.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work autonomously with technical teams, vendors, and healthcare facility stakeholders.

Additional Qualifications

  • Experience with Java, scripting, XML, JSON, SQL, healthcare interface engines, Apache NiFi, and enterprise integration technologies.
  • Experience supporting EHR, claims, public-health, HIE, and FHIR-based integrations in enterprise healthcare environments.
  • Experience with facility and vendor onboarding, integration testing, configuration management, source code management, and production support.

Security Clearance Requirements

Benefits

Forvia, a sustainable mobility technology leader

Travel: Periodic travel to THOR worksites, industry events, other partner locations, and government customer locations within the United States. A fully remote candidate may additionally be required to travel to Virginia Beach, VA frequently.

Eligibility for a SECRET Security Clearance is Required: This position requires eligibility for a Secret security clearance, to be obtained after hire. Only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance; therefore, only current U.S. citizens will be considered for this position.

title: Research Scientist, AI & Systems Co-Design (PhD)
description:

title: CEO / Team Leader
description:
CEO / Team Leader – Keller Williams Real Estate
Blue Bell & Lafayette Hill, PA | Full-Time

About Us
Keller Williams Real Estate—Blue Bell is one of the leading Keller Williams market centers in the Greater Philadelphia region, with over 200 agents across multiple offices in Montgomery County. We're built on the KW belief that when agents grow, the business grows, and we're looking for a leader who lives that every day.

The Role
The CEO / Team Leader is the growth engine of the market center. This is a leadership role focused on recruiting top talent, keeping them, and helping them build real businesses. You'll own agent count, agent productivity, and the culture that holds it all together. If you love real estate, love people, and measure yourself by the success of others, this is your seat.

What You'll Do

Recruiting (your #1 priority)

  • Build and run a consistent, high-volume recruiting pipeline targeting experienced agents from competing brokerages as well as new licensees.
  • Conduct daily recruiting appointments, career visions, and follow-up; hit weekly and monthly appointment and hire goals.
  • Use KW Command, Smart Plans, and data tools to identify, track, and nurture prospects.
  • Present the KW value proposition with confidence, including profit share, wealth building, training, and technology, and back it up with real net-income comparisons.

Retention

  • Create a culture where productive agents want to stay and grow.
  • Hold regular one-on-ones, business planning sessions, and mid-year strategy reviews with agents.
  • Spot at-risk agents early and step in with coaching, support, and accountability.
  • Recognize wins and build a sense of community across all office locations.

Coaching & Productivity

  • Coach agents on lead generation, conversion, and business planning using KW models (MREA, BOLD, and the KW training curriculum).
  • Deliver or facilitate training sessions and team meetings.
  • Drive agent productivity through clear goals and consistent accountability.

Market Center Leadership

  • Partner with the Operating Principal and MCA to hit profitability and growth targets.
  • Lead the Associate Leadership Council (ALC) and support agent leadership development.
  • Represent KW Blue Bell in the community and across the local industry.

What We're Looking For

  • Real estate experience is required. You must have a strong track record in residential real estate as a producing agent, team leader, or brokerage leader. This is not an entry-level or out-of-industry role.
  • Active Pennsylvania real estate license (or ability to obtain one quickly).
  • A proven ability to recruit, whether through building a team, growing an office, or attracting agents.
  • A coaching mindset: you get energy from helping others win.
  • A competitive drive, strong accountability, and comfort with numbers and metrics.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, one-on-one and in front of a room.
  • Keller Williams experience not required, but will be considered a strong plus.
  • Knowledge of the Montgomery County / Greater Philadelphia market is preferred.

What You'll Get

  • Base salary + performance bonus / profit-based compensation, along with significant ownership opportunities
  • Access to Keller Williams' world-class leadership training and coaching programs.
  • A large, established agent base and a strong local brand to build on.
  • A real opportunity to shape the growth and culture of a multi-office market center.

Ready to lead?

Keller Williams Real Estate—Blue Bell is an equal opportunity employer.

title: Senior Service Desk Analyst
description:
EP Wealth Advisors (EPWA) is a wealth management advisory firm with over $49.1 billion as of June 30, 2026, serving predominately high net worth individuals. EPWA fosters an inclusive environment that offers opportunities for our associates to learn, grow and enhance their skills to take on new challenges to progress in their professional careers.

As a member of our growing Information Technology team, the Senior Service Desk Analyst provides support for applications, user account administration, and Tier 2/3 enterprise application support. The Senior Service Desk Analyst is responsible for ensuring timely and effective resolution of IT-related issues, maintaining high levels of client satisfaction, and providing a senior level of technical and business acumen. This role engages with the managed service provider (MSP) responsible for ticket triage and Level 1 support, serving as a technical escalation point and contributing to support playbooks that expand the range of tickets the MSP can resolve.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provide Tier 2/3 service desk support for moderate to complex technical issues, service requests, and incidents.
  • Provide C-Suite/VIP in person support.
  • Serve as an escalation point for users, coordinating resolution with appropriate support groups while maintaining a high level of service quality and client satisfaction.
  • Engage with the MSP responsible for ticket triage and Level 1 support as a technical escalation point for tickets requiring Tier 2/3 support or coordination with other IT teams.
  • Contribute to the creation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of support playbooks that expand the range of tickets the MSP can resolve.
  • Participate in team training and knowledge-sharing activities.
  • Assess problems and issues related to, but not limited to: Hardware (such as, laptops, desktops, peripherals), Software (Microsoft Office365, SharePoint, OneDrive, Adobe Acrobat), Active Directory account issues, Mobile Devices, and other enterprise applications.
  • Fulfill routine end-user requests, resolve service failures, perform routine operational maintenance, and perform administrative tasks.
  • Strive for timely resolution of assigned and MSP-escalated tickets; when applicable, escalate and assign issues to appropriate support groups.
  • Utilize the ITSM application for issue and request tracking, ensuring all user requests for assistance are documented with an appropriate ticket, and all tickets requiring follow-up work and/or calls receive appropriate attention within designated SLAs.
  • Interact with asset management, network services, software systems engineering, applications development, and printer maintenance services to identify, correct and restore technical problems.
  • Partner with the Service Desk Team Lead or Service Desk Manager in recommending continuous improvement initiatives that support improved services.
  • Help ensure that industry standard cyber security standards are implemented and followed.
  • Serve as a technical resource for service desk team members, providing guidance and support as needed.
  • Collaborate with other IT teams and organizational stakeholders to resolve complex technical issues.
  • Ensure that all business activities are performed with the highest ethical standards and in compliance with the EP Wealth Code of Business Conduct.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Associate or bachelor’s degree in information technology, or related field (preferred) or equivalent experience.
  • A minimum of 3-5 years in a similar senior service desk or technical support role, preferably within a corporate environment.
  • Strong knowledge of ITIL functions (Incident, Change, Knowledge Management, IT Asset and License Management)
  • Knowledge of network administration and troubleshooting.
  • Experience supporting Microsoft Entra ID; experience with Microsoft Intune is preferred.
  • Hands-on experience supporting Microsoft Windows 11, macOS, and iOS.
  • Experience supporting Microsoft 365 products, including Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and SharePoint.
  • Experience supporting Zoom Workplace products, including Meetings, Phone System, Zoom Rooms, Scheduler, and Workplace Reservation.
  • Experience supporting enterprise applications and productivity tools, including Adobe products, Salesforce, Slack, ChatGPT, and Claude.
  • Exceptional customer service orientation and demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Robust organizational skills, with the capacity to multitask and prioritize in a high-demand environment.
  • Ability to travel to company offices throughout the US. (~25%)

What We Offer
We offer a highly competitive suite of holistic benefits designed to help our team members balance their personal and professional life commitments. These include options designed to encourage employee's health, happiness, and financial well-being.

  • 11 Paid Holidays + 2 Floating Holidays
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Paid Volunteer Time
  • Flexible Work Schedule
  • Highly subsidized Health, Dental, and Vision Plans
  • 401k Retirement Account with company match contributions
  • Free Mental Health services, Life Insurance, Long & Short-Term Disability Insurance
  • Flexible Spending Accounts and Health Savings Accounts
  • Employee Financial Education

  • Employee Charitable Donations
  • Employee Referral Incentives
  • Employee Team Building Activities
  • Employee Assistance Program

title: Associate Video Editor, TODAY Digital

We’re looking for a talented, versatile and highly organized Associate Video Editor to join our team. This role will work closely with producers, editors and other members of the TODAY and NBC News teams to edit, organize and deliver video content across TODAY’s digital, streaming and social platforms.

title: Mechanical Assembler I
description:
SUMMARY

This Job Description provides a description of the duties for which the Mechanical Assembler I will be accountable and responsible. The intent of this Job Description is to enable the Employee to be successful within the chain of command, by promoting transparent, effective, efficient, and quality corporate operations. Other duties may be assigned to the Mechanical Assembler I from time to time: these additional duties will be communicated directly from the Fit-up/Assembly Supervisor or Plant Manager.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES

Perform all duties assigned by the immediate supervisor or technician to which the Assembler I is assigned. This includes, but is not limited to material handling, abrasive metal cleaning, sweeping, washing, general helper duties.

Position and align parts in specified relationship to each other in jig, fixture, or other holding device.

Keep work area tidy and orderly.

Crimp, stake, screw, bolt, rivet, weld, cement, press fit, or perform similar operations to join or secure parts in place.

Devise, fabricate, and assemble new or modified mechanical components or assemblies for products.

Use and maintain safety equipment as required.

Ensure that all problems with equipment and machinery are promptly reported to the Maintenance

Department for corrective action. Halt production on equipment and machinery if they cannot be safely operated.

The Mechanical Assembler I must be trained in the proper use of material handling equipment such as forklifts and overhead cranes. Must know and follow requirements for the proper storage and allocation of supplies and material. Must also be trained in company safety requirements.

Perform other related duties, as assigned, for the purpose of ensuring an efficient and effective work environment.

Ensure activities are conducted in accordance with Vital Link International Standards Organization (ISO9000) policies and correct and report any deviations to appropriate area manager/supervisor.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

N/A

ISO9000 SPECIFIC DUTIES

Be familiar with and understand Vital Link Quality Policy and company objectives.

Understand required ISO9000 specific Procedures and Work Instructions.

Complete all records required by Procedures and Work Instructions.

Participate in Vital Link Continuous Improvement activities as appropriate.

Participate in ISO9000 training as required.

Cooperate with Auditors.

Report any deviations to appropriate area manager/supervisor.

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE

High school diploma or General Education Degree (GED); a minimum 2 years’ experience with Metal fabrication or assembly shop experience is preferred; or combination of education and experience.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

N/A

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Employee is frequently required to stand, sit, stoop, crouch, bend, walk and routinely lift and/or move up to (50) pounds.)

Must be able to perform medium to heavy physical labor. Should have the ability to operate hand and power tools required to perform general labor activities. Must have the ability to coordinate and communicate effectively with other personnel.

Should be able to properly lift moderate and heavy steel parts, equipment, and supplies on a routine basis.

Typical lifting requirements will not exceed fifty (50) pounds.

The employee must have a full range of body movements including the use of hands to fingers, handle or feel objects, climbing, bending, reaching, lifting, and walking.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position will be working primarily outdoors and in an open shop in all types of weather. This position is exposed to heavy amounts of potentially hazardous dust and fumes requiring the use of safety glasses and protective clothing is required.

Noise level in the work environment is often quite high, which may often require hearing protection.

Usually eight (8) hour workdays (5) days per week are required. Occasional Saturday and Sunday work, or overtime, may be required to accommodate special business circumstances.

Extended work hours and/or travel may occasionally be required.

Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to disability or protected veteran status.

If you need a reasonable accommodation, please contact Andrea Lopez at 281-276-2700.

title: ASST COMM MGR FAM SUPP COORD - Aida Palms
description:

Under direct supervision of the Community Manager, the Assistant Community Manager/ Family Support Coordinator acts as the administrative assistant for the property and is responsible for understanding company policies and procedures and assisting the Community Manager in implementing such on the property. The Assistant Community Manager is responsible for effectively computing, classifying, and recording numerical data to keep financial records complete while assisting with leasing, marketing, and resident relations for the community.

In the Family Support Coordinator role, the incumbent facilitates and coordinates various activities and training methods to assist adult residents with improving their prospects for self-sufficiency, employability, health care and economic self-reliance. In addition, the Coordinator will assist community residents with improving their education opportunities by providing tutoring, computer training and other creative and educational activities.

This position receives support from the Community Manager and RAM’s Resident Services Director. Incumbent is expected to have excellent attendance and communication skills, possess the ability to build lasting business relationships, and exhibit professionalism.

Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Create a positive, welcoming, supportive environment for residents, visitors, and community associates
  • Assist Community Manager in attracting, screening, and selecting prospective residents in accordance with federal and state governing program laws and regulations utilizing the set Resident Selection Criteria
  • Maintain knowledge and awareness of market conditions affecting leasing and operations
  • Assist Community Manager in developing and executing marketing and advertising campaigns for apartment leasing
  • Maintain sound rent collection procedures, including following up with delinquent accounts
  • Deliver rent deposits to bank and submit relevant documentation
  • Assist in overseeing the security deposit administration including inspecting units to determine resident’s balance or refund, prepare disposition letters, and process security deposit returns
  • Maintain familiarity with all procedures and requirements for accounts payable
  • Assist in the preparation of the annual operating budget, and works with the Community Manager to maintain budgetary guidelines
  • Assist in monitoring landlord-tenant relations and mediate disputes when necessary
  • Utilize maintenance software program to enter in and track service request, and regularly review maintenance reports
  • Inspect apartments for move in condition and turn over status
  • Inspect property grounds, office, community room(s) and all other amenities to ensure they are clean and maintained
  • Ensure all contractors/vendors have approval from Vendor Compliance prior to performing any work on the property, once approved monitor the activities being performed
  • Provide resources to residents to assist with finding employment as part of a Resident Employment Assistance program
  • Provide resource and referral information to residents to assist with basic family needs, including but not limited to childcare, transportation, medical care, chemical and drug addiction, elderly services, food pantry, clothes closet, domestic violence, energy assistance, housing assistance, etc.
  • Provide residents with personal interest workshops, social and holiday activities, and community and safety involvement activities
  • Provide software instruction in Microsoft Office applications, Microsoft Windows and Internet basics as part of a computer literacy program
  • Market programs to the community and residents, post flyers throughout the community, develop and distribute monthly activity calendar highlighting all workshops, classes and activities to take place during the upcoming month
  • Complete and submit by email accurate monthly reporting package
  • Maintain accurate documentation showing resident participation levels and progress
  • Develop community partnerships
  • Raise funds to supplement current budget
  • Coordinate transportation and/ or transport residents for shopping and activities and assist them with groceries, walkers, and other mobility equipment.
  • Maintain clean and orderly appearance of center

  • Demonstrate strong written and oral communication skills

title: Transportation Planner
description:
Lochner and Egis are entering an exciting new chapter as one organization.

We have combined decades of trusted U.S. engineering expertise with the global reach, technical excellence, and career opportunities of a leading international engineering, consulting, and infrastructure firm. While our name has changed, our commitment to our people, clients, and communities is stronger than ever.

At Egis, every project is an opportunity to create lasting impact. We collaborate with public and private clients to design and deliver innovative transportation, aviation, rail, transit, water, structural, environmental, and infrastructure solutions that connect communities and improve everyday life. Join a team where innovation is encouraged, collaboration is valued, and your work helps build a more sustainable future.

The Transportation Planner will lead and support a variety of transportation, environmental planning, and applied technology projects. This role requires an experienced professional capable of managing tasks independently, mentoring junior staff, and serving as a key technical resource under the guidance of senior leadership. The ideal candidate brings robust analytical skills, a proven track record in transportation engineering or planning, and a strong capability in leveraging data and emerging technologies to solve complex transportation challenges. This position offers significant opportunity for professional growth, client interaction, and leadership within NCDOT project delivery, environmental planning, and innovative decision-support tools.

The Impact You'll Make:

  • Serve as technical lead, major task lead, and possibly deputy project manager on public sector Transportation Projects
  • Guide multi-disciplinary teams in delivery of transportation projects
  • Execute and deliver high-quality work products, on schedule
  • Coordinate with clients, resource/regulatory agencies, subcontractors, and technical staff in a confident and professional manner.
  • Lead GIS analysis and the preparation of GIS graphics
  • Preparation of visuals for presentation of project information
  • Public involvement and multi-agency stakeholder meetings in support of project work
  • Provide research and analysis for transportation projects
  • Develop client relationships and perform business development functions if necessary
  • Stay current on the latest transportation planning subject matter, policies, regulations, and techniques.
  • Serve as a Local, Regional and National resource for Egis transportation planning projects
  • Occasional travel may be required depending on project-specific requirements.

Project Management & Deliverable Support

  • Ensure all technical reports, figures, tables, and presentations meet the highest professional and clarity standards.
  • Coordinate directly with Project Managers, clients, and agency representatives to meet strict deadlines and budget constraints.
  • Mentor and guide junior engineers and planners, providing technical QA/QC on their tasks and workflows.
  • Maintain meticulous project documentation consistent with firm QA/QC standards.

The Expertise You'll Bring:

  • 5+ years of experience working in the transportation planning field.
  • AICP Certification (preferred)
  • Exceptional writing and verbal skills, specifically with planning documents
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and work with a collaborative team
  • Strong communication and research skills
  • Experience coordinating with clients, stakeholder agencies, and the general public
  • Proficiency with technical writing, communication software, technology (GIS software), and tools.
  • Completion of degree in Transportation planning, Natural Resources, Urban planning, or related field
  • Agency Experience: Proven track record working on NCDOT, MPO, or North Carolina municipal transportation projects.

Professional Attributes

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to convey technical concepts clearly.
  • Self-motivated with the ability to manage tasks efficiently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Collaborative team player who enjoys working across disciplines and seniority levels.
  • Intellectual curiosity and an eagerness to learn new tools, methods, and technologies.

title: Aviation Operations and Compliance Specialist
description:
*** Unable to provide sponsorship at this time. Only considering persons eligible to work in the United States.


Global Support and Development (GSD) is hiring a full-time Aviation Operations and Compliance Specialist based in Charlotte, N.C.


In this high-impact role, you’ll direct critical air movements, manage charter networks, and ensure strict FAA compliance to transport vital relief personnel and up to 10,000 lbs of emergency cargo directly into disaster-affected regions across the Caribbean and Central America. If you bring 5+ years of aviation operations experience, strong FAA knowledge, and a passion for rapid-response humanitarian action, apply today to pilot logistics where they matter most!


GSD offers a comprehensive benefits package to include:

  • Up to 25 days of accrued vacation
  • Up to 80 hours of annual sick leave
  • Up to 80 hours of Military Pay and 30 Days Differential
  • Medical, Dental and Vision (GSD covers monthly premium)
  • Group Life and AD&D Coverage (GSD covers monthly premium)
  • Retirement (Pre and Post Tax Options) and a Company Match
  • Matches on Qualified 529 Plans
  • Up to 14 Paid Holidays

Want to know more? Read on to learn more about the role.


PURPOSE OF POSITION:


Aviation Regulatory Compliance Specialist works with and for the Senior Manager of Aviation to meet the aviation needs of GSD. This includes vendor coordination and management, ensuring operations comply with aviation regulations, and coordination with vendors to meet safety, legal, and insurance thresholds for GSD. This position directly supports the safe transport of GSD personnel and equipment within the Caribbean and Central America.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:


  1. Support the development, implementation, and execution of aviation policy, plans, processes, and projects in support of departmental strategy, maximizing efficient use of resources and ensuring shared vision;
  2. Work collaboratively with peers and cross functionally to achieve org outcomes;
  3. Support critical decision-making processes, to include identifying issues and driving problem-solving, especially in resource-constrained and time-sensitive contexts;
  4. Maintain a network of charter operators in the Caribbean and Central America, with a focus on maintaining current master service agreements, vendor insurance minimums, non-disclosure agreements, and statements of work;
  5. Coordinate aviation training for GSD personnel in both the maritime and land environments;
  6. Interface between vendors, insurers, and legal departments to in order to coordinate agreements for services;
  7. Coordinate for aerial movement of personnel and equipment, as well as for aerial cargo movement up to 10,000 lbs;
  8. Plan aviation support, schedule operations, and interface with aviation vendors;
  9. Receive invoices and follow up to confirm payments for services provided to GSD;
  10. Conduct flight coordination (scheduling and synchronizing of flights in support of response personnel and cargo movement);
  11. Generate and process permits for aviation operations in the Caribbean and Central America;
  12. Prompt and action GSD’s core values of accountability, humility, and integrity in all work we conduct;
  13. Promote good stewardship of financial and other resources to achieve maximum benefit to those impacted by disaster or at risk of impact; and
  14. Perform other duties as assigned.


QUALIFICATIONS:

Required Experience:

  • Five (5) or more years of relevant experience in aviation operations, preferably in the humanitarian sector and preferably with fixed wing aircraft;
  • Three (3) or more years experience operating in support of aviation operations within an international context, including with small operators, preferably in connection to the humanitarian field;
  • Understanding of documentation required for air cargo or air passenger transport;
  • Understanding of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) related to aviation (specifically Parts 91, 133, 135 and special permits);
  • Working knowledge of aviation safety management system and risk management;
  • Working knowledge of ICAO regulations, aviation regulations, and the air charter market in the LAC Region;
  • Experience working at or contracting with charter aircraft operations (FAA part 135), and aviation insurance, preferred;
  • Experience and familiarization with aviation operations (and/or contracting) specific to maritime fields, ideally within the Caribbean and/or Central America preferred; and
  • Experience with aerial HAZMAT transportation and inspections, aviation law, familiarization with UAS, FAA instrument ratings, and rotary and fixed wing experience, preferred.


Required Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in air operations, air traffic management, maritime aviation operations, aviation business administration or relevant field; or
  • Equivalent experience and training in aviation operations.

Desired Professional Licenses/Certifications:

  • FAA private, commercial, or airline transport pilot (ATP)desired; and
  • FAA part 107 certification desired.


Knowledge/Skills:

  • Proven ability to produce quality results within challenging timeframes and ongoing change;
  • Ability to support the development of programmatic policy, procedure, and guidelines;
  • Ability to coordinate multiple projects simultaneously under pressure;
  • Confident and effective written and verbal communication, to include presentation ability;
  • Cultural awareness and the ability to work collaboratively with a wide array of stakeholders to build relationships;
  • Ability to work with external partners to coordinate with GSD mission activity;
  • Discernment for confidentiality in relation to organizational, partner, and donor activities and communications;
  • Proven experience supporting the development of programs preferred;
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to rapidly shift tasks;
  • Experience working and/or traveling domestically and internationally; and
  • Working knowledge of Spanish and/or French desired.


WORKING CONDITIONS AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • At this time, GSD is not offering sponsorship and is only accepting applications from persons eligible to work in the United States; and
  • Routine domestic and international travel up to 30% is required.


Working Conditions


  • May be regularly exposed to and required to work in varying outdoor weather conditions, including extreme heat or cold, heavy rainfall, and other extreme weather events;
  • May be required to engage in irregular travel and / or work schedules, which may include extended hours exceeding 8 hours in a day, including holidays/weekends/evenings, and overnight travel requirements;
  • While wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) some of which is required and may be provided by GSD:
    • Work may be conducted near moving mechanical parts, which could include exposure to loud noises;
    • Work may be conducted near and include potential exposure to fumes, airborne particles, and toxic or caustic chemicals; or
    • Work may be conducted in areas that include exposure to the risk of electrical shock or vibration.
  • Ability to obtain necessary travel documents and fulfill any other travel requirements (including an active passport, visa requirements, vaccinations, etc.);
  • This role may include deployments to support natural disaster response efforts within hazardous environments (economically/environmentally) in pre and post disaster scenarios which could include, among other conditions: lack of access to medical care, exposure to critical incidents (including severe injury, death, traumatic encounters, and/or mental strain), and uncommon sleeping arrangements (i.e. not in a hotel, could include close living quarters and cohabitation);
  • GSD’s nutritional environment contains milk, eggs, peanuts, tree nuts, fish, shellfish, soy, and wheat products. Ability to make dietary accommodations may be limited. Potential exposure to food borne allergens;
  • Employees may be required for this role to work upon our humanitarian vessel for up to 30 consecutive days. The vessel’s working environment entails performing in conditions inherent to vessel travel, including but not limited to: steep and narrow stairs and living spaces, close quarters including cohabitation, sharp surfaces, metal gangways and ladders, heavy doors, European-type plugs and wiring (220-240v, 60Hz) which cannot support all American appliances, in addition to bright and flashing lights, loud noises, nuts and shellfish exposure, poor weather, movements which can trigger motion sickness, and / or limited access to hospital / definitive care. This setting involves various sea conditions, including but not limited to rough seas, adverse weather, and potential for sea sickness;
  • At this time, GSD is not offering sponsorship and is only accepting applications from persons eligible to work in the United States; and
  • Routine domestic and international travel up to 30% is required


Physical Demands


  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position (sitting or standing) for 50% of the time;
  • Ability to regularly engage in manual dexterity;
  • [FOR VESSEL] Essential physical requirements (depending on job description requirements) may also include climbing, balancing, reaching or stretching, stooping, kneeling, crouching, crawling;
  • Ability to frequently carry materials weighing up to 30 pounds for various needs;
  • Ability to observe details at a close range (within a few feet of the observer), and the ability to communicate information and ideas so that others will understand (must also be able to exchange accurate information in these situations);
  • Specific vision abilities include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.


This job description reflects an assignment of essential functions. It does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Other duties and tasks may be assigned to this job at GSD’s discretion.


Work Authorization Requirements: GSD participates in E-verify, an internet-based system that allows employers to determine the eligibility of their employees to work in the United States. E-Verify is administered by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security and the Social Security Administration. Our participation in E-Verify is in compliance with federal law and is limited to the use of E-Verify for employment eligibility verification only. title: Ministeriet for Samfundssikkerhed og Beredskab søger skarp konsulent
description:
Vil du være med til at styrke Danmarks samfundssikkerhed og beredskab? Og ønsker du at bidrage til ministerbetjening og til at omsætte politiske aftaler til konkret handling, der styrker samfundets kriseberedskab?

Om Ministeriet for Samfundssikkerhed og Beredskab
Ministeriet for Samfundssikkerhed og Beredskab har i tæt samarbejde med relevante sektorer ansvaret for at forebygge, modstå og håndtere større ulykker, kriser, katastrofer og andre hændelser, der udfordrer samfundets grundlæggende funktioner – uanset om det drejer sig om cyberangreb, sabotage, spionage eller ekstreme vejrhændelser. Ambitionen er at samtænke beredskab, krisestyring og robustgørelse på tværs af sektorer, så vores samfund står stærkere – både til hverdag og under kriser.

Ministeriet består af departementet og to faglige styrelser: Styrelsen for Samfundssikkerhed og Beredskabsstyrelsen.

Om stillingen
Ministeriet for Samfundssikkerhed og Beredskab søger en erfaren konsulent til Kontoret for Beredskab på land og til havs (BERED). Du vil i BERED blive en del af et kontor, der arbejder med et område med stor politisk bevågenhed, og som er i rivende udvikling. Du får en varieret arbejdsdag med faglige udfordringer, gode kolleger og en uformel tone.

BERED løser en række opgaver vedrørende det operative beredskab til lands og til vands, herunder bl.a. Beredskabsstyrelsen, de kommunale redningsberedskaber, kystredning, havmiljøberedskabet og sikker sejlads og beredskabssamarbejdet inden for Kongeriget Danmark.

BERED arbejder herudover bl.a. med rammerne for beredskabsplanlægning på tværs af myndigheder og med civilbeskyttelse, dvs. hvordan vi bedst beskytter befolkningen i forbindelse med katastrofer, kriser og i værste fald krig.

Sammen med ministeriets underliggende styrelser omsætter vi politiske aftaler til konkret handling, der skal gøre det danske samfund mere beredt på kriser.

Dine opgaver vil blandt andet kunne omfatte:

  • Ministerbetjening, herunder udarbejdelse af folketingsbesvarelser, svar på henvendelser fra interessenter mv.
  • Udarbejdelse af politiske beslutningsoplæg, herunder regeringssager til bl.a. Koordinationsudvalget og Økonomiudvalget
  • Lovforberedende arbejde og tværministerielle høringer
  • Koordination af tværgående opgaver og samarbejde på tværs af ministeriet, myndigheder og organisationer
  • Bidrag til den faglige udvikling af ministeriets opgaveløsning
  • Bidrage til den faglige sparring med kolleger
Du vil som konsulent i Ministeriet for Samfundssikkerhed og Beredskab ligeledes kunne varetage andre opgaver inden for ministeriets ansvarsområde.

Om dig

Vi leder efter en kollega, der kan tænke analytisk, udvikling og formidle klart, samt kan trives i en rolle, hvor man skal navigere mellem mange interessenter og hensyn.

Du har derudover en relevant videregående uddannelse, f.eks. cand.jur eller cand.scient.pol og et højt akademisk fagligt niveau. Det vil være en fordel, hvis du har erfaring med og/eller indsigt i beredskabs- og krisestyringsområdet i Danmark, herunder de centrale aktører (som f.eks. politiet, forsvaret og redningsberedskabet) samt de rammer og regler, de arbejder inden for.

Vi tilbyder et udfordrende job tæt på den politiske beslutningsproces. Din arbejdsdag vil være præget af stor variation og fagligt udfordrende opgaver. Der vil være perioder med travlhed, hvorfor fleksibilitet og evnen til at håndtere korte deadlines er nødvendig.

Vi lægger desuden vægt på, at du:

  • Er ambitiøs, har politisk forståelse samt en interesse for sikkerhedspolitik
  • Er en stærk samarbejdspartner, der kan skabe gode relationer både internt og eksternt
  • Har veludviklede analytiske evner og kan omsætte komplekse problemstillinger til konkrete beslutningsoplæg
  • Kommunikerer klart og præcist – både skriftligt og mundtligt
  • Trives i et miljø med høj faglighed og varierede arbejdsopgaver
  • Kan holde overblik over og skabe fremdrift i en bred vifte af opgaver
  • Har erfaring fra og indsigt i Centraladministrationen, herunder via arbejde i et departement eller styrelse og derfor kender proces- og arbejdsgange.
Afhængigt af kandidaters profiler kan det komme på tale at ansætte to konsulenter.

Ansættelsesvilkår
Ansættelse og aflønning sker i henhold til den til enhver tid gældende overenskomst mellem staten og Akademikerne (AC-overenskomsten), og indplacering kan afhængig af erfaring ske som special- eller chefkonsulent.

Stillingen er på fuld tid.

Forventet tiltrædelse er 1. december 2026 eller snarest muligt derefter.

Det er en forudsætning for ansættelsen, at du kan sikkerhedsgodkendes.

Ansættelsesområdet er Ministeriet for Samfundssikkerhed og Beredskab med tilhørende institutioner.

Tjenestestedet er indtil videre departementet, Slotsholmsgade 12

Vil du vide mere?

Har du spørgsmål til stillingen, kan du få yderligere oplysninger hos souschef Mette Saaby Johansen på tlf. +45 24 89 82 46 vedr. stilling i BERED.

Din ansøgning
Send din ansøgning, CV og eksamensbevis senest den 14. oktober 2026. Du søger stillingen ved at klikke på ”Søg stillingen” i opslaget og udfylde ansøgningsformularen.

Vi forventer at holde samtaler i uge 43 og 44.

Ministeriet for Samfundssikkerhed og Beredskab opfordrer alle interesserede uanset race, hudfarve, religion eller tro, politisk anskuelse, seksuel orientering, kønsidentitet, kønsudtryk eller kønskarakteristika, alder, handicap eller national, social eller etnisk oprindelse til at søge.

title: **Internal Posting Only** Gateway Transition Coordinator
description:
SUMMARY DESCRIPTION:

The Gateway Transition Coordinator is responsible for the initial response to the referral, completion of the Return to Community Assessment (RTCA) and Options Counseling, obtaining Gateway to Community Living (GCL) Informed Consent, and initiating the Individual Transition Plan (ITP) under the Alabama Community Living (ACL) Medicaid Waiver Home and Community-based Services Program (HCBS) within the SARPC area and surrounding counties following specific requirements as set out in ACT Medicaid Waiver guidelines.


SUPERVISORY CONTROLS:

Receives general supervision from the Medicaid Waiver Coordinator. Supervisor sets the overall objectives and employee and supervisor, in consultation, develop the deadlines, projects, and work to be done; employee is responsible for planning and carrying out the assignment; and work is reviewed only from an overall standpoint.


RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES:
1. Serve as the first line for individuals who seek to transition from an institutionalized care settingback into the community under the Alabama Community Transitions (ACT) Waiver / Gateway toCommunity Living (GCL).
2. Responsible for initial response to the referral, completion of the Return to CommunityAssessment (RCA), Options Counseling, and obtaining GCL Informed Consent.
3. Initiate the Individual Transition Plan (ITP) through a person-centered process, ensure the waiverPlan of Care is integrated into the ITP, and is responsible for overall tracking of the ITP throughcompletion of implementation.
4. Work closely with the participant, the nursing facility discharge planner, and the waiver casemanager to monitor and facilitate the overall implementation of the ITP and its projectedtimeframes.
5. Ensure the GCL Office is informed of projected move/transition dates in a timely manner andensure completion of a Quality of Life (QoL) Survey is completed by the local Ombudsman.
6. Market and perform outreach regarding the ACT Waiver and transition procedures to include onevisit monthly to every regional facility.
7. Ensure compliance with state and federal standards and regulations.
8. Attend conferences, seminars, and other continuing education programs as required.
9. Other duties as required.


KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES REQUIRED:
1. Knowledge of social work programs and processes preferred.
2. Knowledge of community resources and support network available to clientele served.

3.Excellent communication skills, both orally and written.

4.Excellent organizational and time management skills.

5.Ability to relate to the elderly and their unique problems. Working knowledge of Medicaid eligibility and Nursing Home requirements preferred.

6.Knowledge and ability to operate office equipment including telephone, copy machine, fax machine, computer, and calculator.

7.Knowledge and ability to do basic arithmetic.

8.Ability to read and interpret guidelines and regulations and apply them to the job.

9.Bachelor’s Degree from an accredited four-year college or university in Social Work, Behavioral Sciences, Psychology, Geriatric Studies, or a related field. At least one (1) year of case management experience.

10.A valid driver’s license and a good driving record.


WORK CONDITIONS:
The work requires some physical exertion such as long periods of standing; walking over rough, uneven, or rocky surfaces; recurring bending, crouching, stooping, stretching, reaching, or similar activities; recurring lifting of moderately heavy items such as furniture, home goods, etc. This position requires driving on a regular basis.

None

This position will also be responsible to complete initial assessments on reports of child abuse/neglect and establish safety plans based on needs identified from the family assessment. This position will arrange for and/or coordinate needed services. This position will start as a Protection and Safety Trainee. After the completion of the State HHS pre-service training, and 90 day Probation, may be promoted to Protection and Safety Worker.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES and/or RESPONSIBILITIES include the following:

  • Handle Intake calls/reports of child abuse and/or neglect.

  • Assess risk and develop risk assessments findings.

  • Conduct family assessments and home studies.
  • Maintain daily data entry for each case.

  • Educating the community through community presentations

title: Associate Director, Strategic Insights
description:
Reporting to the Head of Strategy & Corporate Development, the Associate Director, Strategic Insights will serve as an analytical engine for Attovia Therapeutics, Inc. The role spans competitive intelligence (CI), commercial assessment and forecasting, cross-functional strategic initiatives, etc., with priorities shifting based on the company’s needs in a given quarter.

Attovia is advancing multiple programs in a public company operating environment while building the infrastructure that will carry the portfolio toward later-stage development and commercialization. The person in this seat will work across that agenda, leading CI capture and synthesis while supporting opportunity assessment, indication and portfolio decisions, and materials prepared for executives and external audiences. This is a hands-on role in a lean organization, with direct exposure to company leaders and the strategic questions the company is actively working through.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the capture and delivery of CI spanning competitor programs, targets, and modalities, drawing on congresses, publications, trial registries, regulatory actions, company disclosures, and analyst commentary, and serve as the company's internal reference point on competitor pipelines, trial designs, data readouts, and disclosed strategy
  • Translate competitive developments and broader industry trends in immunology into implications for portfolio strategy, indication sequencing, clinical development benchmarking, and partnering posture, and carry those implications through to actionable recommendations
  • Own the assumption base underlying commercial forecasts across new and existing indications, working with company leadership and external consultants
  • Own the use of AI and LLM tooling for CI, identifying and applying opportunities to improve information capture, structuring, and searchability of the knowledge base
  • Design and guide primary research across KOL/HCP, payor, and patient audiences, and secondary research across analyst reports, publications, claims data, etc.
  • Support company leadership on high-priority cross-functional initiatives and on external facing materials for partners, investors, analysts, etc.

Qualifications

  • Strong scientific foundation in molecular/cellular biology, with the ability to read primary literature, interpret discovery/preclinical and clinical trial data, and hold technical discussions
  • An advanced degree (PhD, MD) with 3+ years of experience in a strategy and/or insights function at a therapeutics company, or at a top-tier life sciences strategy consulting firm, venture capital firm, or life sciences equity research group
  • Demonstrated experience across competitive positioning, market sizing, revenue forecasting, and due diligence
  • Qualitative and quantitative market research capability, with the financial modeling skill to build the underlying analyses and the storytelling judgment to distill them into clear presentation materials with a defensible narrative
  • Demonstrated proficiency with AI and LLM tools to accelerate research and analysis workflows, and strong interest in building or deploying custom tools to enhance how a function operates
  • Clear and concise written and verbal communication, adaptable to relevant stakeholder audiences (e.g., executives, investors, KOLs, scientists)
  • Comfort operating across multiple functions and workstreams at once, with the project management discipline to hold deadlines through ambiguity
  • Based in or relocating to the San Francisco Bay Area

About Attovia

Attovia™ is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing next-generation biotherapeutics for immune-mediated diseases with high unmet need. Our product candidates are internally discovered using our proprietary ATTOBODY™ platform, an evolution-driven, high-throughput biologics platform that enables the rapid discovery and creation of diverse biparatopic complex biologics. Our pipeline spans chronic pruritic diseases, inflammatory skin diseases, inflammatory bowel disease, and other immune-mediated conditions.

Our values define how we make decisions, work with one another, and pursue our mission:

  • Teamwork & Collaboration: We communicate openly, debate constructively, mentor and learn from one another, and recognize that our strongest results come from working together

We take pride in fostering a strong team and dynamic work environment, and we are seeking individuals who align with our values and contribute to a positive and impactful workplace.

title: Shipper/Reciever
description:
About Charm
Our mission is to return the atmosphere to 280 ppm CO₂. We convert excess inedible biomass into carbon-rich bio-oil and inject it into underground storage for permanent carbon removal. At scale, we can use bio-oil to make fossil-free iron.
Our carbon removal efforts began in 2020 with initial purchases from customers like Stripe, Shopify, and Microsoft. Since then, we’ve scaled to thousands of tons of carbon removal, grown to over a hundred employees, and established three locations in San Francisco, Colorado, and Louisiana.
We're expanding our team of ambitious, creative, and hands-on problem solvers. We value psychological safety, collaboration, and continuous learning. We take calculated risks and treat mistakes as opportunities to improve. If you're excited about tackling big challenges, we encourage you to explore our company values.
Come help us reverse climate change. Gigatons or bust!

About the Role

As a Shipping & Receiving Specialist, you will be responsible for managing the day-to-day flow of materials, parts, and freight across the site, ensuring inbound and outbound shipments are received, inspected, documented, stored, and delivered accurately and efficiently. You will receive general parts and materials into NetSuite, inspect incoming goods for accuracy and condition, and ensure inventory is properly stocked and available to Operations, Engineering, and Facilities teams.

You will coordinate inbound freight, dock appointments, carrier access, and on-site pickups and drop-offs, working closely with internal teams to ensure shipments have the appropriate information and documentation. You will also prepare outbound shipments by verifying carriers, freight class, dimensions, weights, and shipping documentation before release. This role will support domestic and international FedEx shipments, including preparing commercial and packing documentation when required.

A key part of the role is maintaining accurate material flow and inventory control throughout the site. You will be responsible for processing material transfers between receiving, staging, storage, kitting, production, and shipping locations while maintaining organized dock and staging areas to prevent materials from becoming mixed, lost, or unprocessed.

You will maintain detailed shipping and receiving records to support supplier and customer traceability, including proof of delivery and documentation for freight damage, shortages, overages, and concealed damage. When issues arise, you will gather receiving evidence and escalate them to the appropriate teams.

In addition to shipping and receiving responsibilities, this role will provide support to the Facilities team by assisting with Facilities work orders and site-related tasks as needed. This may include helping with general site maintenance, material movement, inventory organization, setup and teardown activities, and other day-to-day Facilities needs. The ability to shift between warehouse, shipping and receiving, and Facilities responsibilities based on site priorities will be an important part of the role.

Success in this role requires strong attention to detail, organization, communication, and the ability to prioritize competing requests while keeping materials and site operations moving efficiently in a fast-paced environment.

You Bring

You Bring

  • Experience in shipping, receiving, warehouse, logistics, inventory, or a related operational environment

title: Total Rewards & HR Operations Leader
description:
Total Rewards & HR Operations Leader

Location: Torrance, CA (corporate headquarters), on-site 3–4 days per week
Reports to: Chief Human Resources Officer
Compensation: $200,000–$225,000 base + 25% bonus + equity

About the Company

Our client is a highly profitable, fast-growing food manufacturer with approximately 2,500 employees, producing sushi in manufacturing facilities for some of the largest retail partners in North America, including Costco. With strong financial footing and demand that exceeds current production capacity, the company is positioned for significant growth.

Operations span corporate headquarters in Torrance, CA; Houston, TX; roughly 700 employees in Canada; and a presence in Australia, along with franchise operations that require HR oversight.

The company is centralizing HR and building the function largely from scratch under a newly hired CHRO. This is a rare opportunity to shape the people infrastructure of a profitable business at an inflection point.

The Opportunity

As the CHRO's right hand, the Total Rewards & HR Operations Leader will assess what exists today and build, from the ground up, every function they own: benefits, compensation, HRIS, and payroll. This leader will be the bridge between HR and the CFO and finance team, turning people data into insight for headcount planning, reporting, and people analytics.

This role is for a builder and creator who thrives in ambiguity and complexity and wants to design scalable systems that support high growth across multiple countries and business models.

What You'll Do

Total Rewards Strategy

  • Build a unified total rewards strategy across U.S., Canadian, and Australian operations that supports growth, competitiveness, and cost discipline.
  • Partner with the CHRO to evaluate current programs, identify gaps, and set a multi-year roadmap.

Benefits (expert level)

  • Serve as the company's benefits subject-matter expert, overseeing health and welfare, retirement, leave, and wellbeing programs.
  • Evaluate plan design, funding, broker and vendor relationships, and compliance across all locations and countries.
  • Drive consolidation and optimization of benefit programs as HR centralizes.

Compensation

  • Design and implement compensation structures, including job architecture, salary ranges, market pricing, and incentive plans.
  • Lead merit and bonus cycles and ensure pay practices are equitable, compliant, and aligned with business goals.

HRIS & Systems

  • Own the HR technology strategy. The company runs ADP across all sites, but under separate contracts, and this leader will consolidate and optimize those contracts or evaluate alternative platforms.
  • Build an integrated HR data stack that connects HRIS, payroll, benefits, and finance systems.
  • Explore opportunities for automation and AI-enabled tools to improve efficiency and employee experience.

Payroll Oversight

  • Oversee the payroll team and processes across all entities and countries, ensuring accuracy, compliance, and scalability.
  • Standardize payroll practices and controls as the organization centralizes.

People Analytics & Finance Partnership

  • Partner closely with the CFO and finance team on headcount planning, labor cost modeling, budgeting, and reporting.
  • Build people analytics capabilities that give leadership clear, reliable data for decision-making, including workforce metrics tied to manufacturing productivity and growth.

HR Operations & Franchise Oversight

  • Build HR operations infrastructure (policies, processes, and service delivery) to support a centralized model.
  • Provide total rewards and HR operations oversight for franchise operations.
  • Lead and develop a team across benefits, compensation, HRIS, and payroll.

What You Bring

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in total rewards and HR operations, including leadership of benefits, compensation, HRIS, and payroll.
  • Expert-level benefits knowledge, including plan design, vendor management, funding strategies, and compliance.
  • Strong financial acumen and comfort partnering with finance on budgets, forecasting, and cost modeling.
  • Deep HR systems and data expertise: a strong understanding of data stacks and HR technology. ADP experience is highly preferred.
  • Track record of building HR functions or programs from scratch in complex, ambiguous, high-growth environments.
  • Experience with multi-country operations (U.S., Canada, Australia) is a strong plus.
  • Experience in manufacturing, food production, or multi-site/franchise environments is a plus.
  • Bachelor's degree required; CCP, CEBS, or related certifications preferred.

Why This Role

  • Build a function from the ground up alongside a new CHRO, with executive visibility and direct partnership with finance.
  • Join a profitable company with real growth ahead, backed by major retail partnerships.
  • Competitive package: $200K–$225K base, 25% bonus, and equity.

title: Senior Director, Program Management
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

The Senior Director, Program Management is a senior cross-functional leader responsible for helping move complex drug development programs from strategy to execution.

This role works across clinical, regulatory, CMC, nonclinical, commercial and other functions to connect plans, build and maintain the integrated program timeline, identify risks and trade-offs, prepare for key decisions, and drive follow-through.

The Senior Director must understand drug development well enough to contribute meaningfully to program discussions, challenge assumptions, and help the team understand the implications of different choices. At the same time, this person must be strong in the core mechanics of program management, including timelines, dependencies, risks, decisions, actions and execution.

The role reports to the Vice President, Program Management.

Employees designated as onsite or hybrid are expected to be onsite at Rigel’s South San Francisco headquarters during business hours on Wednesdays and Thursdays each week. Employees designated as remote are expected to be onsite during business hours on Wednesdays and Thursdays at least twice per month, and more frequently as business needs require.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Program Planning and Leadership

  • Develop a strong understanding of the program’s objectives, development strategy and key scientific, clinical, regulatory, CMC and commercial considerations.
  • Partner with functional leaders to translate agreed program strategy into an integrated and executable plan.
  • Lead integration of functional plans, assumptions and dependencies across the program.
  • Build, own and maintain the integrated program timeline, including key milestones, decision points, critical paths and cross-functional dependencies.
  • Work with functional leaders to obtain, challenge and confirm the assumptions, durations and dependencies underlying the timeline.
  • Identify gaps, conflicts and trade-offs across functional plans and help drive them to resolution.
  • Develop integrated scenarios and timelines when alternative development paths are being considered.

Execution and Risk Management

  • Monitor progress against the integrated plan and identify material changes in timing, scope, resources or assumptions.
  • Assess and communicate the impact of changes on the broader program.
  • Identify major program risks early and work with accountable functions to ensure mitigation or contingency plans are in place.
  • Drive clear actions, owners and timelines following key discussions and decisions.
  • Ensure decisions are reflected in updated plans and follow-through.
  • Escalate unresolved issues when they cannot be addressed within the program.

Decision Support

  • Anticipate upcoming program decisions and ensure the right information is available to support them.
  • Help clearly define the decision needed, relevant assumptions, options, risks and execution implications.
  • Distinguish between facts, assumptions, risks and unresolved questions.
  • Ensure functional input is aligned and areas of disagreement are clear before major decisions are brought forward.
  • Prepare concise program updates for senior leadership and governance discussions.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Build strong working relationships across functions and levels.
  • Facilitate productive discussion when priorities, timelines or perspectives differ.
  • Ask informed questions and challenge assumptions constructively.
  • Maintain focus on the overall program rather than any one functional perspective.
  • Drive cross-functional execution while keeping functional accountability clear.
  • Ensure material changes are communicated to affected stakeholders.
  • When assigned broader program leadership responsibility, lead the cross-functional development program and advance integrated program recommendations for decision.

Financial and Resource Planning

  • Partner with Finance and functional leaders to connect development plans with budgets and forecasts.
  • Ensure planning assumptions used for financial work are consistent with the current program timeline.
  • Identify changes in scope, timing or resources that may materially affect program cost or investment needs.
  • Highlight resource constraints and their potential impact on program execution.

Program Management Leadership

  • Apply consistent Program Management practices across assigned programs.
  • Identify practical ways to improve planning, execution, decision-making and communication.
  • Mentor and provide guidance to Program Management colleagues and consultants.
  • Contribute to broader portfolio, alliance and cross-functional work as needed.
  • Support the continued development of the Program Management function.

Role Accountability

  • Leading integration of the cross-functional development plan.
  • Building, owning and maintaining the integrated program timeline.
  • Connecting functional assumptions and dependencies across the program.
  • Driving cross-functional planning, execution and follow-through.
  • Identifying and communicating major risks, trade-offs and changes.
  • Preparing the team and leadership for key decisions.
  • Ensuring decisions are reflected in updated plans and actions.
  • Providing clear and concise program-level communication.
  • Resolution of broader organizational issues that extend beyond an individual program.

Leadership Expectations

  • Understand the development context, not just the project mechanics.
  • Connect strategy with execution.
  • Bring structure and clarity to complex or ambiguous situations.
  • Anticipate risks and decision needs.
  • Challenge assumptions constructively.
  • Communicate clearly with senior scientific, medical, technical and business leaders.
  • Drive accountability without taking ownership away from accountable functions.
  • Exercise sound judgment in a dynamic biotechnology environment.
  • Be capable of leading a cross-functional development program when needed.

KNOWLEDGE AND SKILL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Bachelor's degree in a scientific, technical, business or related discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
  • Typically, 12+ years of relevant biotech or pharma industry experience.
  • Significant experience in cross-functional drug development and Program Management.
  • Demonstrated experience independently managing complex development programs across multiple functions and development stages.
  • Strong understanding of the drug development process and the relationships among clinical, regulatory, CMC, nonclinical, commercial and operational activities.
  • Demonstrated experience building and managing integrated development timelines.
  • Experience supporting major development decisions, scenario planning and senior leadership or governance reviews.
  • Ability to contribute credibly to complex drug development discussions beyond project management mechanics.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, facilitation and communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with senior functional leaders without relying on positional authority.
  • Experience mentoring or guiding other Program Management professionals preferred.
  • Prior experience serving in a Program Team Lead, development team lead or equivalent cross-functional leadership role preferred.

Measures of Success

Success in this role means the program has a clear integrated plan, a credible timeline, visible risks and dependencies, timely decisions, clear accountability and disciplined follow-through. Success means the program team and senior leadership have a clear view of where the program stands, what has changed, what decisions are coming, what could affect execution and who owns the next step.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

The anticipated salary range for this position is $270,000 to $325,000. The actual salary offered will depend on several factors, including experience, qualifications, geographic location, internal equity, and business needs.

This position is eligible to participate in Rigel's annual bonus program and is eligible for equity incentive awards, subject to the terms of the applicable plans. This position is not commission-based.

Rigel offers eligible employees a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage; life and disability insurance; flexible spending accounts; a 401(k) plan; paid time off; paid company holidays; and other benefits.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

  • PHYSICAL DEMANDS: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is required to stand, walk; sit; talk and hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and the ability to adjust focus.
  • WORK ENVIRONMENT: The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Some travel may be required.

Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by the law.

title: Director of Community Engagement
description:
Candidates must live in Columbus, Ohio to be considered for this position.

POSITION OVERVIEW

Navita Health is expanding across Ohio, and we are seeking an experienced, high-impact Director of Community Engagement to lead our growth initiatives in the Columbus region and surrounding markets.

This hybrid leadership role bridges high-level strategic partner development, community outreach, and sales operational management. The Director of Community Engagement will oversee local growth efforts, manage and empower outreach/sales personnel, establish high-value partnerships, and drive service utilization for behavioral health and substance use disorder recovery services. As the face of Navita Health, in the region, you will play a pivotal role in expanding our footprint, building community trust, and ensuring team alignment with organizational revenue and impact goals.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Partner Development & Market Expansion

  • Territory & Market Growth: Define and execute regional growth plans; analyze market data, trends, and service gaps in Ohio’s behavioral health landscape to identify emerging opportunities.
  • Partnership Management: Identify, secure, and nurture strategic relationships with treatment centers, housing providers, healthcare networks, state/local programs, and community leaders.
  • Customized Alignment: Tailor partnership strategies to match market needs and partner goals, ensuring sustainable growth and mutually beneficial relationships.
  • Brand Representation: Serve as the primary senior contact and ambassador for internal and external partners across the Columbus market and state footprint.

Sales & Outreach Leadership

  • Team Management & Supervision: Hire, train, onboard, and lead local community engagement managers, outreach representatives, account managers, and community liaison staff in accordance with company policies and applicable laws.
  • Performance & Quotas: Establish regional outreach goals, key performance indicators (KPIs), and conversion quotas; oversee daily operations and performance of the team to achieve growth targets.
  • Budgeting & Operations: Prepare regional outreach budgets, projections, and sales/pipeline forecasts; manage expenditures and implement cost-saving measures while driving revenue.
  • Process & Compliance: Guide partners and team members on policies and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs); handle and resolve customer or partner escalations regarding services.
  • Compliance: Follow HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality, and federal and state anti-kickback and patient-brokering laws in all outreach and referral activities.

Community Engagement & Network Growth

  • Client & Provider Recruitment: Conduct targeted outreach activities to engage and recruit new clients and service providers into the Navita Health ecosystem.
  • Provider Support: Work alongside Lead Peers to support new peer recovery supporters through placement, training, certification, and credentialing processes to ensure a smooth transition to providing services.
  • Events & Advocacy: Coordinate and attend local community events, forums, panel discussions, and networking groups (educational, wellness, recovery-focused) to deepen community connection and drive awareness.
  • Board & Forum Participation: Active involvement on local community boards and advocacy groups to foster long-term trust and promote service utilization.

Key Leadership Competencies

  • Ethical Leadership & Integrity: Leads with honesty, transparency, and accountability; upholds the highest ethical standards in partner relationships, client recruitment, and referral practices; ensures all outreach and growth activities comply with healthcare regulations and reflect Navita Health's mission and values.
  • Strategic Thinking & Business Acumen: Understands the business implications of decisions; displays an orientation toward growth while aligning work with Navita Health’s mission.
  • Relationship & Sales Excellence: Proven ability to initiate new contacts, overcome objections, navigate complex healthcare landscapes, and maintain exceptional stakeholder satisfaction.
  • Team Leadership & Development: Skilled at inspiring, coaching, and managing a team to reach quantitative and qualitative metrics.
  • Cost Consciousness & Fiscal Responsibility: Operates within approved budgets, tracks expenditure, and optimizes resource allocation based on data-informed decisions.
  • Data & Reporting: Track referral sources, outreach activity and conversions in the CRM or EHR, and report monthly results to leadership.
  • Quality & Adaptability: Demonstrates thoroughness and accuracy in work; adapts strategies dynamically based on changing market conditions.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Experience

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Public Health, Healthcare Administration, or a related field (preferred; or equivalent combination of education and hands-on leadership experience).
  • Experience:
    • 4+ years of progressive experience in partnership development, community engagement, account management, or healthcare sales.
    • 2+ years in a supervisory, management, or team leadership role required.
    • Strong background in the behavioral health, mental health, or substance use disorder recovery field is strongly preferred.
    • Existing professional relationships within the Columbus healthcare community is preferred.
    • Knowledge of Ohio’s Medicaid behavioral health system and treatment programs, insurance processes and managed care plans, and referral management is preferred.
  • Licenses/Designations/Certifications:
    • Must have a valid OH Driver’s License, reliable vehicle and active auto insurance with liability coverage and have the ability to drive for extended periods of time.
    • Ohio clinical licenses or certifications are preferred, but not required.

SKILLS & REQUIREMENTS

  • Technical Proficiency: Proficient in CRM platforms (Salesforce, HubSpot), Google Suite, EHRs, and data management/analytics tools.
  • Driving & Background Requirements: Valid state driver’s license, active auto insurance, and willingness to undergo regular background and MVR checks.
  • Lived Experience / Recovery: If in personal recovery, a minimum of 5 years of continuous, verified sobriety is preferred.
  • Communication & Math Skills: Excellent written, verbal, and public speaking skills. Ability to calculate growth metrics, ROI, conversion rates, and budget projections.
  • Mission Alignment: Passion for improving lives through accessible recovery support services and a strong commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Directly supervises Ohio Community Engagement Managers and any aligned staff or contractors; including hiring, onboarding, training, performance management, and professional development for all members.
  • Ensures all team members follow company policies, SOPs, and applicable regulations, including HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2.
