title: Product Lead, Panel & Recruitment (Remote, EU/UK)
description:
About Maze

Maze is the user research platform that helps companies build the right products faster by making user insights available at the speed of product development.

In most companies, research demand far exceeds supply. Time, cost, and lack of access to expertise hold teams back. In today’s AI-powered world, anyone can build a product fast. The real challenge? Deeply understanding user needs and building the right product. That’s where Maze comes in.

We believe companies shouldn’t have to choose between building fast and building right. Maze makes research accessible, intuitive, and fast so product teams can put user insights at the center of every decision.

Our platform enables researchers, designers, and product managers to quickly recruit participants, run studies autonomously, and surface insights that actually drive product decisions. Our AI capabilities automate the busywork and add depth and direction to the insights themselves.

That’s why Maze was recently named the #1 user research platform in UX Tools’ Design Tools Survey—and why we’re scaling fast across industries like B2B SaaS, e-Commerce, Financial Services, Retail, and Automotive, supporting world class customers such as Uber, Amazon, Atlassian, Anthropic & more.

Maze is a Series B company backed by top-tier investors (Felicis, Emergence & Amplify). We operate a global remote workforce driven by our core values.

Location: Remote, preference for Netherlands, United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain or Portugal.

Key engineering and product teams are based in these locales.

About the Role

Maze customers need to reach the right participants and trust the quality of the people taking part in their studies. Recruitment is a critical part of research.

We’re looking for a Product Lead to own the recruitment and panel experience at Maze. You’ll set the product vision for how customers recruit and manage participants across Maze, working across unmoderated, moderated, AI-moderated, and future research experiences.

This is a highly cross-functional product area that sits at the intersection of product, operations, and our panel partner ecosystem. You’ll work in a trio with Engineering and Design while partnering closely with our Panel Operations team, GTM, Customer Success, Research Partners, and other product teams.

You’ll own the customer and participant experiences as well as the systems behind them, helping Maze deliver a recruitment experience that is high-quality, reliable, and able to scale with increasingly complex customer needs.

You’ll work on:

  • Set the product vision and roadmap for recruitment and participant management across Maze.

  • Improve participant quality by building stronger feedback loops, quality signals, filtering, and experiences that reduce confusion for participants.

  • Make it easier for customers to recruit the audiences they need across different study types, including more complex enterprise use cases.

  • Understand panel performance and identify gaps in participant supply, quality, and fulfillment.

  • Partner with Panel Operations to continuously improve the tools, workflows, and handoffs used to fulfill recruitment requests.

  • Help evaluate and onboard new panel partners and determine where deeper integrations can improve quality, coverage, or efficiency.

  • Develop smarter ways to route studies to the right participant supply based on customer and study needs.

  • Stay close to the operational side of recruitment so product decisions are grounded in how participant fulfillment actually happens.

  • Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Research Partners on customer needs, recruitment feasibility, packaging, adoption, and opportunities where recruitment capabilities can unlock deals.

  • Define and measure success across participant quality, fulfillment, and the overall recruitment experience.

You should apply if:

  • You have experience as a Product Lead, or equivalent, owning complex product areas from strategy through execution.

  • You’re comfortable working on products that span software, operations, and external partners rather than living entirely within a single product surface.

  • You can turn messy, cross-functional problems into a clear product vision and an actionable roadmap.

  • You’re comfortable getting close to operational workflows and using what you learn to make better product decisions.

  • You have strong product judgment and are comfortable bringing a clear recommendation to the room, even when there isn’t a perfect answer.

  • You’re experienced partnering closely with Engineering and Design while bringing stakeholders from across the business into your product process.

  • You think in systems and look for scalable product solutions rather than one-off workarounds.

  • You’re comfortable balancing customer experience, business needs, operational realities, and technical constraints.

  • You thrive in an environment where you can move quickly, make decisions with imperfect information, and continuously learn from customers and internal teams.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Experience with user research or research participant recruitment.

  • Experience building products with a meaningful operational component.

  • Marketplace or supply-and-demand product experience.

  • Experience working with external partners, vendors, or integrations that are critical to the customer experience.

  • Experience building products for enterprise customers with complex requirements.

Inclusivity and Pay

At Maze, we are dedicated to building an equitable, inclusive, and authentic workspace. Unique and diverse perspectives are welcomed, and continuous growth is encouraged. We believe that people are more than their resumes, so if your past experience looks different than the criteria listed, we'd still love to hear from you. We appreciate and celebrate non-traditional life routes and encourage you to apply should you connect with a job description or the Maze culture.

Maze values transparency and it enables us to approach compensation equitably across the world. We are informed by data and regularly check our salary ranges (either United States or Rest of World) against other venture backed companies. Additionally, we are proud of our holistic and generous benefits offerings, included in every compensation package.

Your salary is dependent upon many factors, including years of experience, expertise, etc. During your first interview, you can expect to have an open conversation with your recruiter regarding your compensation expectations.

Why Maze is unique

  • Early-stage startup: You will join an early-stage startup with less than 150 team members. This means you'll have the unique opportunity to directly impact success and help shape the future of Maze.

  • Market disruption: We believe that the way companies build products is fundamentally broken and the user research market is ripe for disruption. For too long, companies have been forced to choose between rapid development without user insights or investing months into research before bringing products to market. But there's finally a groundswell building around a path forward that eliminates this compromise - and Maze is leading the charge.

  • Product-market Fit: Maze is used by 100,000+ brands across 4,000 companies, from SMB to enterprises, and in the last fiscal year, we saw 6.5M questions answered, supporting 25K decisions

Benefits

  • Health insurance with international coverage, vision, and dental: 100% of the team member premium paid

    • For some locations, coverage options vary, please see our benefits pages for more information

  • Free access to proper mental health care, unlimited virtual therapy sessions (with a human) and 24/7 access to resources

  • Life and Disability Insurance, 100% of the team member premium paid

  • Flexible time off

  • Meaningful equity

  • Company retreats, fully paid for by Maze

  • New MacBook (laptop), paid for by Maze

  • Paid Family leave: 16 weeks for birth or adoptive parents

  • $500/month to be used for dependent health insurance coverage

    • If you don't have dependents to add to your plan, you will still get access to this money to be used at your discretion to get the benefits that matter to you with our flexible a-maze-ing benefits - gym memberships, co-working spaces, food, travel, whatever!

  • $1,500 remote work setup fund to ensure you can set up a productive work space

  • Flexible work schedule where you manage your own working hours

  • Monthly points that are awarded to others to recognize teamwork, dedication and helpfulness - points can be cashed out for gift cards and more

  • Virtual social engagements randomly throughout the year

  • SWAG, we have some really cool swag

  • Open, transparent culture that includes virtual: coffee chats, bi-weekly all-hands meetings, and more

Check out all of our a-maze-ing benefits here.

Outreach Notice

We understand you might be excited about the job you’re applying for, we are excited you are interested! However, please refrain from reaching out to our current team members on LinkedIn for referrals. Our policy is that referrals can only be provided by team members who personally know the candidate. With the high volume of interest in our roles, contacting our team members who are not involved in recruitment can be overwhelming. Additionally, please avoid submitting support tickets regarding your application, as our support team is not involved in the hiring process. Rest assured, our recruitment team is diligently reviewing all applications and will reach out directly if there is a match.

title: Agent Solutions Coordinator (Hybrid - In Office 10 days/Month)
description:
We are adding an Agent Solutions Coordinator! This is a hybrid position requiring individuals to work in office 10 days per month; or as needed for business needs.


Who We Are:

Since 1909, National Guardian Life Insurance Company (NGL) has been one of America’s most successful and highly rated independent life insurance companies. We specialize in a suite of innovative products for life’s journey, giving people the financial stability, careful guidance and peace of mind to lead a life filled with confidence, dignity and grace.

NGL's Core Values – integrity, dependability, collaboration, compassion and growth are a foundation of our company and help to build on the interactions we have with our policyholders, partners, funeral homes and each other. We believe in creating an inclusive, welcoming environment for all where diversity is celebrated, and everyone is encouraged to live their best, most authentic self. We offer Employee Resource Groups for employees to get involved, learn, network, and offer professional and personal development opportunities.

title: Resident Experience Coordinator
description:

We are currently hiring for our Inspired Living community located in Alpharetta, GA.

  • Creative, energetic, and comfortable taking the lead.
  • Ability to plan, coordinate, and manage multiple activities and events.
  • Comfortable working with residents with different abilities, interests, and personalities.

We believe life at Inspired Living should be about more than a calendar full of activities-it should be about creating experiences residents look forward to and memories they'll talk about.

title: Director of Global Executive Protection Operations

Meta is seeking an experienced security executive to lead Global Operations within our Global Security Executive Protection organization. Reporting to the Director of Executive Protection and Threat Management, this leader owns the strategy, operating model, and end-to-end delivery of executive protection operations globally — including 24/7 residential and transportation security, domestic and international executive travel, event and offsite protection, and crisis response affecting Meta's senior leadership. The successful candidate is a builder and can execute strategy— someone who exemplifies Meta's values, makes work happen with speed and simplicity, reduces complexity rather than adding to it, and develops leaders who go on to lead. They bring a high degree of discretion, sound judgment in time-sensitive, high-stakes situations, and a demonstrated record of building high-performing, healthy organizations in high-stakes environments.

title: Customer Delivery Lead
description:
Our Mission

Salt AI is building the intelligence layer for the enterprise, starting with life sciences. In a world where AI is fragmented across models, tools, and data silos, Salt unifies them through a compliance-first orchestration platform that lets regulated organizations deploy AI securely, at scale, and with confidence.

We're creating the backend systems that power real-world AI workflows across drug discovery, clinical development, and commercial operations. Our platform turns complex, regulated environments into intelligent, adaptive systems where autonomous AI agents operate in harmony with existing infrastructure.


About the Role

As a Customer Delivery Lead, you own our most strategic enterprise deployments end to end — from initial scoping through production go-live and customer self-sufficiency. Reporting to the Chief Customer Officer, you'll work with leading pharma, biotech, investment banking, and energy enterprises deploying Salt into demanding SaaS, VPC, and on-prem environments.

This is a senior, judgment-heavy role. You define what we're building, negotiate what we're not, direct the Forward Deployed Engineers and Customer Solutions Engineers assigned to your accounts, and hold the line when a customer pushes to expand scope mid-engagement. You'll keep engagement detail current in our existing AI-first project management flow (Slack → Notion → Linear), where engineers groom their own tickets — so your time goes to scoping and direction, not ticket administration.

The Role (What You'll Be Doing)

  • Scope engagements down to one or two named workflows with fixed timelines, and drive customer stakeholders to converge on them quickly.
  • Define the engagement exit before work begins: what customer self-sufficiency looks like, written down and agreed.
  • Own SOW terms and the deal scope boundary — including the authority to decline out-of-scope asks from senior customer stakeholders.
  • Run post-engagement debriefs and drive field learning back into product and platform priorities.
  • Provide and leadership, prioritization, and technical direction to the Forward Deployed Engineers and Customer Solutions Engineers assigned to your accounts.
  • Lead executive communication with customer sponsors throughout the engagement lifecycle.
  • Stay engaged after go-live on the technical outcome — adoption depth and scoping the next workflow. Sales owns the account relationship and review cadence.
  • Partner with Sales on expansion: they lead the pursuit, you control what can be committed on scope, timeline, and capacity.
  • Own the SOW Approval Gate on new and expansion business — no contract or SOW goes to a customer without your sign-off on scope, timeline, and capacity.
  • Build reusable delivery patterns — templates, integration components, and reference architectures that make each subsequent engagement faster.
  • Work with the account's Executive Advisor to bring domain expertise into scoping and validate outputs where correctness depends on it.

Requirements - Core Skills (Must Have)

  • 5+ years owning complex enterprise technical deployments end to end — as a forward deployed engineer, technical program manager, solutions architect, or delivery lead at a technical consultancy or enterprise software company.
  • Technical fluency: enough depth in cloud architecture, APIs, data pipelines, and integration patterns to scope work credibly and direct engineers without needing translation. Engineering or technical background required.
  • Scope discipline: demonstrated ability to hold a line against pressure from senior stakeholders, and the judgment to know when holding is right.
  • Written communication and document hygiene: scopes, exit criteria, and decisions live in writing, not in your head.
  • Executive presence: credible in the room with VP- and C-level customer sponsors at large enterprises.
  • Comfort with ambiguity: our customers often don't know their highest-value use case when we arrive, and finding it is part of the job.

Preferred/Bonus Skills (Nice To Have)

  • Experience with on-premise, VPC, or air-gapped deployments in regulated industries — pharma, life sciences, financial services, or government.
  • Familiarity with GxP, HIPAA, SOC 2, or similar compliance and validation frameworks.
  • Background at a company running a forward deployed engineering model.
  • Hands-on experience with AI/ML workflows, model deployment, or agent orchestration.
  • Track record turning one-off engagements into repeatable delivery motions.

What Makes You A Great Fit

  • You measure success by whether the customer is actually using what you built — not whether it shipped.
  • You'd rather say no early than deliver a bloated engagement late.
  • You're energized by walking into a messy enterprise environment and finding the one workflow that matters most.
  • You're comfortable being the most senior person in the room on delivery, and the person accountable when it goes sideways.
  • You want to build the function, not just work in it — this is the first Customer Delivery Lead at Salt, and the patterns you set become how we operate.
  • You're excited to apply your skills to AI in life sciences and support teams doing high-impact scientific work.

Perks And Benefits

  • Competitive salary based on location and experience.
  • Comprehensive health coverage, including medical, dental, mental health.
  • Fully remote role, collaborating primarily within U.S. time zones.


Based in Southern California, Salt AI is pioneering the future of life sciences with advanced AI. Founded in 2024 by Aber Whitcomb and Jim Benedetto—veterans of MySpace, Jam City, Gravity, and Core Scientific—our leadership team brings over 15 years of collaboration. We’re not just building products, but transforming what’s possible in research and discovery. We value diverse perspectives and are committed to an inclusive team. If you’re excited about shaping the future of AI in life sciences, we'd love to connect with you.

title: Staff Electrical Specialist - Hardware Test (R6122)
description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit . Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

Job Description:

Shield AI is seeking a Staff Electrical Test Engineering Specialist to build, modify, troubleshoot, and sustain the electrical test systems used to prove X-BAT hardware is reliable and mission ready. The Hardware Test Engineering team develops custom equipment for component- and system-level testing at ambient and simulated harsh environmental conditions.

This is a senior hands-on technical role focused on electrical execution and test-system readiness. You will perform complex PCBA and harness troubleshooting and rework, build and validate test equipment, design interface electronics and harnesses, support production and test operations, and lead improvements that make hardware easier to test, repair, and sustain. You will also mentor technicians and engineers, establish strong workmanship practices, and serve as a trusted escalation point for difficult electrical problems.

What success looks like:

  • Keep critical test and production equipment safe, available, calibrated, and ready when programs need it.
  • Resolve difficult electrical failures quickly and document root cause, repair, verification, and prevention clearly.
  • Deliver high-quality electrical assemblies and improve team capability through strong workmanship, standard work, training, design feedback, and configuration control.

What you'll do:

  • Build, integrate, validate, maintain, and repair electrical test systems that combine custom electronics, harnesses, instruments, controls, test computers, and mechanical fixtures.
  • Perform benchtop PCBA testing and advanced troubleshooting using schematics, assembly drawings, test procedures, and laboratory instruments.
  • Perform high-quality PCBA, cable, harness, connector, and electromechanical rework, including inspection and verification of completed repairs.
  • Design and release interface boards, simple-to-moderate PCBs, harnesses, breakout assemblies, adapters, and electrical portions of test fixtures using appropriate CAD tools.
  • Select components, connectors, wire, circuit protection, relays, switches, and instrumentation; document pinouts, bills of material, drawings, and assembly instructions.
  • Support equipment checkout, calibration, preventive maintenance, configuration control, spares, and lifecycle issues such as obsolescence and recurring failures.
  • Respond to emergent production- and test-floor issues, restore safe operation, communicate status, and ensure temporary actions are converted into durable corrective actions.
  • Partner with electrical, mechanical, software, manufacturing, quality, and test engineers in design reviews; advocate for testability, serviceability, fault isolation, and simpler rework.
  • Create and improve work instructions, checkout procedures, troubleshooting guides, inspection criteria, and safe-work practices for electrical equipment.
  • Mentor technicians and engineers, lead difficult builds and repairs, and model strong ownership, workmanship, documentation, and laboratory discipline.

Required qualifications:

  • 6+ years of hands-on electrical experience in aerospace, manufacturing, test, electronics, or a similarly rigorous hardware environment; equivalent military or trade experience is welcome.
  • Demonstrated expertise in benchtop electrical testing, PCBA troubleshooting, and root-cause isolation using oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, electronic loads, logic analyzers, and related equipment.
  • Advanced experience performing PCBA and harness assembly, modification, and rework from controlled drawings and workmanship requirements.
  • Ability to read, create, and review schematics, wiring diagrams, pinouts, assembly drawings, bills of material, and test procedures.
  • Experience designing and maintaining electrical test equipment, interface electronics, harnesses, or production fixtures through release and sustained use.
  • Working knowledge of analog and digital circuits, power distribution and protection, grounding, shielding, connectors, communications interfaces, and electrical safety.
  • A record of resolving urgent production or laboratory issues while preserving safety, quality, traceability, and configuration control, communicating clearly, and mentoring others.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Associate degree, technical certificate, military electronics training, or equivalent practical education; IPC workmanship certification or equivalent experience is valued.
  • Experience with Altium, KiCad, OrCAD, Eagle, or comparable tools and with aircraft wiring, avionics interfaces, communications, sensors, power electronics, batteries, motors, or RF systems.
  • Experience with environmental or qualification-test equipment, data-acquisition systems, programmable instruments, LabVIEW, TestStand, Python, Linux, or test computers.
  • Experience applying ESD controls, electrical safe-work practices, calibration requirements, nonconformance processes, and formal configuration management.
  • Eligibility to obtain a U.S. security clearance if required by the program.

title: Workday Systems Analyst – Finance
description:
The Workday Systems Analyst – Finance supports the design, configuration, delivery, and ongoing management of Workday Financials and related finance applications. This role partners with Finance stakeholders to translate business needs into practical system solutions, improve business processes, and maintain reliable reporting and integrations. The analyst provides production support and contributes to projects that improve the efficiency, accuracy, and scalability of Finance operations.

Responsibilities:

  • Support Workday Financials and related finance applications, including financial management, procurement, reporting, and connected business processes.

  • Partner with Finance stakeholders to gather, analyze, and document business needs, requirements, and functional specifications.

  • Evaluate current processes and workflows, identify gaps and inefficiencies, and recommend improvements that support Finance priorities.

  • Configure and maintain Workday business processes, security-related requirements, reports, calculated fields, and other functional components within the role’s scope.

  • Support integrations and data flows between Workday and adjacent finance applications; coordinate with technical teams when issues require deeper integration or engineering support.

  • Provide day-to-day production support, troubleshoot system issues, communicate resolutions, and escalate risks or defects appropriately.

  • Create, maintain, and improve scheduled and ad hoc reports using appropriate Workday reporting tools.

  • Partner with Finance and Technology Services teams to validate data accuracy, investigate reporting discrepancies, and improve data visibility.

  • Develop test plans, test cases, and acceptance criteria; execute or coordinate testing for configuration changes, integrations, reports, and system releases.

  • Support project planning and delivery for Finance systems initiatives, including requirements, process design, testing, documentation, and implementation activities.

  • Stay current on Workday releases, product capabilities, and relevant finance systems practices; identify opportunities to use new functionality to improve business processes.

  • Create and maintain functional documentation, procedures, job aids, and support materials.

  • Build effective working relationships with Finance, Accounting, Procurement, FP&A, and other cross-functional partners.

Required Qualifications:

title: Network Security Architect
description:
Position: Network Security Architect – Overall 10+yrs experience needed.

Location: NYC, NY (Hybrid- 3 days a week) – face to face is must. Look for candidate from drivable distance as f2f is must.
Duration: 6 - 12 months

Industry- Banking & Financial client
Phone Interview followed by an in-person round of interview.


Must have 13+ years of experience and must attend F2F interview.

Skills: IP routing, MPLS, BGP, SD-WAN, Wireless Network, Data Centre architecture, Palo Alto, Cisco NGFWs, SIEM, EDR, AWS, Azure, GCP, SABSA, TOGAF, COBIT, ITIL, DODAF, Automation

Ideal Candidate:
Senior Network Security Architect + strong enterprise networking/security architecture + hands-on PQC knowledge (FIPS 203/204/205) + experience assessing PQC readiness and its impact on Firewalls, WAF, NAC, Proxy, VPN/PKI and perimeter security.

Role Overview
We are looking for a Senior Network Security Architect who can design and secure large enterprise network environments across on-prem, data center, and multi-cloud platforms.
The most important differentiator for this role is Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) expertise, specifically NIST FIPS 203, FIPS 204, and FIPS 205, and how PQC impacts network security technologies.
A Network Security Architect is a senior-level IT professional responsible for planning, designing, testing, and overseeing the implementation of secure enterprise network configurations to protect an organization from cyber threats. Acting as the strategic blueprint designer, this role ensures that all local area networks (LANs), wide area networks (WANs), virtual private networks (VPNs), routers, firewalls, and cloud integrations align with business objectives and stringent security standards.
Subject Matter expert / domain specialist related to post-quantum cryptography (NIST FIPS 203, 204, 2052) will be required to cover Firewalls, Web Application Security, NAC, Proxy and Perimeter Mail areas within Network Security.
• Strong familiarity with NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography standards (FIPS 203, 204, 205) and their applicability to network security infrastructure
• Understanding of financial industry regulatory frameworks (e.g., FFIEC, DORA, SEC cybersecurity guidance) as they relate to cryptographic standards
• Experience supporting PQC readiness assessments in regulated industries
• Awareness of 'harvest now, decrypt later' threat vectors and their implications for financial data
• Ability to incorporate industry-standard compliance frameworks into the RFP deliverables and final recommendations
The Network Security Architect leads the creation of robust, layered defense infrastructures. They analyze existing security postures, identify structural vulnerabilities, perform gap analyses, and design end-to-end network security solutions. They collaborate closely with project managers, security engineers, and executive stakeholders to translate complex business demands into highly resilient, secure technical realities.

Core Responsibilities
1. Security Architecture & Strategy Design: Design and deliver comprehensive, secure network frameworks using trust domain segregation, Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA), and secure zoning principles. Develop technical solutions and integration strategies across LANs, WANs, SD-WAN, MPLS, data centers, and multi-cloud environments. Establish baseline configurations for network infrastructure, including Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW), Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS), and Network Access Control (NAC).
2. Risk Assessment & Vulnerability Management: Conduct routine gap analyses and security risk assessments against recognized frameworks like NIST, SANS, and CIS. Evaluate proposed acquisitions and software interfaces to determine how they impact the organization's overarching network security posture. Plan and oversee regular vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, and ethical hacking exercises.
3. Access Control & Data Protection: Define and implement secure identity federation, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), Single Sign-On (SSO), and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) systems. Enforce Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to limit network access strictly by corporate necessity and specific employee roles. Architect data-in-transit encryption paths (IPsec/SSL VPNs) and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) parameters to mitigate data leakage.
4. Incident Response & Business Continuity: Design disaster recovery plans, data backup strategies, and conduct routine breach-of-security simulation drills. Provide escalation support during critical network intrusions or unauthorized system access. Conduct comprehensive post-event analyses to determine exact root causes and update network models to mitigate future risks.

Required Technical Skills & Knowledge
Network Technologies: Proficient in IP routing, MPLS, BGP, SD-WAN, Wireless networks, and advanced data center architectures.
Security Hardware/Software: Extensive experience deploying Checkpoint, Palo Alto, or Cisco NGFWs, SIEM monitoring platforms, and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions.
Cloud Architecture: Hands-on experience mapping secure network perimeters inside AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP) environments.
Frameworks & Methodologies: Deep familiarity with SABSA, TOGAF, COBIT, ITIL, and DoDAF architecture frameworks.
Automation & Scripting: Capability to write code in Python or PowerShell to automate network provisioning and logging configurations.

Experience & Education Requirements
Education: Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a closely related technical discipline.
Experience: 8+ years of core IT networking experience alongside 3+ years specifically focused on advanced enterprise cybersecurity architecture.
• IT Infra
• Multi Cloud

• Security
• Agile
• Complex problem-solving skills
Certifications (Highly Preferred):
• Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) or Information Systems Security Architecture Professional (CISSP-ISSAP).
• Cisco Certified Internetwork Expert (CCIE) or Cisco Certified Design Professional (CCDP).
• Certified Information Security Manager (CISM) or SABSA Chartered Security Architect.

title: Sanitation Supervisor
description:
Sanitation Supervisor

The Sanitation Supervisor is responsible for leading the plant’s sanitation program to ensure a safe, clean, and food-safe production environment. This role oversees sanitation staff, ensures proper use of chemicals and equipment, maintains documentation for audits, and supports continuous improvement in plant cleanliness and production readiness.

Key Responsibilities

Sanitation Leadership & Oversight

  • Supervise, train, and schedule sanitation team members across two manufacturing facilities.
  • Ensure all sanitation tasks are completed safely, on time, and according to SSOPs.
  • Conduct daily shift huddles and coordinate responsibilities with QA, Production, and Maintenance.
  • Perform hands-on sanitation duties when necessary to maintain sanitation standards, complete critical tasks, and ensure production readiness.

Food Safety & Compliance

  • Ensure sanitation activities support compliance with GMPs, HACCP, allergen-control, environmental monitoring, and other applicable food safety programs.
  • Ensure compliance with FDA/USDA regulations and internal food safety policies.
  • Perform pre-operational inspections and correct deficiencies before startup.
  • Maintain accurate sanitation records for audits and regulatory reviews.
  • Support internal, customer, regulatory, and third-party audits while implementing corrective actions as needed.

Cleaning & Sanitation Operations

  • Oversee cleaning and sanitizing of equipment, production lines, floors, walls, drains, and facility areas.
  • Manage chemical concentrations, usage, and safe handling procedures.
  • Coordinate equipment to tear down and reassembly with QA, Maintenance, and Production teams.
  • Lead and participate in deep cleaning projects and periodic sanitation tasks.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to reduce chemical usage, improve cleaning efficiency, and minimize downtime.
  • Assist in root-cause investigations of sanitation-related issues (microbial findings, allergen cross-contact, etc.).
  • Implement best practices to support higher food safety standards and operational excellence.

Administration & Documentation

  • Create, maintain and update SSOPs, sanitation schedules, chemical-control practices and training materials.
  • Complete sanitation logs, chemical usage reports, and personnel records.
  • Monitor inventory of cleaning supplies, PPE, and sanitation tools.

Qualifications

  • Strong working knowledge of HACCP, GMP, SSOP, FDA, USDA, and OSHA requirements.
  • Experience supervising sanitation in a manufacturing or food production environment preferred.
  • Knowledge of chemical handling procedures and sanitation best practices.
  • Strong leadership, coaching, and employee development skills.
  • Strong communication, organizational skills and ability to prioritize.
  • Ability to work nights, weekends, or flexible shifts as needed.
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred.

title: National Training & Development Director
description:
Titan Group is a premier provider of electrical contracting services, offering comprehensive solutions for a diverse range of industries. The company specializes in the design, installation, and maintenance of electrical systems for new construction, tenant improvements, and facility upgrades.

With expertise spanning multiple sectors, Titan serves clients in commercial, industrial, healthcare, retail, data centers, and mission-critical facilities, ensuring reliable and innovative electrical solutions tailored to each project's needs. Titan prides itself on exceptional craftsmanship, safety compliance, and customer satisfaction, making it a trusted partner in the electrical contracting industry.

The Manager, Training and Development designs, plans, implements, administers, and continuously improves company training and talent development programs, policies, procedures, and learning resources.

This role partners with functional teams and business leaders to assess current and future training needs, evaluate the effectiveness of established programs, and develop practical learning solutions that support office and field operations. The position researches new training methods, engages outside vendors for supplemental training and content, and ensures training resources and delivery methods remain current, effective, and aligned with Titan’s changing business needs.

ROLES SUPERVISED: May supervise a small team or lead a matrix structure

TRAVEL REQUIRED: Significant travel may be required up to 50%

ONSITE: When not traveling, 4 days a week in office

Essential Functions

  • Establish the annual enterprise training strategy and priorities across all Titan companies and locations, setting consistent standards while allowing for local business needs.
  • Develop coordinated career and leadership development paths for foremen, superintendents, project managers, estimators, engineers, and apprentices in partnership with operations, safety, HR Business Partners, and business leaders.
  • Manage the training budget and establish investment priorities with company presidents based on business needs, workforce priorities, and expected outcomes.
  • Partner with project sponsors, product champions, and subject matter experts to lead training rollouts for new systems and procedures, including ERP, estimating tools, and project management practices.
  • Lead training administration, including the annual training calendar, enrollment, communications, attendance, completion records, and logistical coordination.
  • Administer the learning management system and related training tools, including system configuration, user access, course assignments, technical support, data integrity, and compliance reporting.
  • Partner with functional teams and business leaders to identify current and future organization-wide training needs using business priorities, performance trends, leader input, employee feedback, and workforce development requirements.
  • Design, develop, and implement instructor-led, virtual, and self-paced learning programs focused on leadership, supervision, communication, teamwork, conflict management, coaching, and other interpersonal skills.
  • Facilitate engaging learning programs for leaders and employees across office and field environments, adapting delivery to the audience and business need.
  • Partner with managers to assess individual and team talent, identify readiness and development needs, and create actionable development plans.
  • Coordinate talent reviews and succession planning with HR Business Partners and business leaders, including documentation of readiness, succession risks, and agreed follow-up actions.
  • Establish learning objectives and success measures; analyze participation, completion, feedback, skill progression, adoption of new processes, leadership readiness, and business impact; communicate results and recommend improvements.
  • Source and manage internal subject matter experts and external training vendors, including evaluating capabilities, defining deliverables, coordinating services, and monitoring cost and performance.
  • Maintain the training content library, facilitator guides, participant resources, standard operating procedures, delivery standards, and related records so materials remain accurate, current, accessible, and aligned with company requirements.
  • Build effective relationships across business units and promote a culture of continuous learning, accountability, and employee development.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Position Qualifications

Education, Experience, Certifications and/or Licenses

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Education, Business, or a related field required. An equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.
  • At least seven (7) years of progressive experience in learning and development, training, organizational development, talent development, or a related area, including experience designing, planning, implementing, and evaluating training programs.
  • Experience designing and facilitating leadership and interpersonal skill development programs required.
  • Experience administering an LMS or similar learning platform required.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities (KSAs)

  • Strong facilitation, presentation, coaching, communication, and relationship-building skills.

title: Business Process and AI Product Owner
description:
From the beginning, our goal was to establish an advisory firm that stands apart from the rest – one that is grounded in our Core Values and dedicated to creating a positive experience not just for our clients, but for our people too. We firmly believe in the strength of collaboration, enthusiasm, generosity, and perseverance as the driving forces behind our success. With advisory solutions spanning accounting and risk, technology-enabled transformation, and transactions, we partner with our clients to solve today’s challenges and deliver present and future value.

Our commitment to our people has earned us numerous awards including Inc5000's Fastest Growing Companies and Glassdoor's Best Places to Work. Explore what our employees have to say about our unique culture by clicking here.

CrossCountry Consulting’s AI Innovation & Transformation practice builds the next generation of agentic AI solutions for the Office of the CFO and other enterprise functions. We design, deploy, and manage AI agents that automate and augment core enterprise workflows grounded in production-grade data foundations and domain expertise. As a Business Process & AI Product Owner on this team, you will be the bridge between what clients want to achieve and what AI can actually deliver: translating strategic finance and operational priorities into a disciplined AI product roadmap, orchestrating the cross-functional work required to bring agents from concept to production, and ensuring every deployment creates measurable, defensible enterprise value.

The Role

AI transformation at scale requires more than strong data and great engineering – it requires someone who deeply understands how finance, operations, and technology intersect within an enterprise, can diagnose process dysfunction and quantify value opportunities, and can own a product backlog with the rigor of a seasoned product manager and the credibility of a former finance leader. You will serve as the primary client-facing AI Product Owner, owning requirements, redesigning processes, sprint planning, stakeholder alignment, running training and customer success programs, and value realization from kick-off through steady-state managed outcomes.

What You'll Do:

  • Process discovery & value architecture: Lead structured current-state process assessments across finance and adjacent functions (accounting, FP&A, treasury, procurement, revenue operations, HR finance, legal ops); quantify value opportunities by AI and automation tier, identify high-ROI agent use cases for the enterprise, and build the business case for AI investment with CFO-ready financial models.
  • Process redesign & optimization: Where AI and Machine Learning solutions create value, help clients redesign roles, org structures, and operating models to capture the full value of AI/ML, working across value streams and domains; advise on workforce transition, upskilling, and governance model changes required to operate AI-augmented finance functions.
  • AI product roadmap ownership: Define, prioritize, and maintain a rolling AI product roadmap for each client engagement, sequencing deployments and platform build-out by value, feasibility, and data readiness; balance quick wins against strategic platform capabilities.
  • Requirements & user story development: Translate business requirements, inclusive of new capabilities that AI can bring, into detailed agent specifications: user stories, acceptance criteria, data input/output schemas, exception-handling logic, HITL/HOTL decision points, and success metrics.
  • Sprint planning & delivery governance: Lead development planning, demos, and deployments in collaboration with Forward Deployed Engineers and Data Architects; manage scope, track velocity, surface blockers, and maintain delivery confidence against committed timelines and fixed-fee budgets.
  • Stakeholder management & executive alignment: Build trusted relationships with client CEOs, CTOs, CHROs, CFOs, Controllers, VP FP&A, and functional leaders; facilitate executive steering committees, present sprint demos, and communicate roadmap progress and tradeoffs in business terms that resonate with finance leadership.
  • Change management & user adoption: Design and execute change management plans that drive user adoption of AI & ML solutions within client finance teams; develop training programs, change champions networks, and adoption KPI dashboards; address resistance with empathy and clear articulation of individual benefit.
  • Value realization & ROI measurement: Define outcome metrics at the start of each engagement (revenue growth, retention, spend optimization, hours recovered, error rate reduction, cycle-time compression, variance-explanation coverage, etc.); instrument agentic solution to capture those metrics and produce periodic Value Realization Reports that demonstrate ROI against the original business case. Transform/establish processes to put clients in the position to achieve these outcomes.
  • AI ethics & governance in practice: Partner with the governance, AI/ML Ops & Ethics Lead to embed client-specific governance requirements into product design; ensure agent decision-rights, override protocols, and audit trails are documented and accepted by client legal, compliance, and internal audit.
  • GTM contribution: Contribute client learnings to agentic package refinement; author case studies, ROI benchmarks, and reusable process-assessment frameworks; support business development through proposal development, discovery workshops, and conference presentations.
  • Practice building & mentorship: Mentor junior delivery team members in agile product management and process analysis disciplines; contribute to AI methodology development and quality standards.

What You'll Bring:

  • 8+ years of combined experience in finance (FP&A, accounting, or operations), management consulting, and/or enterprise technology product management; direct experience in at least two of these three domains is required.
  • Deep finance domain expertise: hands-on familiarity with month-end close, financial reporting, budgeting and forecasting, revenue operations, and at least one adjacent function (treasury, procurement, sales operations, revenue operations, HR, IT, or legal); CPA, CFA, or MBA is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience as a Product Owner or Product Manager in an enterprise software, SaaS, or digital transformation context; proficiency with agile methodologies.
  • Experience deploying or overseeing AI/ML or intelligent automation (RPA, NLP, or LLM-based) solutions in a finance or operations context; sufficient technical fluency to evaluate feasibility, challenge engineering assumptions, and communicate credibly with data architects and engineers.
  • Deep domain knowledge of at least 1-2 industries, including their business models and key performance metrics, grounding a clear view of where the AI value levers are in the industry and how to capture them
  • Track record of building and presenting rigorous business cases for technology investment, including NPV/IRR analysis, payback period modeling, and sensitivity analysis, tailored to CFO and board-level audiences.
  • Exceptional workshop facilitation and process-mapping skills.
  • Strong executive presence and communication skills; ability to navigate complex client politics, manage competing stakeholder priorities, and maintain delivery momentum in large, matrixed organizations.
  • Demonstrated change management competency; experience designing and executing change programs for technology-driven finance transformation.
  • Comfort operating in a startup-within-a-consulting-firm environment: building playbooks from scratch, context-switching across clients, and maintaining high quality under deadline pressure.

Qualifications:

  • A bachelor’s degree from an accredited university; MBA, CPA, or equivalent advanced degree or certification strongly preferred.
  • Certified SAFe Product Owner/Product Manager, CSPO, or equivalent agile product certification preferred.
  • If remote - willingness to travel domestically up to 30%–40% (varies by client engagement phase).
  • If hybrid - availability to work on client site or in office 3 days a week, with 2 days remote.

title: Large Loss Field Claim Resolution Specialist, Property
description:
Description

Senior Field Property Claim Resolution Specialist, Large Loss

When a policyholder's home is unlivable, they need more than a claim number - they need someone who knows exactly what to do next. That's you.

As a Senior Field Claim Resolution Specialist, you'll take on Liberty Mutual's most complex property losses, often severe damage that leaves a family unable to stay in their own home. You'll investigate the loss, determine coverage, scope the damage on-site and guide policyholders through every step of getting back on their feet, all with minimal oversight and a high degree of trust in your judgment.

Reliable attendance and full engagement during training aren't optional here - they're the foundation everything else is built on. Show up, lean in and you'll be ready for what this role asks of you.

  • Inspect loss sites in person, write appraisals for dwelling repairs and issue payment to policyholders where possible
  • Independently scope large losses and partner with Liberty's network contractors throughout the appraisal process
  • Certify and re-inspect Liberty-referred contractors and independents as needed
  • Walk policyholders through coverage, help them itemize damages and coordinate emergency repairs and additional living arrangements

Ideal Experience Includes:

Why Liberty Mutual:

You'll work with real independence on some of the toughest claims we see, backed by a team that trusts your expertise and a company that's spent over a century helping people move forward after loss. If you're ready to bring your skills to the moments that matter most, we'd love to have you.

title: Water Sampling Technician – Sterile Processing Water Quality
description:
Position Summary

I-2-I Solutions is seeking a dependable and detail-oriented Water Sampling Technician to perform recurring water sample collection at healthcare facilities in Dallas and Fort Worth, Texas.

The technician will collect Critical Water, Utility Water, and Steam Condensate samples from designated locations within Sterile Processing Service (SPS) areas. This position requires careful adherence to established sampling procedures, infection-control requirements, chain-of-custody protocols, and sample-handling procedures.

Candidates with previous experience in healthcare water sampling, sterile processing environments, environmental sampling, laboratory sample collection, or ANSI/AAMI ST108 are strongly preferred.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Collect water samples from designated locations within healthcare facilities.
  • Perform sampling of Critical Water, Utility Water, and Steam Condensate.
  • Collect samples from designated points of generation and points of use.
  • Perform monthly, quarterly, and follow-up sampling as scheduled.
  • Follow established ANSI/AAMI ST108 sampling procedures.
  • Flush sampling locations for the required period before sample collection.
  • Use proper aseptic sampling techniques to prevent contamination.
  • Clean and disinfect sampling locations using approved procedures before collection.
  • Use appropriate sterile and preserved laboratory sample containers.
  • Properly label all sample containers.
  • Complete chain-of-custody forms and required field documentation accurately.
  • Maintain strict chain of custody from sample collection through shipment.
  • Properly package samples for transportation to the laboratory.
  • Maintain required sample temperatures during transportation and shipment.
  • Protect samples from contamination, damage, freezing, or other conditions that could affect sample integrity.
  • Immediately report any collection, shipping, labeling, or chain-of-custody problems.
  • Assist with repeat sampling when required.
  • Follow all facility safety, infection-control, and PPE requirements.
  • Wear required protective equipment while working within Sterile Processing areas.
  • Coordinate professionally with facility personnel while accessing sampling locations.
  • Maintain consistent sampling procedures and locations between sampling events.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience with water sampling, environmental sampling, laboratory sample collection, or a related technical field.
  • Ability to follow detailed written sampling procedures.
  • Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
  • Ability to properly complete chain-of-custody documentation.
  • Ability to safely handle and transport laboratory samples.
  • Ability to work independently and follow established schedules.
  • Reliable transportation to work locations in Dallas and Fort Worth.
  • Ability to work within an active healthcare environment.
  • Ability to comply with healthcare infection-control and PPE requirements.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain required facility identification/badging.
  • Valid, non-expired government-issued photo identification.

Preferred Qualifications

Preference will be given to candidates with experience in one or more of the following:

  • Sterile Processing Service (SPS) environments
  • ANSI/AAMI ST108 water sampling
  • Critical Water or RO/DI water systems
  • Healthcare or hospital water sampling
  • Point-of-generation and point-of-use sampling
  • Steam condensate sampling
  • Microbiological water sampling
  • Chain-of-custody documentation
  • Federal or VA healthcare facilities

Work Environment

The technician will work inside active healthcare facilities, including Sterile Processing areas. The position may require the use of protective clothing, gloves, face masks or shields, and foot coverings depending on the work area.

Candidates must be comfortable working around water-treatment equipment, plumbing systems, sterilization equipment, sinks, washers, Medivators/AER equipment, and other healthcare processing equipment.

Schedule

Work will generally be performed Monday through Friday between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.

Sampling includes recurring monthly and quarterly visits. Additional visits may occasionally be required for follow-up or repeat sampling.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is reliable, organized, careful with documentation, comfortable working in healthcare environments, and understands that proper sampling technique and sample integrity are critical to producing valid laboratory results.

Experience performing water sampling in hospitals or sterile processing departments is highly desirable.

title: Quality Assurance Inspector Nights
description:
Location: West Valley, UT

Department: Quality Assurance

Reports To: Shift Supervisor

Direct Reports: None

Shift / Coverage:Night Shift - 4:00 PM - 2:30 AM (Monday - Thursday)

Position Description

The Quality Inspector is the front line of product conformity. This role inspects parts against prints, specifications, and inspection plans, documents what was found, and stops nonconforming material from moving forward. Every accept decision on the floor starts here.

The work is judgment as much as measurement. Selecting the right gage for the characteristic, verifying its calibration status before use, and interpreting a callout correctly are all part of producing a result that can be relied on. A measurement taken with the wrong instrument is not a measurement.

Authority here is deliberately asymmetric. This role can reject, hold, and refuse - without prior approval and without fear of reprisal - but it cannot accept nonconforming material, waive a requirement, or release a hold. That asymmetry is the point: stopping is always available, and passing is never a solo decision on a questionable part.

Escalation is a duty, not a fallback. Borderline, ambiguous, or unexpected conditions go to the Shift Supervisor rather than being decided alone, and a nonconforming vendor part is raised as a supplier corrective action request with complete inspection evidence. Cosmetic and non-dimensional SCARs route to the Shift Supervisor; dimensional ones route to Engineering.

Several people carry this role alongside another. Specialists take inspection assignment from the Shift Supervisor and meet the same qualification requirements as any inspector before working unsupervised. There is one inspection standard, and holding a second title does not change it.

Job Responsibilities

Inspection & Measurement

  • Perform first-article, in-process, and final inspection per the applicable inspection plan and sampling requirement.
  • Interpret prints, GD&T, specifications, and inspection plans correctly and consistently.
  • Select and correctly use the appropriate gages and instruments; verify calibration status before use.
  • Perform re-inspection and sorting activity as directed during containment.

Records & Traceability

  • Record inspection results completely, legibly, and accurately, with full traceability to part, lot, and revision.
  • Maintain a clean, organized inspection station and return issued gages in good condition.

Nonconformance & Escalation

  • Identify, tag, and segregate nonconforming material immediately and notify the Shift Supervisor.
  • Escalate borderline, ambiguous, or unexpected conditions rather than deciding alone.
  • Support root cause investigation by providing accurate, factual observations of what was found.

Process Monitoring & SPC

  • Record SPC data points accurately at the required sample size and frequency, and apply the reaction plan on the chart when a signal appears - stop, contain, notify the Shift Supervisor.

Supplier Corrective Action

  • Where an inspection finds a nonconforming vendor part, raise the supplier corrective action request (SCAR) with complete inspection evidence, and route it for approval - to the Shift Supervisor if the issue is cosmetic or non-dimensional, to Engineering if it is dimensional.
  • On approval the system emails the vendor automatically from the quality mailbox. Stay copied on the thread so you see the vendor response, but let the Source Inspector lead the exchange from that point.

Training & Qualification

  • Complete and maintain required training and qualification for the inspections assigned.

Decision Authority

  • Authority to reject nonconforming product against the print, specification, or inspection plan.
  • Authority to place material on quality hold without prior approval and without fear of reprisal.
  • Authority to refuse to inspect with equipment that is out of calibration or unsuitable for the characteristic.
  • No authority to accept nonconforming material, waive a requirement, or release a hold.

Critical Results

  • Nonconforming material stops here - Defects are caught at the operation that produced them, tagged and segregated immediately, and never pass to the next step on the assumption someone downstream will catch them.
  • The same part gets the same call every time - Interpretation does not vary by inspector, by shift, or by how busy the floor is. Where two people would call a feature differently, it is raised and resolved rather than left to whoever measures it next.
  • Every result can be trusted and traced - Records are complete, legible, and tied to part, lot, and revision, produced with a gage that was in calibration and right for the characteristic. An auditor can reconstruct the decision months later.
  • Signals are acted on, not just recorded - SPC points are taken at the required rate and a chart signal triggers the reaction plan on the spot - stop, contain, notify - rather than a note to mention it later.
  • Questions get asked before parts move - Borderline and ambiguous conditions are escalated rather than guessed, and raising a concern, including about one's own mistake, carries no penalty.

Job Qualifications

Required

  • One or more years of dimensional inspection experience, or equivalent machining experience with documented inspection training.
  • Print reading and working GD&T interpretation.
  • Proficiency with calipers, micrometers, height gages, thread and pin gages, and optical comparators.
  • Legible, accurate documentation of inspection results.
  • Willingness to stop and escalate rather than pass a questionable part.

Preferred

  • Firearms, suppressor, or other precision manufacturing industry experience.
  • CMM exposure or willingness to train as a CMM Operator.
  • ASQ Certified Quality Technician/Inspector (CQT/CQI).
  • Experience with QMS or electronic quality data entry.

Key Competencies

  • Consistent - the same part gets the same call every time.
  • Honest about what was found, including when it is inconvenient.
  • Detail-focused across a full shift without drifting.
  • Asks rather than assumes an ambiguous requirement.

Physical Requirements and Work Environment

  • Frequently stands and walks on a production floor for much of the shift.
  • Regularly lifts and carries parts, fixtures, and gages up to 25 lbs; occasionally up to 40 lbs with assistance.
  • Requires near-vision acuity and color discrimination sufficient to inspect small features and read measuring instruments, with correction if needed.
  • Requires fine manual dexterity to handle small parts, precision instruments, and delicate gage surfaces.
  • Works in a machine shop environment with exposure to noise, coolant, lubricants, metal chips, and moving equipment.
  • Required PPE includes safety glasses and hearing protection in designated areas.

title: Staff Engineer, Field Service (R6120)
description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit . Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

Job Description:

At Shield AI, we are developing autonomy solutions that enhance mission effectiveness and operational decision-making. Our Vision Systems / Hivemind Vision portfolio applies computer vision and AI/ML technologies to help defense, government, and commercial customers gain actionable information from optical sensors.

As a Vision Systems Demonstration & Training Specialist on the demonstration and training team, you will support customer demonstrations, operator training, and operational adoption across the portfolio. Working closely with product management, engineering, and business development, you will help customers understand, evaluate, and effectively employ our capabilities.

This role requires operational credibility, technical fluency, and a strong instinct for teaching and customer engagement. The ideal candidate understands the demands facing sensor operators and intelligence teams—including real-time workload, competing mission priorities, and the challenges of integrating multiple sensors and information sources—and brings that perspective to every demonstration, training event, and customer interaction.

What you'll do:

Demonstration & Operational Support:

  • Plan and execute customer flight plans for demonstrations that connect product capabilities to specific mission needs and operational workflows.
  • Prepare and operate Vision Systems software, sensor interfaces, and associated mission equipment during demonstrations, exercises, and evaluations.
  • Support equipment readiness, system configuration, connectivity checks, and field troubleshooting in coordination with engineering and flight operations personnel.
  • Apply crew resource management and operational risk management principles to event preparation, execution, and debriefing.
  • Assist in development of realistic scenarios, demonstration plans, briefing materials, and measures of success in coordination with product management and business development.

Training & Standardization:

  • Develop and deliver operator training, practical exercises, and supporting materials for customers and internal teams.
  • Teach system operation, effective employment, and capability limitations in the context of the customer’s mission.
  • Assess operator proficiency and adapt instruction to different experience levels and operational backgrounds.
  • Develop and maintain procedures, checklists, instructional guides, and standardized demonstration materials.
  • Capture lessons learned and incorporate them into training content and operational practices.

Customer Engagement & Adoption:

  • Build trusted relationships with operators, instructors, intelligence personnel, and customer program teams.
  • Understand customer challenges and help translate them into practical approaches for employing Vision Systems capabilities.
  • Support customer onboarding, operational familiarization, and follow-up engagement after demonstrations and training.
  • Communicate clearly with operational, technical, and leadership audiences, setting realistic expectations for system performance and employment.
  • Help customers understand how product outputs fit into existing mission systems, tactical applications, and intelligence workflows.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Product Feedback:

  • Translate customer observations into clear descriptions of operational needs, usability issues, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Partner with product management and engineering to evaluate new capabilities and validate them against representative operational scenarios.
  • Support integration and field-test activities through mission-system operation, data collection, issue documentation, and operational feedback.
  • Contribute to concepts of operation, application guidance, and customer-facing technical materials.
  • Coordinate with business development and marketing to ensure demonstrations and messaging accurately represent product capabilities and operational value.

Required qualifications:

  • Significant experience in airborne ISR sensor operations, operational intelligence support, or a closely related mission-system or field applications role.
  • Practical understanding of EO/IR sensor employment, particularly gimballed sensors and full-motion video, including real-time task management, crew coordination, and operation alongside other intelligence sensors.
  • Understanding of ISR collection and processing, exploitation, and dissemination (PED), including how sensor outputs support operational decisions.
  • Working familiarity with mission-system interfaces, tactical applications, communications networks, and data links used to exchange sensor information and intelligence products.
  • Familiarity with joint ISR collection and dynamic targeting.
  • Understanding of crew resource management (CRM) and operational risk management (ORM).
  • Demonstrated ability to instruct, mentor, or deliver effective operational and technical briefings.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex concepts to both technical and operational audiences.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, sound judgment, and demonstrated empathy for end users.
  • Ability to learn new software and mission systems, troubleshoot operational issues, and work independently during customer engagements.
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally for demonstrations, training, exercises, and customer support.
Relevant military, contractor, or industry experience may substitute for formal academic qualifications.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience as an airborne sensor operator in manned and unmanned ISR platforms, maritime patrol, special operations, or comparable multi-sensor mission environments.
  • Instructor, evaluator, or standardization experience, including development of curricula, qualification standards, or operating procedures.
  • Experience supporting joint or special operations customers through military service or government-contracted ISR programs.
  • Experience GRP 1, 2 and 3 UAS on platforms such as the MC-12, U-28, AC-130, P-8, or comparable contractor-operated ISR aircraft.
  • Aviation safety experience or comparable responsibility for safety programs, operational risk assessment, and incident prevention.
  • Experience employing EO/IR sensors alongside radar, signals intelligence, or other collection systems.
  • Experience integrating sensors or mission systems on airborne platforms, or supporting operational test and evaluation.
  • Customer-facing experience with a sensor, mission-system, or defense technology provider.
  • Familiarity with automated target detection and recognition, computer vision, or multi-sensor fusion applications.
  • Experience supporting UAS demonstrations or flight-test activities, including coordination with flight crews and operation of payloads or associated mission systems.

title: Staff Systems Engineer – Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Missions
description:
📍 Location: Richmond, BC, Canada
📄 Employment Type: Full-Time
🏢 Work Arrangement: Hybrid
🚀 Start Date: TBD
💰 Compensation: TBD — depending on skills and experience

Important Screening Requirements

  • Graduate degree in Electrical Engineering, Engineering Physics, Mathematics, Physics, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
  • 15+ years of experience working with radar, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), or similar active imaging systems.
  • Experience spanning hardware, processors, and/or data products within radar or SAR systems.
  • 10+ years of experience in space systems engineering or a similarly complex systems engineering environment.
  • Experience with SAR remote sensing, including system design, operations, applications/exploitation, and/or calibration.
  • Experience working across engineering lifecycles for large, complex programs.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain Reliability Status security clearance and meet Controlled Goods Program (CGP) requirements.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical concepts to technical teams, executives, customers, and other stakeholders.
  • Ability to work effectively within a large organization and navigate cross-functional dependencies.

About the Role

We are seeking a Staff Systems Engineer – Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Missions to provide end-to-end technical oversight of SAR-related engineering activities throughout the lifecycle of complex space missions.

This role will contribute to the development of advanced SAR missions that generate high-value imagery and actionable intelligence for customers.

You will work across mission concept development, spacecraft and payload trade studies, SAR system design, mission-level integration and verification, commissioning, calibration, and early operations.

This is a highly senior technical role requiring the ability to connect mission-level requirements with spacecraft systems, SAR payloads, processing systems, and end-user applications.

What We're Looking For

We’re looking for a Staff-level SAR systems engineer with extensive experience bridging SAR technology and space mission systems engineering.

The ideal candidate has the technical depth to work across the SAR lifecycle—from mission concept and CONOPS through payload and spacecraft trade studies, image-quality analysis, integration, verification, commissioning, calibration, and early operations.

This role requires someone who can operate comfortably at both the deep technical and mission/program levels, communicate with a broad range of stakeholders, mentor engineers, and provide technical guidance on complex SAR mission challenges.

Key Responsibilities

Mission Concept & Systems Engineering

  • Provide end-to-end oversight of SAR-related engineering activities across the full lifecycle of a space SAR mission.
  • Lead development of the Mission Concept of Operations (CONOPS).
  • Define high-level mission specifications based on user and customer requirements.
  • Develop and assess spacecraft-level budgets supporting SAR payload requirements.
  • Translate mission objectives into technical requirements and system-level solutions.

SAR Mission Design & Technical Solutioning

  • Lead technical solutioning for enhancements to existing and future SAR missions.
  • Support and lead SAR beam-mode design.
  • Develop and assess SAR mission concepts.
  • Support SAR image-quality modeling and performance analysis.
  • Evaluate technical solutions across mission, spacecraft, payload, processor, and application domains.

Mission-Level Trade Studies

  • Lead design trade studies across:
    • Spacecraft systems
    • Coverage and access
    • SAR payload
    • SAR processor
    • End-user applications
  • Evaluate technical, operational, and mission-level dependencies.
  • Balance competing system requirements and performance objectives.
  • Provide technical recommendations and guidance to program leadership.

Risk Management, Integration & Verification

  • Lead mission-level technical risk management.
  • Oversee mission-level integration activities.
  • Lead or support verification and validation activities.
  • Identify technical dependencies, interfaces, and potential mission-level risks.
  • Ensure SAR mission requirements and technical objectives are addressed throughout the engineering lifecycle.

Commissioning, Calibration & Operations

  • Provide technical leadership for SAR mission commissioning and calibration.
  • Support early operations of space-based SAR missions.
  • Contribute to the development and execution of mission commissioning strategies.
  • Support resolution of technical issues during early mission operations.
  • Apply SAR system knowledge to evaluate mission and image-quality performance.

Technical Leadership

  • Provide technical guidance to senior management and new business activities.
  • Communicate complex SAR and space systems concepts to diverse audiences.
  • Support customer discussions and technical presentations.
  • Mentor and coach engineering team members.
  • Help develop technical capabilities and domain expertise across the organization.

Required Qualifications

  • Graduate degree in Electrical Engineering, Engineering Physics, Mathematics, Physics, or a related discipline, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • 15+ years of experience with radar, SAR, or similar active imaging systems.
  • Experience involving one or more of:
    • Radar/SAR hardware
    • SAR processors
    • SAR data products
  • 10+ years of experience in space systems engineering or a similarly complex systems engineering environment.
  • Experience in SAR remote sensing, including system design, operations, applications/exploitation, and/or calibration.
  • Experience working across engineering lifecycles for large and complex programs.
