title: Principal Product Manager, Microsoft Clarity
description:
Overview

Today, Microsoft Clarity helps businesses understand what people do on their sites. The next chapter helps those same businesses understand how they show up when customers, copilots, and agents search, reason, cite, recommend, and act across the AI web.

We are looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead Clarity Commercialization, with a focus on AI Visibility, enterprise readiness, pricing and packaging, and the product capabilities needed to turn Clarity into a scaled business. This person will define how Clarity moves from broad product-led adoption into paid customer value, including the analytics, workflows, permissions, APIs, reporting, onboarding, and GTM motions needed by enterprises, agencies, sellers, and customer success teams.

This is a role for a product leader who understands analytics products, commercial product strategy, and the messy reality of building in a new market. The work sits at the intersection of web analytics, AI analytics, GEO/AI discoverability, pricing, enterprise SaaS, Microsoft Advertising, and customer-facing GTM. The right person will make Clarity more valuable for customers and more commercially meaningful for Microsoft.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

AI Experiences employees who live within a 50- mile commute of adesignated Microsoft Hub in the U.S. are expected to work from the officeat least four days per week. This expectation is subject to local law and mayvary by jurisdiction.



Responsibilities

  • Define and lead the product strategy for Clarity Commercialization, including paid customer scenarios, pricing and packaging inputs, enterprise readiness, GTM needs, and measurable business outcomes.

  • Translate customer, agency, seller, and partner feedback into clear product requirements for enterprise customers, account hierarchies, agency models, permissions, privacy-safe sharing, onboarding, and support readiness.

  • Define the product capabilities needed for potential paid offerings, including premium analytics, premium compute-backed features, reporting, APIs, MCP or agent integrations, customer administration, and durable value measurement.

  • Partner with engineering, data science, design, marketing, sales, customer success, finance, and business planning to move from strategy to shipped product, launch plans, adoption targets, and commercial outcomes.

  • Build the connection between product usage and business value, including activation, retention, paid conversion, revenue attribution, Microsoft Advertising value, and customer ROI.

  • Use data, experimentation, customer conversations, competitive signals, and field feedback to prioritize the highest-value commercialization bets and stop work that does not create customer or business value.

  • Create clear executive and cross-functional alignment on Clarity’s commercial roadmap, including what is free, what is paid, what is enterprise-only, and what must be built before the product can scale through sellers and partners.

  • Help Clarity become the trusted analytics layer for the AI economy: where businesses understand human behavior, AI-mediated discovery, agent activity, and the actions that drive growth.

  • Model Microsoft culture through customer obsession, high accountability, direct communication, inclusive collaboration, and a willingness to work through ambiguity without hiding behind process.



Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 10+ years experience in product/service/program management or software development\
    • OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 15+ years experience in product/service/program management or software development
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • Experience commercializing SaaS, analytics, advertising, marketing technology, or enterprise platform products.
  • Experience with pricing, packaging, GTM strategy, paid product adoption, or monetization models for digital products.
  • Experience building analytics products, AI analytics, web analytics, experimentation, attribution, measurement, or customer insight tools.
  • Experience defining product requirements for paying customers, including enterprise workflows, admin controls, access models, reporting, onboarding, support, and customer success needs.
  • Experience working across engineering, design, data science, sales, marketing, finance, business planning, and senior leadership.
  • Experience communicating with audiences at all levels and disciplines, written and verbal communication, with the ability to make ambiguous product and business tradeoffs clear.
  • Experience with AI search, GEO, SEO, LLM visibility, content discovery, citations, knowledge retrieval, or agentic product experiences.
  • Experience with web analytics or product analytics tools such as Clarity, Google Analytics, Adobe Analytics, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Pendo, FullStory, or similar products.
  • Experience building enterprise SaaS products with RBAC, account hierarchy, multi-tenant controls, compliance, privacy, and admin workflows.
  • Experience with advertising, marketing technology, agency workflows, Microsoft Advertising, or customer acquisition products.
  • Experience with API strategy, partner integrations, data exports, MCP-style integrations, or products that become part of a customer’s operating workflow.
  • Experience taking a free or product-led growth product into paid tiers, enterprise packaging, or sales-led adoption.
  • Strong customer empathy for marketers, growth teams, agencies, ecommerce teams, publishers, and enterprise digital teams.
  • Ability to operate like a business owner: product strategy, customer value, GTM, economics, execution, and organizational alignment.

title: Design Leader
description:
Forvia, a sustainable mobility technology leader

We pioneer technology for mobility experience that matter to people.

Your mission, roles and responsibilities

The Design Leader oversees the complete design process from initial concept through final customer release. This role is accountable for delivering fully developed CAD models and prints that align with project milestones, product and process specifications, and customer requirements. Responsibilities are divided into two main areas: design activities and cross‑functional collaboration.

  1. Design Activities
  • Develop system packaging concepts and overall product layouts
  • Lead and coordinate Design activities within assigned programs
  • Ensure consistency across systems, sub‑systems, and components
  • Maintain alignment between internal and customer PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) systems
  • Collaborate with design teams to meet customer milestones
  • Ensure proper use and compliance with DCS (Design Check Sheet), GD (Generic Drawings), and CAD quality standards
  • Manage CAD data exchanges with customers and suppliers
  • Oversee and maintain the Engineering Bill of Materials (EBOM)
  • Conduct design studies as requested by the Product Development Leader (PDL) and Product Experts
  • Ensure all data delivered to the customer meets internal and customer standards
  1. Cross‑Functional Team Engagement:
  • Participate in packaging reviews and formal customer events
  • Help define critical characteristics (KPC – Key Product Characteristics; KCC – Key Control Characteristics)
  • Conduct customer‑requested design studies
  • Collaborate with Product Development Leader (PDL) and Product Experts on TOP5 priorities
  • Partner with Product Experts on DCS application and deviations
  • Work with Process Experts on DFM (Design for Manufacturing) reviews
  • Support Process Planning activities such as EDW (Equipment Design Workshop) and PFA (Process Flow Analysis)
  • Participate in weekly APQP (Advanced Product Quality Planning) meetings
  • Engage in prototype activities, including PPKO (Prototype Plant Kick‑Off)
  • Drive continuous design improvement through cross‑functional collaboration
  • Support 3D and 2D design and drawing reviews

Your profile and competencies to succeed

The ideal candidate will have/be:

  • A bachelor’s degree with 5 years of experience, or a Mechanical Engineering degree with relevant product development experience; automotive industry experience preferred
  • Training and proficiency in program‑specific CAD tools (Catia V5, NX, Creo)
  • Experience with PLM (Product Lifecycle Management) systems
  • Knowledge of primary manufacturing methods
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively in a team
  • An international mindset

What we can do for you

  • At Forvia, you will find an engaging and dynamic environment where you can contribute to the development of sustainable mobility leading technologies.
  • We are the seventh-largest global automotive supplier, employing more than 157,000 people in more than 40 countries which makes a lot of opportunity for career development.
  • We welcome energetic and agile people who can thrive in a fast-changing environment. People who share our strong values. Team players with a collaborative mindset and a passion to deliver high standards for our clients. Lifelong learners. High performers. Globally minded people who aspire to work in a transforming industry, where excellence, speed, and quality count.
  • We cultivate a learning environment, dedicating tools and resources to ensure we remain at the forefront of mobility. Our people enjoy an average of more than 22 hours of online and in-person training within FORVIA University (five campuses around the world)
  • We offer a multicultural environment that values diversity and international collaboration. We believe that diversity is a strength. To create an inclusive culture where all forms of diversity create real value for the company, we have adopted gender diversity targets and inclusion action plans.
  • Achieving CO2 Net Zero as a pioneer of the automotive industry is a priority: In June 2022, Forvia became the first global automotive group to be certified with the new SBTI Net-Zero Standard (the most ambitious standard of SBTi), aligned with the ambition of the 2015 Paris Agreement of limiting global warming to 1.5°C. Three principles guide our action: use less, use better and use longer, with a focus on recyclability and circular economy.

Why join us

FORVIA, a global automotive technology supplier, comprises the complementary technology and industrial strengths of Faurecia and HELLA.

With over 137 500 people, including more than 12,000 R&D engineers across 40+ countries, FORVIA provides a unique and comprehensive approach to the automotive challenges of today and tomorrow. Composed of 6 business groups and a strong IP portfolio of over 12,400 patents, FORVIA is focused on becoming the preferred innovation and integration partner for OEMs worldwide.

In 2025, the Group achieved a consolidated revenue of 26.2 billion euros prior to IFRS 5. FORVIA SE is listed on the Euronext Paris market under the FRVIA mnemonic code and is a component of the SBF 120 index.

FORVIA aims to be a change maker committed to foreseeing and making the mobility transformation happen.

title: Community Health Worker
description:
Statement of Purpose

Seasonal Position

Under the direct supervision of the Clinic Manager, the Community Health Worker (CHW) serves as a trusted liaison between patients, families, healthcare providers, and community resources within a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) and/or Behavioral Health setting. The CHW supports patient engagement, health education, care coordination, outreach, navigation, and social support services to improve health outcomes and reduce barriers to care. This position works collaboratively with medical, behavioral health, care management, and community-based teams to promote patient-centered, trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and equitable healthcare services.

Major Tasks, Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provide outreach, engagement, education, advocacy, and support services to patients and community members.

  • Assist patients with navigation of healthcare systems, specialty referrals, social services, insurance programs, and community resources.

  • Support care coordination activities including appointment scheduling, referral follow-up, transportation coordination, and linkage to services.

  • Conduct screenings, intake activities, assessments, and patient interviews as assigned.

  • Provide health education related to preventive care, chronic disease management, behavioral health, maternal-child health, wellness, and healthy lifestyle practices.

  • Assist patients with registration, enrollment, consent forms, applications, and access to healthcare services.

  • Conduct outreach and follow-up regarding appointments, referrals, treatment adherence, preventive services, chronic disease management, and identified care gaps.

  • Document patient encounters, interventions, outreach activities, and referrals accurately within the Electronic Health Record (EHR) and applicable tracking systems.

  • Identify social determinants of health barriers impacting patient outcomes and assist with resource linkage and advocacy.

  • Collaborate with providers, behavioral health staff, care coordinators, case managers, and community partners to support patient care plans.

  • Participate in community outreach events, educational activities, support groups, and health promotion initiatives.

  • Assist with data collection, reporting, quality improvement activities, and program evaluation efforts.

  • Maintain confidentiality and compliance with HIPAA, HRSA, Medi-Cal, OSHA, and organizational policies and procedures.

  • Participate in safety programs to promote patient and staff safety.

  • Maintain professional boundaries and standards of conduct.

  • Treat patients with respect, care, and concern at all times.

  • Maintain health and safety standards within the facility.

  • Recognize personal biases and demonstrate cultural sensitivity when working with diverse populations.

  • Attend meetings, trainings, and participate in committees as assigned.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Community Health Worker Competencies and Performance Expectations

  • Ability to complete the above major tasks, duties, and responsibilities.

  • Ability to demonstrate professional judgment and decision-making.

  • Ability to adhere to professional standards.

  • Demonstrates effective communication, customer service, and relationship-building skills.

  • Demonstrates strong advocacy, outreach, patient engagement, and healthcare navigation skills.

  • Demonstrates the ability to provide culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and patient-centered services.

  • Demonstrates knowledge of social determinants of health, community resources, and healthcare support programs.

  • Demonstrates strong organizational, documentation, and follow-through skills.

  • Demonstrates the ability to collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary care teams.

  • Demonstrates professionalism, accountability, confidentiality, and problem-solving skills.

Prerequisite Qualifications

The following are the qualifications required to perform the essential functions of this position. Qualifications may be subject to modification based on the Americans with Disabilities Act.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

  • Community Health Worker certification or willingness to obtain certification preferred.

  • Experience working in community health, behavioral health, public health, healthcare, social services, outreach, or related field preferred.

  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred.

  • Experience working in a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) or community-based healthcare setting preferred.

  • Knowledge of community resources, Medi-Cal programs, and social service systems preferred.

  • Must have a valid California driver's license, reliable transportation, and liability insurance if driving a personal vehicle on BHS business.

  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and comply with HIPAA regulation

  • Vision, hearing, manual dexterity, and eye-hand coordination must be adequate for the performance of job duties. Able to sit at a desk, use a keyboard, write and physically perform other job duties. Able to move about the facility to observe clients and staff.

title: Principal Program Manager
description:
Overview

The Cloud Delivery team helps Microsoft Defender deliver reliable, secure services for customers around the world, including in sovereign and regulated cloud environments. We bring together product engineering, cloud infrastructure, and service operations to improve readiness, resolve cross-team delivery challenges, and turn operational learnings into lasting improvements for the services customers rely on.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

We are seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager to build, coordinate, and drive security fundamentals across the Microsoft Defender organization. You will create a clear, consistent view of risk and progress using risk registers, security metrics, and engineering plans. Working across teams rather than within a single engineering group, you will establish the operating rhythm that helps teams resolve obstacles and gives leaders the information they need to see and understand organizational security posture.

• Build and govern a scalable program across Defender's security fundamentals efforts. Establish review cadences, reporting expectations, escalation paths, and clear ownership with engineering and security leaders.

• Use existing risk registers and key performance indicators to explain where risks remain, how they are changing, and whether remediation is making progress. Identify gaps or conflicting information and work with the relevant owners to resolve them.

• Partner with deputy CISO leadership, engineering managers, and technical leads to understand plans, dependencies, milestones, and obstacles. Help teams make commitments visible and maintain a regular rhythm for reviewing progress.

• Coordinate across teams when risks or remediation efforts span services or ownership boundaries. Bring unresolved priority, dependency, and resource decisions to the appropriate leaders with clear options and tradeoffs.

• Produce and maintain concise, periodic summaries of security posture, progress, and emerging themes across the Defender organization.

• Establish planning and review mechanisms that give senior leaders a clear view of portfolio health, strategic tradeoffs, unresolved decisions, and required actions.

• Support division-wide security efforts, including initiatives such as Microsoft's Secure Future Initiative, by connecting their goals to Defender's existing governance and engineering execution.



Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

•Bachelor's Degree AND 6+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree AND 14+ years of experience in engineering, product/technical program management, OR equivalent experience.

• 5+ years of experience leading complex, cross-functional technical programs

•Working knowledge of security fundamentals, including vulnerabilities, exposure, remediation, and risk assessments sufficient to discuss security prioritization with engineering teams.

• Technical understanding of network infrastructure and distributed services sufficient to discuss architecture, dependencies, and security tradeoffs with engineers.

• Written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical risk, uncertainty, and progress to executives.

• Experience coordinating security posture or vulnerability remediation programs across a large product or infrastructure organization.

• Familiarity with large-scale security initiatives and the challenges of applying shared goals across multiple engineering teams.

• Experience finding gaps in security reporting, reconciling inconsistent data, and turning program-level trends into decisions.

• Background in cloud infrastructure, network security, identity, or endpoint protection.

There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $188,000 - $304,200 per year.

This role will work directly with senior leaders, software teams, systems engineers, integration teams, and operational stakeholders to evaluate, develop, test, integrate, and field Command and Control User Interface (C2UI) software capabilities at operational scale. The candidate will help establish and sustain production and development environments, manage technical backlogs, and drive software capabilities from requirements and proof-of-concept development through integration, testing, deployment, and sustainment. The role requires extensive software engineering and systems integration expertise, strong knowledge of modern DevSecOps and AGILE methodologies, and the ability to provide technical direction in a rapid innovation environment.


Responsibilities:

  • Lead the software development and integration lifecycle for resilient software, web applications, and C2UI capabilities, including requirements analysis, specification, architecture, design, development, integration, testing, deployment, maintenance, and sustainment.
  • Work directly with senior leaders, operational users, and technical teams to evaluate mission needs, define technical objectives, develop and prioritize backlogs, and deliver software capabilities supporting fleet operations at scale.
  • Design, develop, integrate, and implement software solutions using modern DevSecOps practices, Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA), microservices, APIs, and other modular software approaches.
  • Perform system and software design, development, integration, and implementation of proof-of-concept prototypes to evaluate emerging capabilities and rapidly transition successful solutions toward operational use.
  • Integrate software applications, web-based products, network operating environments, data services, and supporting systems to ensure interoperability and reliable end-to-end capability delivery.
  • Apply software architecture, requirements-driven design, test-driven development, and behavior-driven development principles to improve software quality, resiliency, maintainability, and alignment with operational requirements.
  • Analyze system workflows, data usage, software dependencies, interfaces, and technical problem areas to identify integration challenges and develop effective engineering solutions.
  • Serve as a senior technical authority by providing recommendations to engineering and program leadership, mentoring junior engineers, reviewing technical approaches, and guiding teams through complex software development and integration challenges.
  • Document and demonstrate technical solutions through system documentation, architecture diagrams, flowcharts, interface descriptions, specifications, standards, code comments, technical briefings, and other engineering artifacts.

About Us: PMAT is an innovative small business founded with a passion for developing forward-leaning solutions from exceptional people that increase the mission's capability. We focus on designing and building impactful digital solutions that utilize modern cloud, data, and software concepts. Our passion is working on complex and progressive challenges such as edge platform computing, containerizing legacy platforms, distributed data platforms, or heterogeneous data analysis.

We recruit, retain, and foster a team motivated to pursue passions, investigate new ways of doing things, and embody an innovative and entrepreneurial spirit. We believe in being curious about every element of a problem and experiment relentlessly. We foster continuous learning in an environment that encourages positive collaboration and expands our capabilities. We tap into collective intelligence, acknowledging that the most brilliant people may not be in the room. Above all else, we believe that delivering and demonstrating is more potent than a sheet of paper. We are passionate about mission-centric design and delivering effective capabilities to and for the warfighter.

Whether you’re an experienced engineer or just beginning your career, you’ll work alongside experts who are committed to solving mission-critical problems. If you’re passionate about using your skills to make a real difference, apply today and become part of a team that’s shaping the future of defense technology!


Required Skills and Experience:

  • Extensive experience in software engineering, software systems integration, application development, systems engineering, or related technical disciplines supporting complex software environments.
  • Strong understanding of software architecture, requirements-driven design, software integration, system interfaces, and the complete software development lifecycle.
  • Experience designing, developing, integrating, testing, deploying, and sustaining resilient software applications, web applications, or distributed software systems.
  • Experience developing software solutions using modern development practices, modular architectures, APIs, services, or microservices-based approaches.
  • Experience supporting DevSecOps and Agile software development environments, including backlog management, iterative development, integration, testing, and rapid capability delivery.
  • Experience performing system design, software development, integration, and implementation of prototypes or proof-of-concept capabilities.
  • Experience analyzing system workflows, data flows, application interfaces, software dependencies, user requirements, and technical integration challenges.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide senior technical leadership, mentor engineers, coordinate across multidisciplinary teams, and provide recommendations to technical and program leadership.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to translate complex software and integration topics into clear recommendations for engineering, program, senior leadership, and operational audiences.

Preferred Skills and Experience:

  • Experience developing, integrating, testing, or fielding Command and Control, C2UI, or other mission-critical software capabilities supporting Navy or fleet operations.
  • Experience supporting Navy, Department of War, government, tactical, or other mission-focused software environments.
  • Experience establishing or supporting production and development environments for operationally deployed software capabilities.
  • Experience with Service-Oriented Architecture, microservices, containerized applications, APIs, distributed systems, and modern web application architectures.
  • Experience with modern DevSecOps technologies and practices, including CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, containerization, orchestration, configuration management, and secure software delivery.
  • Experience applying test-driven development, behavior-driven development, automated testing, software quality practices, or similar approaches within complex development environments.
  • Experience integrating software across network operating environments, data services, infrastructure platforms, external applications, or other System of Systems components.
  • Experience supporting rapid innovation, prototyping, experimentation, operational demonstrations, testing, and transition of software capabilities into fielded environments.
  • Experience developing and maintaining technical backlogs, translating operational requirements into executable engineering work, and coordinating priorities across multiple development or integration teams.

title: Especialista em Orçamento
description:
A TXT Build é uma empresa de construção civil certificada como Great Place to Work, com atuação em obras de grande porte no Brasil. Nossa cultura é orientada à precisão, melhoria contínua e trabalho em equipe. Afinal, não é pressa, é precisão.


Buscamos um(a) Especialista em Orçamento para integrar nosso time em Salvador - BA, atuando diretamente no acompanhamento da qualidade e planejamento das obras, com autonomia para propor melhorias e contribuir com a excelência dos nossos processos.



  • Analisar o projeto: estuda os projetos (arquitetura, estrutura, instalações), os memoriais descritivos, os editais e os escopos enviados pelo cliente. Identifica o que está faltando ou é ambíguo e pede esclarecimentos.
  • Levantar quantitativos: mede nas plantas e no BIM tudo o que será executado, como m² de piso, m³ de concreto, metros de tubulação e pontos elétricos.
  • Compor custos: monta as composições de preço unitário (material + mão de obra + equipamentos) usando bases como SINAPI, TCPO, ORSE ou o banco de dados da própria empresa.
  • Cotar com fornecedores e empreiteiros: pede e compara propostas de materiais e de serviços terceirizados, fazendo a equalização (deixar as propostas comparáveis entre si).
  • Calcular o BDI e os encargos: define as despesas indiretas, os impostos, o risco e a margem, além dos encargos sociais da mão de obra.
  • Montar a planilha orçamentária: organiza a EAP (Estrutura Analítica do Projeto), a curva ABC (os itens que mais pesam no custo) e o cronograma físico financeiro.
  • Apoiar o comercial: ajuda a formar o preço da proposta, participa de concorrências e licitações e defende o orçamento em reuniões com o cliente.
  • Acompanhar a obra: compara o orçado com o realizado, analisa aditivos e mudanças de escopo e alimenta a base de custos para os próximos orçamentos.

  • Formação: Engenharia Civil ou Arquitetura ou Técnico em Edificações com experiência.
  • Ferramentas: Excel avançado, softwares de orçamento (Sienge, OrçaFascio, Volare, MS Project) e leitura de projetos em AutoCAD ou Revit.
  • Conhecimentos: métodos construtivos, bases de preço, encargos e tributação da construção.
  • Competências: atenção a detalhes, raciocínio analítico, trabalho com prazos apertados e boa comunicação com as áreas comercial, de suprimentos e de engenharia.

title: Lead Materials Engineer (Miami, FL)
description:

  • Develop novel material compositions and processing techniques for our proprietary sensible heat battery technology that must withstand temperatures exceeding 1000°C

  • Cross-Disciplinary Innovation:
  • Collaborate with our world-class team of mechanical, thermal, and optical engineers to solve complex multi-physics problems at the intersection of materials science, thermodynamics, and optics
  • Lead materials selection and optimization for our Fresnel lens systems, requiring expertise in optical materials, coatings, and durability under concentrated solar radiation
  • Drive materials innovation for heat engine components (Stirling engines) requiring expertise in high-temperature alloys, tribology, and fatigue resistance

  • Strategic Materials Engineering:

  • Drive intellectual property development through patents and publications in high-impact journals
  • Technical Leadership:

Required Experience

  • Minimum 5 years of deep research experience in materials engineering, with preference for renewable energy, aerospace, concentrated solar power, or advanced energy storage industries
  • Proven track record of breakthrough research evidenced by high-impact publications, patents, and successful technology transitions from lab to commercial applications
  • Technical Expertise:
  • Extensive hands-on experience with advanced materials including high-temperature ceramics, refractory alloys, optical materials, thermal barrier coatings, and phase change materials
  • Deep understanding of materials thermodynamics, kinetics, and processing methods (powder metallurgy, additive manufacturing, thin film deposition, crystal growth)

Opportunities for professional growth and development in a rapidly evolving industry.

title: Burn Table Operator
description:
Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Burn Table and Plate/Pipe/Angle Roll Operator to join our team in Creola, AL. This is a hands-on, high-volume production role supporting heavy fabrication projects.

This position requires a seasoned professional with proven experience who can walk in and operate machinery independently on day one. You must also be willing to assist with other shop tasks as needed to keep production moving.

The ideal candidate is safety-focused, mechanically skilled, and fully capable of independently burning plate and rolling plate, pipe, and angle profiles strictly to engineering prints.

What You Will Do

  • Burn Table Operation: Power up CNC burn tables from startup, load existing cutting programs, verify nesting layouts, and begin cutting without assistance. Set torch heights, check consumables, confirm cut parameters, and perform basic troubleshooting.
  • Rolling Equipment Operation: Operate 4-roll plate rolling machines to roll thin to heavy plate steel up to 1-1/2” thick x 10’ wide. Shape components like shell plates for storage tanks, vessel cans, and manway necks.
  • Section Bending: Run 3-roll pipe rollers (1” up to 4’ diameter) and 3-roll angle rollers to bend angles from 1”x1” up to 5”x5” (both leg-in and leg-out).
  • Material Handling: Safely load and unload heavy raw plates and finished parts using forklifts and overhead cranes.
  • Quality Control: Verify finished parts against drawings, troubleshoot cut-quality issues, and mark, etch, and organize burned parts for the welding and fabrication teams.

What We Are Looking For

  • Experience: 5–10 years of professional plate cutting and rolling experience is highly preferred.
  • Materials: Prior experience handling and shaping carbon steel and/or stainless steel.
  • Autonomy: Must be capable of working independently with little to no supervision.
  • Testing: Because this is a senior role, candidates will be asked to complete a hands-on equipment operation test prior to receiving a formal job offer.

Why Apply?

  • Top-Tier Earning Potential: We reward elite skills with a highly competitive compensation structure.
  • Complete Work Autonomy: We don’t micromanage. If you can walk in, read the blueprints, check your nests, and execute clean cuts and rolls independently, we step back and let you run your station.
  • Build Massive, Crucial Equipment: Your daily work directly impacts heavy-duty industrial builds, shaping components for large storage tanks, pressure vessels, and structural components.
  • Stable, Long-Term Growth: Move past unstable short-term gigs. This is a secure, full-time production role within a highly collaborative, safety-first shop culture.

title: U.S. Army Transition Course - Alternate Instructor
description:
Are you looking for a Challenge? Looking for an innovative organization and the opportunity to learn and grow professionally? We can help! We are seeking an Alternate Instructor to support Army University’s Army Strategic Education Program – Transition Course (ASEP-T), an executive career-transition program for retiring and separating U.S. Army General Officers and their spouses. This is a Key Personnel position. Courses are delivered in person in the National Capital Region (historically the AUSA Conference and Events Center in Arlington, VA) and online, with five (5) five-day courses per year, one (1) Introductory Transition Module, and up to eight (8) Four-Star Executive Sessions annually.

I’ve never heard of Terrestris. What do you do?

At Terrestris, we leverage technology to create better mission outcomes through better human performance. We form strong client and team relationships through transparency and strive to create an environment where our team can let their excellence shine through. By finding, developing, and incorporating new ideas, we provide memorable services. Rooted in the USMC values of honor, courage, and commitment, Terrestris seeks to deliver extraordinary value to the American people by helping the Government become more efficient and effective.

So, what will the Alternate Instructor at Terrestris do?

The Alternate Instructor partners with the Primary Instructor to teach, present, or facilitate the majority of ASEP-T, a five-day executive education course that prepares transitioning General Officers and their spouses to move from senior military leadership into the civilian workforce in accordance with the Veterans Opportunity to Work (VOW) Act, Transition Assistance Program (TAP), and Soldier for Life requirements. The Alternate Instructor steps in as lead whenever the Primary Instructor is unavailable, ensuring at least one qualified instructor is present for the entire course.

Using executive adult learning models and challenging experiential exercises, the Alternate Instructor helps General Officers translate their military experience into civilian executive terms, build transition plans, resumes, and networking strategies, and prepare for interviews and offer negotiations. The Alternate Instructor also provides individual counseling, supports the spouse curriculum, and contributes to continuous course improvement in coordination with the ASEP-T Course Director.

What does a typical day look like for an Alternate Instructor?

You will:

  • Co-instruct five (5) five-day ASEP-T courses per year (approximately eight hours per day) for up to 18 General Officers in person or 22 online, plus their spouses.
  • Serve as lead instructor when the Primary Instructor is unavailable, ensuring continuity of instruction throughout every course.
  • Help develop and maintain a current, modular curriculum adaptable to face-to-face and online delivery (e.g., Zoom, Teams) that meets VOW Act, TAP, Soldier for Life, and Department of Labor requirements.
  • Guide participants in building individual transition plans, including pre-separation timelines, realistic career goals, interest/aptitude assessments, and translation of military experience into civilian terms.
  • Instruct on resumes/CVs and cover letters, networking plans, LinkedIn and social media, job search methods, personal branding, interviewing, civilian salary scales and negotiation, and post-interview actions.
  • Facilitate experiential exercises, including internet- and AI-enabled exercises, resume building, mock interviews, and mock offer negotiations.
  • Conduct individual counseling sessions with participants (and spouses, as applicable), including in-depth resume critiques, transition plan feedback, strengths assessments, and networking plan and LinkedIn reviews.
  • Support delivery of the integrated spouse curriculum and spouse-specific break-out sessions.
  • Support the Day 2 no-host networking event with recently retired General Officers.
  • Support the annual one-day Introductory Transition Module (ITM) for up to 200 students and customized Four-Star Executive Sessions, as assigned.
  • Provide follow-on coaching (up to two hours per participant for up to 90 days after retirement) on resumes, job search, interviewing, and salary negotiation.
  • Help administer pre-course surveys and course evaluations, participate in after action reviews, and contribute to post-course, quarterly, and annual reports.

What qualifications do you look for?

You might be the professional we’re looking for if you have:

  • Authorization to permanently work in the United States without sponsorship.
  • Ability to pass background checks (NCIC-III and Terrorist Screening Database) for Army installation and facility access. No security clearance is required.
  • A master’s degree in business, management, counseling, or a related field; or experience plus recognized industry credentials or certifications in human resources management, career counseling, or career services.
  • Military veteran who transitioned within the last ten (10) years at the rank of O-4 or above, or as an E-9 (SGM/CSM).
  • Three (3) or more years of experience leading talent management, recruiting, or counseling General Officers or senior military executives.
  • Three (3) or more years of experience with executive-level curriculum development and delivery, training or educating an executive-level audience.
  • Three (3) or more years of experience working with or for Army Generals, senior military officers, and/or senior civilian executives.

title: Industrial Automation and CSV Engineer - San Diego

title: Family Advocate

title: Senior Healthcare Interface Engineer (Remote Opportunity)
description:

The engineer will work on advanced interoperability initiatives involving data mapping, transformation, routing, troubleshooting, and production support.

The role operates in a highly collaborative environment, partnering with architects, FHIR engineers, application developers, testers, onboarding teams, and external partners to deliver secure, reliable, scalable, and standards-compliant healthcare integrations.

The candidate must reside within the continental US.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement healthcare integration solutions connecting applications, data sources, EHR systems, claims systems, public health systems, and external partners.
  • Engineer and configure MLLP gateways, Apache NiFi processing pipelines, Open Integration Engine adapters, and healthcare interfaces supporting complex data feeds.
  • Develop and support bidirectional Clinical Health Information Exchange and partner exchange integrations.
  • Evaluate existing systems, interfaces, data flows, and integration requirements to design reliable, secure, and scalable interoperability solutions.
  • Perform data mapping, transformation, routing, interface configuration, testing, troubleshooting, and production support while resolving complex interface and data-flow issues.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Healthcare Informatics, or a related field and 10+ years of related professional experience.
  • Extensive experience with healthcare interoperability, enterprise application integration, and healthcare interface development.
  • Strong experience with HL7 v2, MLLP, healthcare interface engines, data transformation, and message routing.
  • Experience with Apache NiFi, Open Integration Engine, EHR integration, and complex healthcare data flows.
  • Strong problem-solving and debugging skills with the ability to troubleshoot complex interface and data-flow issues.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work autonomously and provide technical leadership on complex integration initiatives.

Additional Qualifications

  • Experience with Java, scripting, XML, JSON, SQL, APIs, and enterprise integration technologies.
  • Experience integrating claims data, public health data, Clinical Health Information Exchange systems, and external healthcare partners.
  • Experience with FHIR-based integrations and collaborating with FHIR engineering teams.

Security Clearance Requirements

Benefits

title: Appeals Analyst
description:
Vālenz Health® is the destination for employers, brokers, payers, and providers to reduce costs, improve quality, and elevate the healthcare experience. Through advanced technology and clinical expertise, Valenz creates a distinctly different approach to a complex healthcare system. With our solutions, we execute across the entire healthcare journey — from member experience to payment integrity, provider quality, and plan performance. With one of America’s largest cost, quality and utilization datasets, we create greater transparency, flexibility, and cost containment — empowering members and employers with the information they need to make smarter, more cost-effective decisions.

About This Opportunity:
As an Appeals Analyst, you’ll review provider appeals by applying established procedures, service level agreements, plan documents, and network contract requirements to ensure accurate and timely claim determinations. You’ll calculate and negotiate settlement offers, prepare agreement documentation, issue denial determinations when appropriate, and coordinate approvals that exceed delegated authority while maintaining compliance with ERISA and applicable federal and state regulations. You’ll also maintain detailed records of appeal activity and outcomes, ensure claims are priced according to finalized terms, communicate statuses and resolutions with clients and providers, and utilize Zendesk, internal claims systems, Microsoft Outlook, and Microsoft Teams to support efficient case management and workflow.

Things You’ll Do Here:

  • Review appeals received from providers while adhering to established Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Service Level Agreements (SLAs), and maintaining timely communication with clients and providers.
  • Compare reimbursement findings against applicable plan documentation, network agreements, and contract requirements for in- and out-of-network appeals.
  • Calculate and propose initial settlement offers based on claim history, other pricing tools, and relevant data.
  • Complete agreement templates detailing negotiated terms and forward them to providers for review.
  • Support compliance with ERISA and applicable federal and state regulations.
  • Maintain detailed documentation of appeal research, negotiations, approvals, and outcomes.
  • Record and document finalized agreements for future reference and compliance.
  • Ensure claims are priced accurately, reflecting the terms stipulated in finalized agreements.
  • Communicate regularly with clients to provide updates on appeal statuses, outcomes, and other pertinent information.
  • Prepare and issue denial determinations based on appeal reviews, ensuring compliance with applicable policies and guidelines.
  • Coordinate with clients when approvals exceed delegated authority in accordance with established policies and standard processes.
  • Utilize Zendesk, internal claims systems, Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Teams, and other departmental software to manage appeals, documentation, and communication.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential duties.


What You’ll Bring to the Team:
  • 2+ years of healthcare claims, provider appeals, reimbursement, revenue cycle, or medical billing experience.
  • Knowledgeable in of CPT-4, HCPCS, Revenue Codes, DRG, and ICD-10 coding for accurate claims review, pricing, and payment validation.
  • Knowledge of the No Surprise Act, ERISA guidelines, and related legislation.
  • Highly detail-oriented with the ability to identify discrepancies and ensure accurate results
  • Proficient in analyzing out-of-network claim appeals, utilizing claim pricing tools and data to assess reimbursement accuracy and support appeal determinations.
  • Knowledgeable of Medicare reimbursement methodologies
  • Proficient in reviewing Explanation of Benefits (EOBs) to identify payment discrepancies and support claim appeal resolution.
  • Ability to interpret contracts and Plan documents to support accurate claim adjudication and appeal determinations.
  • Experienced in provider negotiations and evaluated counter offers to achieve timely and cost-effective claim settlements.
  • Experience with Microsoft Outlook, Teams, and Excel
  • Dependable and committed to maintaining a reliable work schedule while meeting productivity and performance expectations.

A plus if you have…
  • Associate or bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, or related field.
  • CPC Certification
  • Experience with international plans and self-funded insurance.
  • Knowledge of Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process, including applicable reimbursement guidelines and compliance requirements.



Where You’ll Work: This is a fully remote position, and we’ll provide all the necessary equipment!

  • Work Environment: You’ll need a quiet workspace that is free from distractions.
  • Technology: Reliable internet connection—if you can use streaming services, you’re good to go!
  • Security: Adherence to company security protocols, including the use of VPNs, secure passwords, and company-approved devices/software.
  • Location: You must be US based, in a location where you can work effectively and comply with company policies such as HIPAA.

Why You'll Love Working Here

Our mission is to advance healthcare through technology and expertise to optimize cost, quality, access, and utilization for all. We bring that mission to life through our commitment to Collaboration, Performance, Transparency, and Trust—the core values that guide how we work with our members, our customers, and each other.

Benefits

  • Generously subsidized company-sponsored Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance, with access to services through our own products, Healthcare Blue Book and KISx Card.
  • Spending account options: HSA, FSA, and DCFSA
  • 401K with company match and immediate vesting
  • Flexible working environment
  • Generous Paid Time Off to include vacation, sick leave, and paid holidays
  • Employee Assistance Program that includes professional counseling, referrals, and additional services
  • Paid maternity and paternity leave
  • Pet insurance
  • Employee discounts on phone plans, car rentals and computers
  • Community giveback opportunities, including paid time off for philanthropic endeavors

title: Project Estimator - Construction

The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills, a solid understanding of construction methods and industry standards, and experience using estimating software to prepare accurate project budgets. The Project Estimator must be able to manage multiple priorities, communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, and deliver high-quality estimates within established deadlines.

This position offers the opportunity to contribute to large-scale capital improvement and construction projects that support NYCHA’s mission of providing safe, quality housing throughout New York City.

title: Special Projects Social District
description:
"Your Community Needs You" -- "Begin Your Journey as a Block By Block CA Special Projects Ambassador Today!"

The starting pay for this position is $22.88 per hour.

So Why Block by Block CA

At Block by Block CA we employ friendly Ambassadors to make public spaces better, which includes making them friendlier, safer and cleaner. With nearly 800 employees across the state of California, Block by Block CA is large enough to provide lots of opportunities, but small enough to have your work noticed. Our Mission Statement is as follows: "With pride, we make public spaces friendly and vibrant for the communities we serve."

Our rapid growth provides endless opportunities for your long-term career, not just your next job. 68% of our management team started in another job within our company, with a vast majority starting out as an Ambassador.

All About Being a Special Projects Ambassador

Block by Block CA is looking for people who like working outdoors, staying active and feeling a sense of accomplishment, while improving some of your cities most important public spaces. If you love interacting with people in your current environment, but are looking for more variety in your assignments this might be the job for you!

Special Project Ambassadors are often like the local caretakers in the public spaces they serve because they:

  • Professionally represent not only us, but our customer, and they realize we're highly visible and operate in one of our cities' most important fish bowls.
  • Help the public see that the space we serve is well cared for, leading to more return visits and sharing positive experiences.
  • Take ownership of every person's experience in the public space, whether it's a visitor, resident, worker or member of the street population.

As a Special Projects Ambassador, no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will likely include the following responsibilities:

  • Circulate through assigned work zones in the work area completing manual and/or mechanical cleaning of needed items or spaces.
  • Operate large hot water power unit to clean sidewalks or plazas, street furniture, or any other areas in need of deep cleaning.
  • Operation of large litter vacuums to sweep up litter, debris or leaves.
  • Staying Visible, and Be Really Friendly: Our job is to not only clean, but to be a visible presence and have friendly interactions with the people in the public space we serve
  • Ongoing Reporting: Be comfortable using our simple smart phone app to report normal activities and maintenance reports

We might be a great match if:

  • If you have a driver's license (Yes! This is required)
  • You're handy with basic tools and understand how things work
  • You like being active! (who doesn't like paid exercise!) Candidates must have the physical capacity to stand and move continuously during an eight-hour shift, with normal breaks (two fifteen-minute breaks and one thirty-minute meal break)
  • You like working outdoors! (we provide inclement weather gear) All of our work is performed outside.
  • You love going home every day with the sense of accomplishment that you made your city or someone else's day better.
  • You are looking for a fantastic, second career opportunity (a.k.a. We love retirees!)

Maybe not so much if...

  • You are looking for only a Monday through Friday job. We are busy all day (especially on the weekends)
  • You only like working indoors
  • You want to be sitting most of your day.
  • You don't like people.
  • You're not 18.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you're proactive, community driven individuals and like working in a team environment, apply today for this fantastic role to help become part of our thriving public space team!

We are proud to offer the following benefits:

  • Insurance: Medical with available FSA and/or HSA, Dental, Vision, Short-Term and Long-Term Disability, Life, and Accidental Death and Dismemberment, Critical Illness, and Accident.
  • Paid time off: Vacation, Sick Time and/or PTO (Only where required by local requirements and contract agreements), Paid Leave (only where required by law), Holidays (only where required by contract agreement), Floating Holidays (only where required by contract agreement), Birthday Pay (eligible after one year of service at most locations unless otherwise stated in CBA), Jury Duty (only where required by law).

The Enterprise Architect joins the Americas Markets & Industries (AMI) Office of the CTO to work directly with Microsoft's most strategic customers in Canada. As part of the AMI Office of the CTO, you will help connect customer needs, industry trends, and real-world implementation experience back into Microsoft. You'll set direction on architecture that others build against, take on the problems where the right approach isn't yet obvious, and raise the engineering bar through design review, mentorship, and the standards you establish. This is a hands-on role: you'll still write and review code, but your leverage comes from decisions that shape systems well beyond what you personally build.

  • Design and build distributed services that handle high request volumes and sensitive financial data with strong reliability, latency, and correctness guarantees
  • Identify the highest-leverage technical problems facing the team and drive them to resolution, including work that spans organizational boundaries
  • Partner closely with product, data science, analytics, and risk to translate ambiguous business goals into durable technical plans
  • Raise engineering quality across the org through design reviews, code reviews, testing strategy, observability, and incident response practices
  • Mentor and grow engineers, helping senior engineers take on larger scope and develop their own technical judgment
  • Make deliberate tradeoffs between speed and long-term maintainability, and communicate the reasoning clearly to both engineering and non-engineering stakeholders

  • Contribute to the team's technical roadmap and influence platform and tooling decisions that affect adjacent teams

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant time at a senior or staff level

title: Rhombus Research: Software Engineering Intern
description:
About Rhombus Research:
Rhombus Research is an independent research lab in San Antonio. We build systems that make the behavior of autonomous machines visible and verifiable: coordination and accountability infrastructure for autonomous fleets, spanning swarm robotics, systems security, and data visualization. We treat engineering and design as one discipline. Our work has been presented at IEEE ICRA and will be presented at ITS Texas.

Position Overview:
We are building a public API for Reptile, our browser-based simulation engine for autonomous fleet coordination, so outside researchers can author their own scenarios and run experiments against it. The intern will help design, implement, and test that interface: endpoints and data contracts, a test suite, reference examples, and developer documentation, including validating the API through Reptile's built-in AI scenario builder. You would work directly with the founder on production code from the first week. React and TypeScript required. Remote, with occasional in-person collaboration in San Antonio.

Rhombus Research

Summer 2027 Software Engineering Intern: Simulation API

About us

Rhombus Research is an independent research lab in San Antonio working on coordination and accountability systems for autonomous infrastructure. Our work spans swarm robotics, systems security, and data visualization. Recent work has been previously presented at IEEE ICRA and upcoming at ITS Texas.

We are small enough that you would work directly with the founder on production code from your first week.

The role

We are building a public API for Reptile, our browser-based simulation engine for autonomous fleet coordination. Today Reptile runs scenarios we author ourselves. The goal is an interface that lets outside researchers define their own scenarios, bring their own devices and data, and run experiments against the engine.

You would help design, implement, and test that interface.

Specific work includes

  • Design an API interface alongside Rhombus Research

  • Implementing API endpoints and data contracts

  • Writing the test suite: unit tests, integration tests, and validation against malformed input

  • Building reference examples that demonstrate how an outside user would use the API

  • Writing developer documentation, including a getting-started guide and API reference

  • Identifying gaps and inconsistencies in the design

This is a platform engineering role centered on API design, shared services, and building reliable developer tooling.

What you would get

  • A portfolio project: A shipped, documented public API with your name in the commit history.

  • Founder mentorship: Direct collaboration with the founder, including structured weekly one-on-ones and daily communication as needed.

  • Hands-on domain experience: Practical work across simulation engineering, API design, and developer tooling.

  • Compensation: Funded through the Students + Startups program. A $6,000 stipend for the 10-week summer term, with housing support and onboarding handled by the program.

What we are looking for

Required

  • Proficiency in React and TypeScript

  • Comfort with Git and collaborative development

  • Ability to read an existing codebase and work within its conventions

  • Clear written communication, since documentation is part of the job

Helpful but not required

  • Three.js or react-three-fiber

  • Experience working with LLM APIs

  • Experience writing tests, any framework

  • Interest in autonomous vehicles, swarm systems, or infrastructure

Logistics

10 weeks, 40 hours per week.

Remote. Occasional in-person collaboration in San Antonio.

We prioritize core engineering fundamentals over specific toolsets or domain experience. If you are a strong programmer, we encourage you to apply.

title: Tullverket söker teamledare till vår framtida tullhantering
description:
Jobbar du inom IT och söker nya utmaningar? Då är det hos oss du vill vara!

Tullverkets IT-avdelning är norra Sveriges största arbetsgivare inom IT. Hos oss får du arbeta med samhällsviktiga uppdrag där du bidrar till att effektivisera Sveriges varuflöde. Vi bygger långsiktiga agila team som bidrar till både verksamhet och samhällsnytta. Nu söker vi efter teamledare, ta chansen och bli en del av gemenskapen.

Din roll

Som ledare för våra agila team jobbar du i mångt och mycket som en scrum master och är teamets servant leader. Du agerar spindel i nätet mot bland annat andra team och intressenter samt leder teamet i det fortlöpande förbättringsarbetet. Att jobba nära leveransområdet blir en viktig komponent för att teamet och leveransområdet tillsammans ska uppnå rätt verksamhetseffekter.

På Tullverket vill vi att teamen jobbar självorganiserande och åtar sig sina uppgifter tillsammans. Våra team äger själva sitt arbetssätt och man vågar prova saker för att sedan lyckas eller misslyckas tillsammans. Att våga prova är viktigt för oss på Tullverket och vi ser det som en nyckel till att utvecklas.

Du kommer att ingå i ett nätverk av personer med liknande arbetsuppgifter som utvecklar våra team och deras arbetsmetoder. Du är med och påverkar vår resa samt samarbetar med andra team, leveransområden och våra agila coacher. Idag har vi ett stort antal team och vill möjliggöra en kreativ frihet och samtidigt lära av varandra.

Du kommer kontinuerligt att ges förutsättningar att utveckla din ledarförmåga. Hos oss har du möjlighet att fördjupa dina kunskaper i en coachande och stöttande miljö.

Vi erbjuder dig

  • Friskvårdsbidrag och en friskvårdstimme varje vecka för att främja hälsa och välmående. Tullverket har även en aktiv idrottsförening i Luleå som kontinuerligt arrangerar hälsofrämjande aktiviteter
  • Goda semester- och pensionsvillkor

En vänlig arbetsplats där vi värderar trivsel och kultur högt. Hos oss får du fördjupa dina kunskaper i en coachande och stöttande miljö

Är du den vi söker?

Vi söker dig som har:

  • Du har en akademisk utbildning inom IT alternativt erfarenhet vi bedömer likvärdig
  • Du har aktuell yrkeserfarenhet inom IT i roller som t.ex. systemutvecklare, kravanalytiker eller lösningsarkitekt

Det är meriterande om du har:

title: Controller, Station Operations Control and Recovery
description:
Summary

The Controller, Station Operations Control and Recovery executes real-time SOCR operations at the desk, serving as the primary point of contact for station coordination, irregular operations management, and customer recovery execution during day-of operations. The Controller works the full lifecycle of irregular operations—from assessment through resolution—while maintaining accurate records, executing recovery standards, and communicating timely and accurate information to stations, vendors, and SOCR leadership.

This role operates under the direction of the SOCR Supervisor and is responsible for ensuring SOCR functions deliver safe, consistent, effective, and customer-conscious support across scheduled service, public and private charters, DOD charters, and company repositioning flights. The Controller is expected to apply sound judgment, maintain desk discipline, and escalate to the Supervisor in accordance with SOCR escalation standards.

Visa Sponsorship Available

No

Minimum Requirements

Combination of Education and Experience will be considered. Must be authorized to work in the US as defined by the Immigration Act of 1986. Must pass a Criminal Background Check.

Education:
High School Diploma/GED

Education Details:
N/A

Certification:
No

Certification Details:
N/A

Years of Experience:
Minimum one (1) year of airline industry experience in an operational setting.

Credit Check:
No

Valid/Unexpired Passport Book:
No

Valid/Unexpired Driver's License:
No

  • Ability and willingness to work varied shifts, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, and the ability to stay late for delayed flights or irregular operations in a 24/7 environment.

  • Ability to attend and successfully complete required training.

  • Ability to read, write, and speak English in order to receive and understand instructions and directives, ensure safety, and interact with customers.

  • High level of proficiency in Microsoft Office.

  • Ability to work in a fast-paced and potentially high-stress environment.

  • Extensive problem-solving capabilities when working with irregular flight operations.

  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, with a proven ability to develop customer correspondence at an executive level.

  • High level of organization, with multitasking ability and the ability to work through stressful situations.

  • Team-building skills with an orientation toward positive contributions.

Preferred Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred but not required.

  • Prior experience in an OCC, station operations, or airline operations control environment.

  • Familiarity with airline IROP processes, vendor coordination, and customer recovery procedures.

  • Knowledge of FAA, DOT, and TSA regulations applicable to ground and station operations.

Job Duties

  • Executes real-time station coordination at the desk during the operational window, maintaining situational awareness, managing workload priorities, and applying SOCR procedures and standards in accordance with Supervisor direction.

  • Works all phases of irregular operations—assessment, coordination, facilitation, and documentation—for scheduled service, public and private charters, DOD charters, and company repositioning flights.

  • Serves as the primary point of contact for stations during IROPs, delays, cancellations, diversions, and turn recovery, ensuring timely and accurate information flow between stations, vendors, and SOCR leadership.

  • Executes customer recovery actions, including compensation issuance, service recovery coordination, and station handling, in accordance with established SOCR recovery standards and Supervisor direction.

  • Coordinates all service recovery elements with outside vendors, including ad hoc charters, hotels, transportation companies, and food and beverage outlets.

  • Executes, approves, and maintains alternate procedures for ground network operations, including deicing and fuel, ensuring compliance with applicable regulatory and company requirements.

  • Establishes and maintains proactive communications via email and phone with stations, operational departments, regulatory agencies, and charter-related entities throughout the operational window.

  • Completes operational records, communication logs, trackers, recovery documentation, and shift handoff notes accurately and in a timely manner to support operational continuity, post-event review, and audit readiness.

  • Executes escalation discipline per the SOCR escalation chain, routing unresolved station issues, compliance concerns, and developing situations to the SOCR Supervisor in accordance with established thresholds.

  • Acts as the first point of contact for ground emergency procedures, initiating appropriate notifications and escalations in accordance with SOCR and company protocols.

  • Serves as the initial point of contact and information liaison for Threat, Reasonable Suspicion, and Post-Accident scenarios; initiates and executes the applicable departmental checklist for each event type and escalates notifications to the SOCR Supervisor and appropriate operational and compliance partners in accordance with established protocols.

  • Coordinates Positive Contact between Crew Services, stations, and crew members per Flight Operations and Inflight contractual requirements.

  • Coordinates, facilitates, and distributes international requirements for international aircraft movements for induction and/or heavy maintenance repositions.

  • Validates and reconciles expenses related to coordinated events, supporting SOCR cost control and recovery spend accountability.

  • Provides on-the-spot guidance and process reinforcement to station agents during active events, advising on policy, procedures, and recovery actions.

  • Communicates developing situations, station constraints, and customer impact proactively and timely to the SOCR Supervisor and other designated leadership.

  • Supports compliance with all applicable FAA, DOT, and TSA directives, security requirements, and company policies and procedures.

  • Liaises with IT to ensure Allegiant system bugs and issues affecting SOCR desk functions are communicated and tracked.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Physical Requirements

The Physical Demands and Work Environment described here are a representative of those that must be met by a Team Member to successfully perform the essential functions of the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role.

Office - While performing the duties of this job, the Team Member is regularly required to stand, sit, talk, hear, see, reach, stoop, kneel, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer, key board, printer, and phone. May be required to lift, push, pull, or carry up to 20 lbs. May be required to work various shifts/days in a 24-hour situation. Regular attendance is a requirement of the role. Exposure to moderate noise (i.e. business office with computers, phones, printers, and foot traffic), temperature and light fluctuations. Ability to work in a confined area as well as the ability to sit at a computer terminal for an extended period of time. Some travel may be a requirement of the role.

Essential Services Provider

Essential Services Provider

Allegiant as a national air carrier is deemed an essential service provider during declared national and state emergencies. Team Members will be required to report to their assigned trip or work location during national and state emergencies unless prohibited by local, state or federal order.

We welcome all individuals from varied backgrounds and experiences to apply. Our company values the unique perspectives and talents that each person brings to our team.

title: Reagent Manufacturing Technician
description:
About Countable Labs

At Countable Labs, we’re reimagining the future of genomics and we’d love for you to be a part of it! As the innovators behind our groundbreaking Countable PCR platform, we’re building tools that make a real impact in precision medicine. We’re a startup fueled by innovation, collaboration, and a mission-driven spirit. If you’re ready to roll up your sleeves, build something from the ground up, and help shape the future of genomics, we want you on our team! Countable Labs is an Equal Opportunity Employer

Role Summary

The Reagent Manufacturing Technician leads the daily production of reagents and ensures that all manufactured reagents and kits meet the requirement per the procedures.

You will formulate, test, and package chemical and biological reagents used in diagnostics and research. Responsibilities include precise liquid handling, operating automated filling and labeling equipment, following ISO/GMP regulations, and accurately maintaining batch records and Device History Records (DHRs)

Key Responsibilities

  • Formulation & Processing: Accurately measure, weigh, mix, and filter chemical and biological solutions based on precise standard operating procedures (SOPs).
  • Filling & Packaging: Aliquot bulk reagents into final container bottles, operate automated/semi-automated fill lines, and assemble multi-reagent kits.
  • Quality Control & Assurance: Perform visual inspections, incoming material QC, gather samples for testing, conduct pH/concentration checks, and support root-cause investigations into production deviations.
  • Documentation & Compliance: Complete and review batch records and DHRs, ensuring 100% compliance with cGMP, GDP, and ISO standards.
  • Inventory & Maintenance: Track raw materials in ERP systems, manage reagent cold-chain storage, and maintain a sterile, organized laboratory workspace.


Additional Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in reagent manufacturing, reagent preparation, or inventory management; experience in PCR and/or NGS reagent manufacturing highly preferred
  • Familiarity with working with flow hood and fume hood environments, as well as common equipment in a typical molecular biology lab
  • Skillful with pipetting and mixing reagents, including enzymes, oligos, and buffer solutions
  • Strong teamwork skills and ability to work collaboratively in a supportive, production-focused lab setting.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities and perform additional duties as assigned.
  • Previous experience and understanding of OSHA hazard communication requirements such as biosafety protocols.
  • Familiarity with PCR and DNA quantitation techniques is highly preferred.
  • Ability to support as a back-up to shipping, receiving and inventory control.

Required Qualifications

  • Education: B.S. degree in a STEM discipline (Biology, Chemistry, Biotech) is preferred, though relevant hands-on experience and completed STEM coursework are often accepted.
  • Experience: 1 to 3+ years working in a GMP/ISO-regulated manufacturing environment in life science tools, diagnostic, medical device, or pharmaceutical manufacturing environment. Experience with manufacturing of PCR, NGS, and other molecular biology reagent products highly preferred.
  • Skills: Aseptic techniques, high dexterity for repetitive pipetting, proficiency with metric/imperial volume measurements, prolonged standing, color differentiation (relevant given reagent manufacturing such as pH/concentration visual checks) and the physical ability to lift up to 25–50 lbs.
  • Superb attention to details; ability and desire to work in a fast-paced environment, and priorities can change on a regular basis

Work Environment

This role is based in a laboratory setting within a manufacturing and packaging department. The standard production hours are flexible and only part-time. The desire is for someone to be here between Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., weekends are not currently required. This role is an onsite work that includes time under flowhoods and fume hood areas while filling liquid products, as well as operating printers, labelers, electronic or mechanical filling equipment, and other common molecular biology lab equipment. The position requires wearing appropriate personal protective equipment, including latex gloves and safety glasses. The company offers a supportive and collaborative culture that encourages employees to focus on their professional strengths while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. This is a contract role created to address an extensive backlog, with a history of extensions beyond the initial term based on business needs and performance.


Job Type & Location

This is a Contract position based out of Headquarters in Palo Alto, CA.
